articleTitle: Graph Neural Network-Based Entity Extraction and Relationship Reasoning in Complex Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study proposed a knowledge graph entity extraction and relationship reasoning algorithm based on a graph neural network, using a graph convolutional network and graph attention network to model the complex structure in the knowledge graph. By building an end-to-end joint model, this paper achieves efficient recognition and reasoning of entities and relationships. In the experiment, this paper compared the model with a variety of deep learning algorithms and verified its superiority through indicators such as AUC, recall rate, precision rate, and F1 value. The experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper performs well in all indicators, especially in complex knowledge graphs, it has stronger generalization ability and stability. This provides strong support for further research on knowledge graphs and also demonstrates the application potential of graph neural networks in entity extraction and relationship reasoning.

articleTitle: Urban Trash Detection and Cleanliness Assessment Based on YOLOv7 for Autonomous Sweeper
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Urbanization accelerates, increasing municipal waste volumes. Automatic sweepers are crucial for urban cleanliness, but assessing ground cleanliness remains challenging, hindering efficient operations. We developed a ground cleanliness evaluation method based on urban waste recognition and detection. To mitigate the high false-negative rates and feature integration difficulties associated with diverse waste, we enhanced the YOLOv7 backbone with Res2Blocks for improved fine-grained feature fusion and detection accuracy. A quantifiable cleanliness index was formulated considering waste quantity, distribution, and area. A dataset of 10,543 images of typical urban park litter was compiled to train the model, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of ≥0.926 at an Intersection over the Union (IoU) threshold of 0.5. This resulted in effective pre- and post-cleaning assessments, providing performance feedback and strategic guidance for future cleaning activities.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning in Deep Networks: A Pathway to Robust Few-Shot Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study aims to optimize the few-shot image classification task and improve the model's feature extraction and classification performance by combining self-supervised learning with the deep network model ResNet-101. During the training process, we first pre-train the model with self-supervision to enable it to learn common feature expressions on a large amount of unlabeled data; then fine-tune it on the few-shot dataset Mini-ImageNet to improve the model's accuracy and generalization ability under limited data. The experimental results show that compared with traditional convolutional neural networks, ResNet-50, DenseNet, and other models, our method has achieved excellent performance of about 95.12% in classification accuracy (ACC) and F1 score, verifying the effectiveness of self-supervised learning in few-shot classification. This method provides an efficient and reliable solution for the field of few-shot image classification.

articleTitle: Attention-Based Temporal Convolutional Networks and Reinforcement Learning for Supply Chain Delay Prediction and Inventory Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Accurately predicting supply chain delays is crucial for maintaining resilience in inventory management systems. This paper presents a novel framework integrating an Attention-Based Temporal Convolutional Network (ATCN) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to address the challenges of supply chain delay prediction and inventory optimization. The ATCN model leverages convolutional layers to capture long-term dependencies in time series data, while the attention mechanism enhances prediction accuracy under high demand volatility. Additionally, the RL component optimizes inventory decisions by minimizing holding and shortage costs through multi-agent collaboration. Our proposed approach outperforms baseline models in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics. Ablation studies confirm the importance of both the attention mechanism and RL in improving forecasting accuracy and inventory management. This work offers a robust solution for enhancing supply chain resilience and lays the groundwork for future exploration in multi-layered and real-time supply chain systems.

articleTitle: Online Group-Based Face Recognition and Tracking Algorithm Using Kalman Filtering in Team Learning Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Since the 21st century, with the advancement of the times, the educational model has changed, and a new teaching model, the team learning model, has emerged. However, traditional methods of educational assessment are inadequate to meet the new demands. Obtaining personalized characteristics of learners in the classroom is essential for achieving precision, objectivity, personalization, and intelligent education. To efficiently collect students' facial images, this paper proposes an online group face recognition and tracking algorithm based on Kalman filtering. The algorithm considers the continuity of facial targets in time and the correlation in space, addressing the impact of partial facial poses, occlusions, and expressions on face detection and recognition. Moreover, by utilizing the predictive function of the Kalman filter, the algorithm reduces the number of face feature comparisons, improving the timeliness and accuracy of face recognition. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Graph-Channel Attention U-Net for Undersampled MRI Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Due to the lengthy acquisition time required for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), researchers have proposed various methods to shorten this time. However, these methods often overlook the non-local similarity within the images, resulting in the inability to reconstruct images with clear structures. To address this issue, we present a Graph Channel Attention U-Net (GCA-Unet).The input to GCA-Unet consists of three images with different resolutions. Each encoder is specifically trained on input images of varying scales, as well as feature information from the downsampled preceding decoder. The architecture employs a Multi-Head Graph Attention Module (MGAM) to capture non-local features within the images. In the final layer of the decoder, we output the reconstructed image. Given that the input comprises images of different scales, we also introduce a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Module (MFFM) to effectively integrate features across multiple scales. Extensive experiments conducted on brain and knee datasets demonstrate that our proposed GCA-Unet significantly outperforms other MRI reconstruction methods across various sampling rates. These results validate the effectiveness of GCA-Unet in reconstructing images with clear structures.

articleTitle: Application of Group-Aware Hierarchical Transformation Based on Grouping in Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Currently, deep learning algorithms shine in the field of hyperspectral image (HSI) classification and processing of hyperspectral images. Still, due to the limitations of the input size sensing field of deep learning algorithms, it is generally necessary to cut the input of HSI into fixed-size image chunks first, and then carry out the classification operation. This approach is limited by the size characteristics of HSI. In recent years, the visual transformer (ViT), as a deep learning algorithm that can be applied to multi-tasks, has not surprisingly been introduced to the HSI classification task, which is capable of selecting appropriate patch scales for different input maps through a flexible input feature selection mechanism. Nevertheless, when ViT deals with HSI with many bands, the features extracted by its global self-attention mechanism may exhibit a tendency of over-dispersion, which affects the classification performance. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a ViT-based packet-aware hierarchical converter (PSHC) architecture that aims to optimize the classification of HSI. The architecture strengthens the local relationships within all spectral channels by embedding a pixel group mapping (PGM) module, which applies a global self-attention mechanism to the algorithm for extracting global spatial-spectral features and achieves better characterization by fusing global and local features. In addition, PSHC adopts a hierarchical structural design, which firstly effectively extracts and fuses multiscale features without enlarging the number of model parameters, significantly improving the classification accuracy. Experimental validation on two benchmark HSI datasets shows that the proposed PSHC method outperforms previous deep learning algorithms in HSI classification tasks, especially in city-like map applications.

articleTitle: SODDA-YOLO: A Traffic Sign Target Detection Network in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the field of autonomous driving, the recognition of traffic signs is a very important safety issue. However, traffic sign detection is easily affected by the environment. Complex climate changes and surrounding lighting changes will affect the accuracy of traffic sign detection. Therefore, we propose a traffic sign target detection network SODDA-YOLO (Small Object Detection with Deformable Attention YOLO) based on YOLOv8. In this network, we first propose a downsampling module combined with a self-attention mechanism, which enhances the model's ability to correlate global information by adding a self-attention mechanism to the c2f module. Secondly, when the model performs sampling operations, we use the HWD module to replace the original single convolutional module. When performing sampling operations on the feature map, Haar wavelet sampling is added to replace the direct use of the convolutional module to retain more detailed information of the feature map. Experiments show that the mAP of SODDA-YOLO on the dataset TT100K reaches 68.9%, which is 1.6% higher than that of the original YOLOv8.

articleTitle: DGNet: Effective Image Rain Removal through Comprehensive Detection and Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Rain in real-world scenes is influenced by a multitude of environmental factors, presenting considerable challenges for single image deraining (SID) techniques. Current methodologies predominantly depend on intricate feature extraction modules to enhance visual quality, albeit on a limited subset of synthetic data. Nevertheless, due to the pronounced discrepancy between synthetic and real-world data, the efficacy of these methods in practical applications is diminished. To mitigate these limitations, we introduce a novel rain detection and generation network. In particular, we refocus the learning objective on rain mask identification, for which we develop a dedicated rain detection module. Subsequently, a pixel-wise filtering module is employed to utilize the derived mask information, thereby refining the image restoration process. Furthermore, we introduce a Rain Generation Module designed to bridge the gap between synthetic and real data during network training. The experimental results, derived from both synthetic and real-world datasets, substantiate the superior performance of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: SegUMamba: Integrating Mamba with U_net for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In medical image segmentation, capturing long-range dependencies is critical for precise segmentation. Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs)excel at local features, while Transformers comprehend global context, but both struggle with long-range dependencies. Mamba addresses this with its selection mechanism and dynamic matrix. By integrating Mamba with U-Net, we developed the SegUMamba model, which effectively captures local lesion details as well as distant interactions between lesions and surrounding skin. The encoder-decoder architecture, built on VMamba and utilizing skip connections, merges shallow and deep-level information, enhancing segmentation accuracy. We designed a flexible integration mechanism that enables feature exchange between the encoder and decoder while restoring features within the decoder, achieving efficient and lossless multiplexing. Experiments on the ISIC2018 Task1 dataset show that, with the same system configuration and hyperparameter settings, our model significantly outperforms others in accuracy, completeness and efficiency, making it promising for complex medical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network for Image Classification Research - Based on VGG16
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have increasingly become the predominant approach for image classification, demonstrating remarkable performance in this domain. Notably, VGG16 has gained widespread adoption due to its deep architecture and robust feature extraction capabilities. Consequently, this paper investigates the efficacy of employing the VGG16 convolutional neural network model for image classification on the CIFAR-10 dataset. The architecture of the VGG16 model and its distinctive application characteristics are first introduced, followed by an exploration of key steps including data preprocessing, model training, and hyperparameter tuning. 99.4% accuracy on the training set and 90.6% accuracy on the test set were attained after the training procedure was optimized. To improve the model's classification performance even more, this paper identifies limitations inherent in the current framework and proposes optimization strategies such as incorporating attention mechanisms and transfer learning. These strategies provide valuable insights for future applications of deep learning techniques on small-scale image datasets.

articleTitle: Improving YOLOv5 for Traffic Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the development of deep learning models, current traffic sign detection models often suffer from large size and numerous parameters. In order to balance the accuracy, size, and speed of models within limited hardware resources, a lightweight improvement of the YOLOv5 traffic sign detection model is proposed. This model restructures the YOLOv5 network using the GhostNet module, introducing smaller volume modules like C3Ghost and GhostConv. Additionally, it incorporates an ECA channel attention mechanism and replaces the loss function from CIOU to SIOU, enhancing the model's focus on detection targets and improving attention to small objects. Experimental validation on the CCTSDB2021 dataset demonstrates that compared to the YOLOv5 model, this improved model reduces parameter count by 45.5% and model size by 44.4%, emphasizing more accurate detection of real targets. This indicates that the model is more suitable for deployment on embedded platforms than the original model.

articleTitle: CIB-SE-YOLOv8: Optimized YOLOv8 for Real-Time Safety Equipment Detection on Construction Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Safety equipment is a crucial component in ensuring safety on construction sites, with helmets being particularly essential in reducing injuries and fatalities. Traditional methods, such as manual checks by superintendents and project managers, are inefficient and labor-intensive, often failing to prevent incidents related to the lack of safety gear. To address this, a new approach leveraging computer vision and deep learning has been developed, utilizing real-time detection techniques, specifically YOLO. This study utilizes the publicly available SHEL5K dataset for helmet detection tasks. The proposed CIB-SE-YOLOv8 model builds upon YOLOv8n by incorporating SE attention mechanisms and replacing certain C2f blocks with C2fCIB blocks. Compared to YOLOv8n, our model achieved a mAP50 of 88.4%, representing a 3.2% improvement. It also demonstrated a 0.5% increase in precision and a 3.9% increase in recall, significantly enhancing helmet detection performance. Additionally, the proposed model, with 2.68 million parameters and 7.6 GFLOPs, offers greater efficiency in real-time detection tasks compared to YOLOv8n’s 3 million parameters and 8.1 GFLOPs, making it a more effective solution for improving construction site safety.

articleTitle: Dual-Branch Brain Tumor Segmentation Algorithm by Fusing CNNs and Mambas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Due to the varying shapes and sizes, blurred boundaries, and unstable positions of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging, extracting both local and global features from the images is crucial for accurate segmentation of tumor regions. Existing deep learning methods have insufficient ability to model long-range dependencies in 3D medical images and face challenges in fusing global and local features. To effectively extract and utilize both global and local features, a dual-branch parallel brain tumor segmentation model combining CNNs and Mambas named MamFuse is proposed. MamFuse consists of two branches: one branch employs Mamba module, built on a selective state-space model (SSM), to model long-range dependencies, while the other branch utilizes the convolutional module to extract local information. Additionally, we introduced an innovative fusion module, GAFusion, to integrate multi-level features from both branches. Experimental results on the BraTS21 dataset show that the proposed network outperforms other state-of-the-art segmentation networks, achieving more accurate brain tumor segmentation.

articleTitle: Research on Lightweight Surface Defect Detection Network Model Based on Improved Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The deep learning-based surface defect detection method exhibits advanced detection capability. Aiming at the problems of large networks, high computing power and difficult deployment on edge devices, this paper presents a method for detecting surface defects using YOLOv8n. By substituting the original YOLOv8n backbone with lightweight FasterNet module, redundant information processing is reduced and model speed is improved. Use lightweight cross-scale feature fusion modules to enhance the fusion of low-level and high-level features, further reducing the amount of computation and parameters while maintaining accuracy. The multi-head self-attention mechanism has been incorporated to enhance the model's effectiveness. Test results indicate that, compared to YOLOv8n, the improved method achieves the same mean average precision (mAP) of 76.6% on the NEU-DET steel surface defect dataset. However, the number of model parameters and the computational load have been decreased by 69.9% and 44.8% respectively, with the model size now being only 28.6% of the original. These findings demonstrate that the improved model is more lightweight and better suited for use on hardware with constrained computing resources.

articleTitle: Printed Circuit Board Defect Detection Based on Feature Pyramid Spatial Prior Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In modern electronic devices, printed circuit boards play a crucial role as core components, and their quality is essential for device performance and reliability. Due to the complexity of PCB manufacturing processes, issues such as open circuits, short circuits, and solder defects often occur, affecting the overall quality of products. Traditional manual inspection methods are unable to meet high standards, leading to the gradual adoption of automated defect detection technology as the mainstream trend in the industry. This paper presents a network model for PCB defect detection, aimed at addressing the challenge of detecting small targets. We propose SmallObjectEnhancePyramid, which utilizes the P2 feature layer processed by SPDConv to obtain features rich in small object information and fuses them with P3. Then, we integrate features using CSP-OmniKernel to effectively learn feature representations from global to local. Additionally, we introduce RMTBlock to improve RepC3, reducing the computational burden of global information and model parameter quantity. This study not only improves the accuracy of PCB defect detection, but also helps optimize manufacturing processes and enhance production efficiency. Experimental results show that FPSPNet effectively improves the detection accuracy of printed circuit board defects, achieving an mAP0.5 value of 98.8%, precision of 99.3%, and recall of 97.3% on the dataset. It also outperforms existing models in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Image Classification Based on Multimodal Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the underutilization of label text information in few-shot image classification, this paper proposes a multimodal information fusion method that effectively improves classification accuracy. Traditional few-shot classification approaches primarily focus on image features, often neglecting the rich information contained in labeled text. To remedy this, we introduce the CLIP model to map images and text into a unified feature space, aligning visual and textual data at the same semantic level. Based on this alignment, we construct multimodal category prototypes that integrate image and text features, thereby enhancing intra-class similarity and inter-class differentiation. Additionally, we design a masking enhancement module to strengthen the model’s feature extraction capabilities under incomplete information by randomly masking parts of the image and performing a recovery task. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing approaches across multiple few-shot classification datasets, validating the effectiveness of fusing image and text information and offering new directions for few-shot classification research.

articleTitle: Inverse Asymptotic Fusion Framework for Fusion of Infrared and Visible Images of Fires
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In situations where smoke or other light sources obstruct the view of a fire scene, using visible light images for real-time detection and response can be challenging. In contrast, infrared images, which are more sensitive to heat sources, have been proven to be more effective. This sensitivity enables the detection and tracking of high-temperature areas at fire scenes, even in conditions of limited visibility. Combining infrared with visible light images provides a more comprehensive understanding of fire situations, aiding in the assessment of fire intensity and the prediction of fire spread. In this paper, we propose the IAFusion network, a fusion network for fire infrared and visible light images constructed using a progressive inverse feature pyramid. The network uses the IAFPN module to initially retain high semantic information and progressively fuses layers of multi-texture information upwards, ensuring that the fused image incorporates more detailed features on the basis of highlighting significant targets, thereby creating a binary mask focused on the subject. Subsequently, in the newly proposed fusion strategy, the fusion with infrared and visible light images is followed by selective feature reconstruction with the RFN module under the guidance of attention, serving as the input to the decoder, thus completing the image reconstruction. Quantitative and qualitative experiments have validated the advancement of our algorithm. Compared with nine competitive algorithms on the general dataset TNO, our network can generate images with clearer and more comprehensive information. In comparison with RFN-Nest on the Corsican fire dataset, our network can add more texture information while highlighting the main subject of flames in images.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement and Restoration Method Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the challenges of target detection and recognition in high-turbidity water environments, this paper proposes a neural network-based method for underwater image enhancement and restoration, aimed at improving the accuracy of target detection and recognition under such conditions. We introduce an underwater target image enhancement technique that utilizes multidimensional polarization decoupling and establish a neural network model for restoring polarization images of turbid water, which is based on fully dense connections and pyramid pooling. Experimental verification demonstrates that this method has increased the peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity to 20.08 dB and 0.852, respectively, significantly enhancing the accuracy of underwater target detection and recognition.

articleTitle: Lightweight Edge Detection Model with Parallel Pixel Difference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Although existing learning-based edge detection methods have made significant progress, they typically require large network parameters and substantial computational resources, which limits their practical applicability. Instead of focusing on larger deep models to improve detection performance, we propose a lightweight deep edge detection method that reduces computational costs while achieving comparable detection performance. This approach is built on a residual framework network architecture. Specifically, we introduce an efficient Parallel Pixel Difference Convolution Block (PPDB) as the core building block of our method to reduce model complexity. Additionally, to better leverage features from different scales, we incorporate a lightweight dynamic upsampling technique and develop a Refined Feature Fusion Block (RFFB) to achieve high-quality results. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our method requires about 200K fewer parameters and FLOPs compared to state-of-the-art methods such as LDC, while maintaining competitive performance.

articleTitle: Object Detection and Machine Vision Classification of Traffic Markers Based on YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper discusses the research of object detection of traffic signs based on YOLOv8 model, aiming to evaluate the application potential of this model in the field of machine vision. After the training and testing of the model, we selected 30 EPOchs to carry out experiments, and the results showed that the YOLOv8 model could effectively identify and classify most traffic signs, showing good target detection performance. During the training process, by analyzing the confusion matrix, we observed that the model showed high accuracy on different types of traffic signs. This result shows that YOLOv8 can not only quickly locate the target, but also achieve accurate classification in multiple types of traffic signs. With the deepening of training, the model gradually learns more complex features, thus improving its detection ability. By monitoring the loss and mAP of the training set and validation set, we found that the loss value gradually decreased from the initial 0.9 to about 0.4, and finally stabilized. This trend reflects that the model gradually converges during the learning process, indicating that the optimization effect is remarkable. At the same time, both in the training set and the verification set, the mAP value also showed a continuous rise and stabilized at about 0.9, which further verified the efficiency and reliability of the model in the target detection task. In addition, by calculating F1 scores, Precision, Recall, and plotting accuracy-recall curves, we were able to more fully evaluate the performance of the YOLOv8 model. The results show that the model has excellent performance in traffic sign target detection and classification tasks, and all indexes have reached a satisfactory level. These data support our conclusion that YOLOv8 has strong potential for practical applications. To sum up, this study demonstrates the excellent ability of YOLOv8 model in traffic sign detection, which not only proves its adaptability to target recognition and classification tasks in complex scenes, but also lays a foundation for the future application of this technology in intelligent transportation system, automatic driving and other fields. In the future, we look forward to further exploring the application of this technology in a wider range of fields to drive the development and innovation of machine vision."

articleTitle: Simplifying and Enhancing Graph Convolutional Networks for Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The efficacy of collaborative filtering in recommendation systems is undisputed, with the Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering (NGCF) model showing promise in capturing intricate user-item relationships. However, NGCF’s complex operations from Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), such as feature transformation and non-linear activation, raise efficiency concerns. The EfficientGCN model addresses these by streamlining NGCF, retaining only the essential neighborhood aggregation component. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets reveal that EfficientGCN significantly reduces computational overhead while improving recommendation accuracy, outperforming NGCF. This research highlights the importance of judicious model design, showing that simplicity and efficiency can lead to superior performance and future advancements in graph-based collaborative filtering.

articleTitle: Forward Design of 3D Modeling of Bridge Complex Surface Based on GIS+BIM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The conventional forward design method for 3D modeling of complex bridge surface reality mainly uses CODSM (Co-Oppsite-Orientation Slicing Method) point cloud slices to generate 3D contours, which is vulnerable to the impact of geometric parameter quantification, resulting in poor performance indicators. Therefore, a forward design method for 3D modeling of complex bridge surface reality based on GIS+BIM is proposed. That is, GIS+BIM is used to design the 3D modeling process of bridge complex surface reality, and generate the 3D modeling engine of bridge complex surface reality, thus completing the forward design of 3D modeling of bridge complex surface reality. The experimental results show that each index of the designed 3D modeling forward design method is good, reliable, and has certain application value, which has made certain contributions to the realization of fine management of bridge construction.

articleTitle: Design of a Solar-Powered Car Based on Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a smart solar-powered vehicle system based on gesture recognition, implementing real-time gesture recognition using the YOLOv5 algorithm on the K210 platform and controlling multiple motion modes through an STM32 main control module. The vehicle integrates omnidirectional movement with Mecanum wheels, ultrasonic obstacle avoidance, grayscale line following, and features a detachable solar module to enhance energy endurance. To improve recognition accuracy, the gesture dataset was balanced and annotated, and model optimization significantly increased recognition accuracy and real-time performance. Experiments demonstrate that the vehicle can quickly respond to user gestures and switch motion modes in various complex environments, achieving effective path and obstacle avoidance and line-following control, offering an innovative approach for low-power smart vehicles.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-LSD:A Steel Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Based On YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of insufficient detection accuracy and high model complexity of existing steel surface defect detection algorithms, an improved model YOLOv8-LSD is designed based on the YOLOv8 model, and theLSKBlock module is introduced into the Backbone to dynamically sense the defect environment information to improve the detection accuracy. At the same time, the SCConv module is added to the neck to reduce redundant features by combining the spatial reconstruction unit and the channel reconstruction unit, which increases the accuracy of the mo del and reduces the complexity of the model. In order to further improve the performance of the model, the DRB module was introduced into the C2f module, and the model performance was further improved by combining the non-dilated large-core convolutional layer and multiple expanded small-core convolutional layers. Finally, a large number of experiments are carried out on the NEU-DET dataset on the improved model, and the results show that the map of the improved model is increased by 1. 3% compared with the baseline model, reaching 78. 3%, and the number of parameters and computations are 2. 61M and 7. 3G, which are 9% and 8% less than the baseline, respectively.

articleTitle: Path Planning Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning in Unstructured Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In unstructured environments, the irregular distribution, complex shapes, and varied attributes of obstacles make it challenging to define effective reward objectives in deep reinforcement learning frameworks.Consequently, issues such as reward sparsity, reward deception, and convergence to local optima frequently arise. To address these challenges, this paper presents an enhancement strategy that combines external distance-based rewards with internal state-based incentives. Specifically, the integration of a distance-attenuated external reward strategy enables dynamic adjustment of distance rewards, thereby alleviating reward sparsity and minimizing reward spoofing, while optimizing path length through the attenuation of weight coefficients. However, as distance rewards attenuate, exploration may become insufficient, potentially leading to local optima. To counter this, a state-novelty-based internal reward strategy is introduced, encouraging exploration in areas with high obstacle density. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed enhanced reward strategy outperforms conventional approaches in unstructured environments, significantly reducing path length and the number of turns required in planned paths.

articleTitle: FWAVs Object Detection Based on YOLOv8 In Adverse Weather
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, Flapping-wing Micro Aerial Vehicles (FMAVs) have gained increasing attention due to their biomimetic appearance and excellent maneuverability. Equipping them with object detection systems to make them more intelligent is becoming a major trend. This paper proposes an aerial photography small object detection algorithm under adverse weather conditions based on YOLOv8. Using a custom dataset, the concluding mAP50 (mean Average Precision at Intersection over Union threshold of 0.5) reached 0.761, surpassing other datasets. The mAP50 improved from 0.627 to 0.708 compared to model validation on the VisDrone2019 dataset, surpassing other mainstream object detection models.

articleTitle: CLIP-based Text-to-image Pedestrian Retrieval Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text-to-image pedestrian retrieval involves querying a database of images based on a given textual description to find matching images. The main challenge lies in learning how to map visual and textual patterns to a common latent space. This paper improves upon the implicit learning inference framework based on the CLIP model, aiming to learn the relationship between images and text and enhance overall text-image matching. Through text matching learning, fine-grained detail representation learning is promoted. First, a masked language modeling paradigm is designed within the implicit relationship inference module. Then, cross-modal interaction is achieved through the modality alignment module using decomposable attention. Feed aligned image and text features into a multimodal synergy encoder to achieve cross modal interaction, and train the model using distribution consistency loss and ID loss. The improved method achieves better results on the RSTPReid public dataset, with the Rank-1 accuracy improving by approximately 3% compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Image Dehazing Algorithm By Atmospheric Light Fusion Based on The Prior of Dual-Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to solve the problems existing in the traditional DCP dehazing algorithm and improve the quality of the image after dehazing, this paper proposes a image dehazing algorithm by atmospheric light fusion based on the prior of Dual-Channel. Firstly, the corresponding atmospheric light and transmittance map are derived from the D channel and bright channel prior models, respectively. Then, the bright channel atmospheric light values obtained by different filtering sizes are fused by wavelet transform. Finally, the linear fusion function is applied to fit the dual-channel atmospheric light estimate, while the dehazed image is calculated using the atmospheric scattering model. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed algorithm is capable of efficiently removing the haze from the original image, and solve the problems of over-processing of the highlight part and low image brightness in the traditional DCP algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Human Gait Recognition Based on the Improved BECNN-BILSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study proposes a feature optimization strategy based on mutual information to identify the 10 most critical plantar pressure sensors for gait recognition. By reducing data redundancy, this approach enhances both the efficiency and generalization capability of the model. An advanced BECNN-BILSTM algorithm is developed to focus on key channel features, improving feature representation while suppressing irrelevant information. This design facilitates the accurate recognition of eight distinct lower-limb gait patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that the BECNN-BILSTM model significantly outperforms CNN, LSTM, and CNN-BILSTM models in recognition performance. This work offers a practical and efficient solution for real-time gait monitoring and fall prevention posture detection in wearable device applications.

articleTitle: Research on fMRI Image Registration Method Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) is a non-invasive, non-traumatic brain imaging technique with high tissue resolution and the ability to image in any plane. It represents a significant advancement in modern medical technology. In medical image processing, it is often necessary to compare different medical images to draw conclusion. However, due to individual differences and the impact of disease states, there are significant variations between fMRI data from different patients. To ensure data comparability, functional regions of fMRI images from different individuals need to be aligned before data analysis, which is call image registration. A deep learning network method for fMRI registration is proposed in this paper based on the U-net framework. In the network architecture, Transformer is integrated to enhance the model’s feature extraction capabilities. The method also utilizes block-based tissue-specific functional correlation.

articleTitle: Fusion of RGB and Near Infrared Image for Semantic Segmentation of Apple Defects Using Improved DeepLabv3+
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Accurate detection of apple defects, including the location, area, and type of defects, can help prevent the spread of defects and assist in fruit quality management. Therefore, we proposed a semantic segmentation network ADS-DeepLabv3+ for apple defects semantic segmentation. We introduce CBAM between the backbone network and ASPP to measure the channel and spatial weights of the feature maps output by the backbone network and introduce a feature fusion branch based on FPN in the backbone network, and finally construct ADS-DeepLabv3+ for semantic segmentation of apple defects. ADS-DeepLabv3+ got the 3.8% and 3.81% increase in MIoU and MPA than DeepLabv3+. RGB images struggle to detect invisible defects. Considering that near infrared (NIR) imaging is sensitive to changes in object structure and material. We integrate RGB and NIR images with ADS-DeepLabv3+ for semantic segmentation of apple defects. ADS-DeepLabv3+ combined with RGB and NIR images for apple defects segmentation outperformed RGB images alone, with a higher MIoU of 3.57 % and a higher MPA of 2.83%. The proposed method can effectively segment apple defects.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Density-Based Clustering Pipeline for Track Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In high-energy physics, the capability to accurately and efficiently track charged particles is essential for effective data analysis. This article introduces an innovative density-based clustering pipeline intended for the track reconstruction task, incorporating Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm and Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure (OPTICS) algorithm. Results on simulated data suggest that the proposed method offers improvements in both effectiveness and robustness compared to traditional techniques, with performance on par with state-of-the-art neural network-based approaches. Furthermore, this pipeline demonstrates significant potential for real-time applications in high-energy physics experiments, offering a scalable and robust solution.

articleTitle: Multi-focus Image Fusion Using Morphological Filter-Based Bi-Dimensional Empirical Mode Decomposition and Gradient Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at improving the quality of multi-focus image fusion, this paper proposes a multi-focus image fusion method using morphological filter-based BEMD (Bi-dimensional empirical mode decomposition) and gradient optimization. It firstly decomposes the input images into several intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) with multiple frequency levels and residuals by morphological filter-based BEMD. Subsequently, the high-frequency IMF component is used to generate an energy matrix, and the initial focus mapping is constructed by a voting mechanism. In order to improve the fusion accuracy, the objective function related to the image gradient is constructed to optimize the initial focus mapping. Finally, a fusion image is generated by combining the optimized focus mapping with the input images. The experimental results show that the newly-proposed method can achieve good results against the common problems of artifacts, blocking effect and boundary misjudgment near the focus boundary area in the process of multi-focus image fusion.

articleTitle: Multiple Attention and Lesion-aware Dynamic Kernel for Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Colorectal cancer ranks among the primary contributors to cancer-related mortality globally. Polyps growing in the colon and rectum are precursors to colorectal cancer, making efficient and accurate detection of polyps in images of great practical significance. However, due to variations in the shape and size of polyps and the low contrast between polyp boundaries and the surrounding intestinal textures, accurate segmentation of polyps becomes challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes two attention mechanism modules and A scheme for dynamically generating and updating kernels to enhance lesion awareness. Specifically, an efficient self-attention module is used to capture long-range contextual relationships, while a cross-attention module based on the polyp boundary region is employed to perceive differences between the boundary and the surrounding mucosa, along with a dynamic kernel generation and update scheme to obtain global contextual features of the input image. We validated our algorithmic network on two publicly available polyp benchmarks, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms alternative cutting-edge techniques.

articleTitle: Enhancing Breast Cancer Detection Using Dual-View Cross Attention with Swin Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a significant global health issue, particularly impacting women. Early detection and accurate diagnosis are essential for improving patient outcomes. In this study, we explore a deep learning-based approach utilizing Swin Transformer with Dual-View Cross Attention to enhance breast cancer detection. Leveraging mammography images from the RSNA dataset, our method achieved an accuracy of 0.81 and an AUC of 0.87. These results underscore the potential of advanced deep learning techniques in improving breast cancer detection through medical imaging.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Fall Risk Prediction Model for Chinese Older Adults
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To predict the risk of falls in older Chinese adults, and to develop a machine learning model for assessing fall risk based on longitudinal study data, which can help identify high-risk individuals and provide a basis for formulating effective interventions. METHODS: A total of 2350 elderly people who participated in CHARLS during 2020 were selected for the study, and the prediction model was constructed. Several machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, K-nearest neighbor, random forest, neural network, decision tree) were used to assess fall risk. Explore the best cut-off points and adjust parameters in the training set, compare the prediction accuracy of the models in the test set, and further explain the best-performing models. RESULTS:Out of the 26 features analyzed, LASSO regression identified 12 features that were critical to model building. Comparing the performance of five different machine learning models on the test set, the results showed that the RF model performed best on various evaluation measures, with a threshold of 0.168, a specificity of 0.860, a sensitivity of 0.526, an accuracy of 0.693, an F1 score of 0.653 and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.738. .CONCLUSION:: The predictive model of machine learning can effectively evaluate the risk of falls in healthy elderly people. Random Forest (RF) methods clearly explain personalized fall risk prediction.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Classification of Soil Images Based on Frequency-Space Feature Fusion and Dynamic Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved feature extraction method to enhance the accuracy of soil image classification, with the aim of more effectively capturing the diverse structures, textures, and components within soil images. Traditional convolutions often fail to fully exploit deep features when processing complex images. To address this limitation, we replace the original standard convolution with ODConv, which optimizes the convolutional structure and significantly enhances feature extraction capabilities. Additionally, a multi-scale fusion strategy, combining frequency and spatial features, is introduced, enabling the model to more precisely capture feature information at various scales, thereby improving classification robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved model achieves a classification accuracy of 91.07% on the soil image dataset, a 1.09 percentage point increase over the unmodified MobileNetV3. Further experiments indicate that the enhanced model exhibits greater stability and stronger generalization when applied to different types of soil images, thus validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction Based on Graph Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The method for sequence annotation has a large search space and is prone to errors in the extraction fragments of aspect terms and opinion items, and the use of external syntactic dependency parsers is susceptible to producing parsing errors. In this paper, we propose syntactic dependency and semantic relations enhancement based on Graph Convolutional Network (SE-GCN) for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction. The dilated convolution with multiple expansion rates is used to obtain the semantic information of word pairs at different distances, and the double affine parser is used to construct a word-pair syntactic dependence tree. The syntactic dependence relationship between aspect terms and opinion items in the sentence is established, and the word-pair syntactic feature information is obtained. Finally, the graph convolutional neural model is used to aggregate the semantic and syntactic information of word pairs, update the node features, and predict the emotional polarity. Through multiple experiments, the SE-GCN model achieves good performance on multiple datasets and proves that the addition of syntactic information improves the accuracy of aspect sentiment triplet prediction.

articleTitle: Research on Artificial Intelligence Platform for Power Dispatching Based on Cloud Native Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Due to the complexity of the composition of surface features information in remote sensing images, the recognition and mapping effects are often difficult to meet the actual application needs. Therefore, the research on remote sensing image surface features recognition and vectorization mapping based on artificial intelligence is proposed. In the construction stage of remote sensing image feature map, based on the internal relationship between remote sensing data points, the feature map is used to reflect the local similarity characteristics of remote sensing data; Through the semi supervised mechanism of artificial intelligence algorithm - Markov random field model, the specific information of the ground object map is recognized. In the mapping stage, the constrained geometry algorithm is introduced, and the CGA rule file is used as a component to drive the 3D creation process. After the integration of basic terrain and 2D spatial data, the mapping is completed by aligning the footprint of the figure recognition object with the terrain network. In the test results, the OA corresponding to the recognition results of the design method has obvious advantages in stability and specific level compared with the control group, and mapping can effectively reflect the details of ground objects.

articleTitle: Multimodal Emotion Recognition Method Based on Adaptive Selection Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to grasp students' emotional state in time, adjust teaching methods in time to stimulate students' learning interest and improve classroom teaching efficiency, this paper proposes an emotion recognition method based on adaptive selection strategy. Firstly, three kinds of emotion signals are acquired and pre-processed and converted to obtain the image signals of three channels. Then, Residual Deep Convolutional Neural Network is used to extract emotion features and preliminary identification of emotion categories for the image signals of multiple channels respectively. Then, adaptive selection strategy is adopted to select effective channels from the preliminary identification results and carry out the fusion of feature parameters. Finally, multi-classifier decision making algorithm is used for final emotion recognition. This method can select the channel data reflecting the true emotion to make the final decision, which makes up the deficiency of single mode and improves the robustness and recognition rate of the recognition method.

articleTitle: LogABC: A Log Anomaly Detection Model Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Logs record important status information during system operation, and automated log anomaly detection can accurately locate the cause of system failures. However, log statements can evolve over time and have instability issues. Therefore, a new method for anomaly detection of log sequences is proposed. Using Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformers model and quantity feature extraction model to extract log semantic features and quantity features, then using Convolutional Neural Network to extract local information of log sequence semantic features, using Bidirectional Gate Recurrent Unit to extract contextual information of log sequence semantic features, and using Adaptive Boosting algorithm to fuse quantity features and local and contextual information of semantic features for anomaly detection. The performance of the proposed method was validated on HDFS and BGL datasets. Compared with 6 benchmark models, this model has the best precision and F1-score. The experimental results indicate that this method can effectively handle the problem of data instability in log sequences.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Detection Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Fusion and Dual-Backbone
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Addressing the limitations of visible light singlemodal target detection algorithms, which are affected by external factors like illumination, and infrared single-modal algorithms, which lack complete target information, we propose a pedestrian detection algorithm based on dual-backbone and multi-modal multi-scale fusion, building upon YOLOv8.The network employs a dual-backbone structure derived from the YOLOv8n lightweight network. An SMMF(Scale-Multiple Multimodal Feature Fusion) module is designed to fuse features from both modalities at multiple scales. The GhostConv module is introduced to enrich features and reduce computational cost. Additionally, the SBAp2 is integrated into the network neck, enhancing the fusion of deep and shallow features and leveraging both deep semantic information and shallow image location information. The ShapeIoU is adopted as the loss function, replacing the original bounding box regression loss, to incorporate the shape and scale of the bounding box into the loss calculation, thereby improving target detection accuracy. Experimental results indicate that the improved algorithm achieves an AP0.5 of 78.5% and an FPS of 156.3. Compared to the original visible light single-modal and infrared single-modal YOLOv8n algorithms, the missed detection rates were reduced by 30.1% and 13.4%, respectively, while the AP0.5 is increased by 21.2% and 8.2%, demonstrating its superiority over the single-modal YOLOv8n detection algorithm.

articleTitle: A Method for Obstacle Detection in Radiotherapy Room Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The presence of obstacles in the radiotherapy room can disrupt equipment operation and even lead to accidents. To address this, monitoring cameras could be installed to detect these obstacles. In this study, an intelligent obstacle recognition model for radiotherapy rooms is proposed. The model utilizes deep learning to automatically extract obstacle features, eliminating the need for human monitoring and improving the quality and speed of obstacle detection. By proposing the improved YOLOv5 model, which replaces the original module with MobileNetV3 in the backbone section of YOLOv5 and utilizes CA attention mechanism instead of the SENet attention mechanism of MobileNetV3, the detection model’s parameter count is reduced, and the ability to capture spatial information with low sensitivity is enhanced. To evaluate the model, a self-made dataset consisting of commonly encountered obstacles in radiotherapy rooms. Evaluation indicates that while ensuring detection accuracy, the proposed model reduces the parameter count and weight file size to 3187527 and 6.7MB, respectively, which are 3840193 and 7.7MB lower than the unmodified YOLOv5, and 360623 and 0.7MB lower than the MobileNet-YOLOv5. The results demonstrate that the detection efficiency of obstacle recognition in radiotherapy rooms can be significantly improved by applying improved YOLOv5 model.

articleTitle: Ship Target Detection Algorithm for SAR Images Based on YOLOv8-obb Rotating Bounding Box
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the development of rotating bounding box target detection technology, the use of rotating bounding box for ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images has become a research hotspot. However, due to the small ship target, high speckle noise, side flap effect, unclear boundary and other reasons in SAR images, there are still some obstacles in rotating bounding box SAR ship image detection. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a rotating frame SAR image ship target detection algorithm based on YOLOv8-obb. First, using YOLOv8n-obb as the benchmark network, the SPPF_LSKA module fusing LSKA attention is proposed to enhance the feature extraction ability of the model for SAR ship images. Secondly, the noise suppression effect of the image is enhanced by introducing the DySample module. The robustness and reliability of the model are verified through a large number of experiments conducted on the standard datasets SSDD, HRSID and RSDDSAR. The experimental results show that compared with YOLOv8n-obb, the improved model improves the accuracy by 2.7% on SSDD and 1% on mAP50-95; by 1.1% on HRSID and 0.2% on mAP50-95; and by 1.1% on RSDD-SAR and 0.2% on mAP50-95. This model outperforms the existing SAR image ship detection model with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: VM-UNet++: Vision Mamba with Adaptive Feature Reweighting and Multiscale Fusion for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a vital role in contemporary clinical practice, offering clinicians quantitative analysis and visualization of lesions. This process aids in early diagnosis, disease evaluation, surgical planning, and monitoring the effects of treatment.However, how to effectively suppress background noise and accurately segment lesion boundaries poses challenges to the model. In order to solve these problems, we propose an enhanced medical image segmentation model, VM-UNet ++.Specifically, we have developed a novel multilevel feature enhancement mechanism that incorporates bilinear interpolation downsampling and large-kernel grouped attention gate (LGAG) modules, aimed at enhancing detail retention and boundary clarity. Furthermore, we introduce an SE-VSS module designed to dynamically modify the weights of feature maps, thereby improving the model's emphasis on critical features. Additionally, an asymmetric encoder-decoder architecture is utilized in our approach. We performed extensive experimental validation on several publicly available datasets, including Synapse, ISIC17, and ISIC18 datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the VM-UNet++ model achieves outstanding performance across various evaluation metrics, validating its effectiveness and value in the domain of medical image segmentation.

articleTitle: Research on Real-Time 3D Image Acquisition System Based on Stripe Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the demand for rapid acquisition of three-dimensional profiles in industrial online inspection, a real-time 3D image acquisition system has been designed and researched. This system is based on the principles of optical projection and binocular vision fusion, utilizing a DLP projector and industrial cameras to construct a hardware platform, along with the development of an efficient 3D reconstruction algorithm. A three-frequency phase-shifting coding scheme is employed in the stripe pattern design, and a phase unwrapping algorithm guided by a quality map is proposed to enhance reconstruction reliability. The system achieves parallel processing through a CUDA heterogeneous computing platform and establishes a four-stage pipeline structure to optimize real-time performance. Experimental results show that the system meets the expected goals in key metrics such as spatial resolution, measurement accuracy, and real-time performance. In practical applications on the mobile phone casing inspection production line, the system demonstrates superior detection efficiency and reliability compared to traditional methods. The research results provide a complete solution for rapid 3D inspection, holding significant engineering application value in fields like industrial quality inspection and reverse engineering.

articleTitle: Enhancing Astronomical Image Stitching with XFeat: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image stitching is a widely applicable technique, with its importance magnified in the realm of astronomical research, where the assembly of high-quality composite images is essential for the accurate measurement and detailed analysis of celestial bodies. The limitations of astronomical cameras, including their restricted fields of view and the propensity for wide-angle lenses to introduce fisheye distortions, present significant challenges in capturing large field-of-view astronomical images in a single exposure. Consequently, the stitching of multiple images emerges as a critical technique for the acquisition of expansive astronomical imagery. In this paper, a novel deep learning-based approach to astronomical image stitching is introduced. The method leverages deep neural networks to automatically extract keypoints from images and perform feature matching, thereby significantly outperforming traditional stitching techniques. Termed XFeat, the proposed method harnesses the power of convolutional neural networks (CNN) to identify and align features across images with high precision, resulting in a substantial enhancement in the quality of stitched astronomical images.

articleTitle: Character-Based Manchu Segmentation and Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, advancements in artificial intelligence have significantly improved Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for various languages and scripts. Manchu, the official language of the Qing Dynasty, holds valuable historical and cultural information but presents challenges for OCR due to its vertical writing style, character connectivity, and limited resources. This paper presents a character-based segmentation and recognition method for Manchu script. The method uses an improved DBNet algorithm for segmentation and an enhanced Vision Transformer (ViT) algorithm for recognition, ensuring efficient detection and accurate recognition of Manchu characters. We created a dataset for the models through systematic data collection and used data augmentation techniques, including geometric transformations and CycleGAN-based style transfer, to enhance the model's robustness across different styles. The proposed approach shows significant improvements in segmentation and recognition accuracy, outperforming traditional methods. Experimental results show a detection accuracy of 93.5%, a recognition accuracy of 95.5%, and an overall model recognition rate of 91.3%. These findings contribute to the digitalization and automation of Manchu document recognition, aiding the preservation and accessibility of Manchu cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Infrared Small Ship Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To tackle the challenges in infrared ship target detection, such as difficulties in detecting small ships, blurry image boundaries, and varying ship scales, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 target detection algorithm. First, the Selective Boundary Aggregation (SBA) module is employed to enhance boundary feature extraction. Additionally, a lightweight Mixed Local Channel Attention (MLCA) module is introduced to fuse channel and spatial information, improving the network's ability to detect multi-scale targets. The Deep Robust Feature Downsampling (DRFD) module is also incorporated to improve feature extraction robustness. Finally, the combined bounding box loss function Focal-PIoU2-Loss is used to further improve the detection accuracy for small targets and the robustness of the model. The proposed DMS-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates a 3.1% improvement in mean Average Precision (mAP50) compared to the baseline YOLOv8 algorithm.

articleTitle: Parkinson's EEG classification model based on the channel optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, Electroencephalogram (EEG) has gradually become one of the important means of early Parkinson's disease (PD) detection because of its non-invasive and real-time monitoring capability. This paper discusses the EEG signal analysis method from the effective feature extraction techniques and the application of traditional machine learning algorithms. Although traditional methods are able to provide some degree of feature interpretability, there are limitations in handling high-dimensional feature space and redundant features, resulting in decreased classification performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification model based on artificial channel optimization, through channel selection of EEG signals recorded by 64-lead devices, screening out the optimal channel combination highly related to PD, and then achieving efficient classification. Specifically, the study uses publicly available Parkinson's disease EEG datasets, employs power spectral density (PSD) features, and combines manual channel selection with the strong classification capabilities of SVM to achieve effective classification of PD EEG signals. In addition, the article highlights that model performance may vary on different datasets, and more clinical validation is needed in the future, and suggests to combine other machine learning technologies such as deep learning to further improve model performance.

articleTitle: The Intelligence Decision Model Through Improved Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, with the vigorous promotion and support of national policies, the science and technology innovation enterprises are booming. They have actively responded to the country’s call and constantly pursued new technologies, business formats, and models, creating a good atmosphere of "mass entrepreneurship and innovation". The development of science and technology innovation enterprises still faces endless problems, such as irrational allocation of funds and lack of innovative talents. Reasonable strategic intelligence decisions are crucial for science and technology innovation enterprises. However, due to science and technology innovation enterprise data’s professionalism, privacy, and sensitivity, it is difficult to share the data publicly, resulting in data decision model analysis and stagnant development. Therefore, to solve the data sharing problem, this article proposes an improved differential privacy based on information entropy and constructs a data query model. To assess the effectiveness of improved differential privacy, experiments are conducted using the Kaggle dataset and the personal information data of the employees, and error metrics are selected for evaluation, the results prove that the proposed method is strongly competitive.

articleTitle: Enhancing ResNet50 with Depth-wise Separable Convolution Squeeze-and-Excitation and Channel Squeeze-and-Excitation Modules for Accurate Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Remote sensing image scene classification is crucial for urban planning and disaster monitoring. Existing methods often struggle with extracting local texture and global semantic features and exploring inter-channel relationships, limiting classification accuracy. To address these issues, we propose Res2SE50 model, an enhanced ResNet50 model integrating Depth-wise Separable Convolution Squeeze-and-Excitation (DSE) and Channel Squeeze-and-Excitation (CSE) attention mechanisms. This approach preserves spatial and global features while enhancing feature extraction through cascading CSE with DSE. Evaluated with 20% training data on the AID and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets, Res2SE50 achieved accuracies of 91.52% and 94.09%, respectively—0.79% and 1.63% higher than the latest LHNet models. Visualization analysis confirms the model’s effectiveness in distinguishing scene features, demonstrating its strong performance and feasibility for remote sensing scene classification.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Real-Time Object Detection Method Integrated Swin-Transformer and YOLO for Construction Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Computer vision has significantly improved the management efficiency of safety, progress, efficiency, and quality in the construction process due to its real-time, high efficiency, low cost and ability to continuously and automatically recognize various classes of elements at the construction site. However, it is still a great challenge to accurately detect multiple classes of objects and small objects on the site in real-time due to the chaotic and large scope of the on-site construction environment and the concentration and variety of construction elements. Therefore, this study proposes a single-stage object detection method integrating Swin-Transformer and YOLOv5 for real-time detection of multiple classes of objects at construction sites. In the experiments, the v5n model with the smallest size is used for training, and the mAP@50 under this method reaches 80.57%, which is 10.81% higher than the original YOLOv5n model. It achieves an inference speed of 2 milliseconds per image, which meets the real-time requirements.

articleTitle: The Substation Defect Detection Method Based on FEFPN-YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to ensure the safe and stable operation of substation and enhance the intelligent anomaly monitoring ability of substation, this paper proposes a substation anomaly and equipment defect detection algorithm based on the improved YOLOv7 model. Based on the YOLOv7 algorithm, a novel multi-branch backbone and neck network fusion feature pyramid network (FEFPN) framework is introduced. By adding the information of different channels of backbone network and neck network, the method effectively combines spatial location features with rich semantic information in the image, significantly improving the multi-scale target detection performance and improving the sensitivity to small targets. Experimental tests show that the mAP value of this algorithm is 0.917, which is 8.4% higher than that of YOLOv7. The results show that this method can effectively detect the abnormal and faulty equipment around the substation, and improve the level of intelligent monitoring of the substation.

articleTitle: Detection of Pantograph Angle Deficiency Based on Optimized YOLOv8n Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A optimized YOLOv8 detection algorithm, UIB-YOLOv8, is proposed to address the problems of high missed and false detection rates in pantograph fault detection, as well as difficulty in identifying pantograph angles in environments with insufficient lighting. A key point detection algorithm based on a high-resolution feature pyramid network is used to extract the position of the pantograph angle. The UIB module is introduced into the backbone network to enhance feature extraction in the image. The MQA attention mechanism is combined to reduce the number of model parameters and improve detection speed. Finally, a Focal Loss loss function is added before the result output to reduce the problem of imbalanced sample categories. The experimental results show that UIB-YOLOv8 improves MAP by 2.2%, reduces parameter count by 26.35%, and reduces floating-point computation by 24.36% compared to YOLOv8 algorithm. Especially in low light conditions, the accuracy of identifying pantograph angle is improved by 4.8%.

articleTitle: Multi-Region Weighted Registration Method for Facial Deformation in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In image-guided TMS navigation, patients’ posture and facial expression result in facial deformation, which finally affects positioning accuracy of the stimulation coil. This paper proposes a multi-region weighted registration method to mitigate the impacts. First, a facial partition model is built. The facial surface is divided into 9 parts based on facial muscles’ distribution. Second, a coarse registration is implemented automatically based on facial anatomical landmarks. Finally, a fine registration is implemented by an improved ICP algorithm where the reciprocal value of part’s surface distance is assigned as the weight value for each part. Experimental results show that this method effectively improves registration accuracy in the presence of local facial deformation.

articleTitle: FE-YOLOv8n: A YOLOV8 Enhancement Algorithm for Effective Fire Extinguisher Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: People often rely on optical devices to identify the source of fire in a timely manner in order to prevent fires, but it is also crucial to promptly activate firefighting equipment. At present, there are models on the market that combine neural networks such as CNN with location algorithms for real-time detection of fire extinguisher positions, which can make real-time detection and alarm through cloud services. However, there is a lack of algorithms that can accurately identify the type of fire extinguisher and specific occlusion situations. Firstly, this article proposes using a model, based on YOLOv8n, to detect several main types of fire extinguishers (which can be determined by shape). Secondly, we propose a target detection algorithm based on CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) that can effectively detect specific fire extinguishers: FE-YOLOv8. The dataset consists of CSDM, Billbill videos, and on-site images, and specific image enhancements have been made for different types of fire extinguishers.The trained model achieved a mAP of 90%, outperformed the original, and increased by 1.2 percentage points.

articleTitle: SAR Aircraft Image Detection Network Based on Scene Feature Enhancement and Multi-Field Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
