abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of deep learning technology, SAR aircraft target detection research has shown new vitality. SAR aircraft image has the characteristics of strong background noise interference and multi-scale, which makes aircraft image detection very challenging. This paper presents a novel SAR aircraft detection network, ASFF-NET, designed to enhance detection accuracy while remaining lightweight. It features an advanced scene feature fusion module (ASFF) to mitigate background noise, a multi-receptive field interaction module (MRFISPPF) for handling multi-scale targets, and a multi-channel hybrid downsampling module (AFdown). Experimental results demonstrate that ASFF-NET outperforms the original YOLOv8 by 2.3% in mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</inf> and 0.8% in mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50:95</inf>, with minimal increases in parameters and computation, proving its improved accuracy and generalization while maintaining a lightweight structure.

articleTitle: Research on Image Segmentation Method Based on U-net Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image segmentation is a crucial task in the domain of computer vision, aiming to partition an image into multiple connected regions with similar characteristics. This paper focuses on extracting tooth contours automatically from dental medical images through an improved U-net network to enhance dentists’ working efficiency and assist physicians in more accurate diagnosis and treatment. The proposed improvement approach involves a series of modifications based on the U-net, such as introducing the CBAM attention module and integrating the ability of Contextual Transformer (CoT) to incorporate global context. This enhances the performance of U-net in image segmentation tasks, allowing the network to capture and analyze the complex features in medical images more delicately and comprehensively, achieving precise and efficient automatic segmentation of medical images.

articleTitle: Addressing Long-Tailed Age Estimation with Balancing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In real life, the human age distribution exhibits a pronounced long-tail characteristic, which can interfere with age estimation, leading to a decrease in the accuracy of age estimation models under this long-tail characteristic. In recent years, the long-tail characteristic of age estimation datasets has become increasingly prominent, manifesting in both real life and facial datasets as a lack of samples for the elderly and children. We refer to categories with a high number of samples as head classes and those with a low number of samples as tail classes. Traditional research methods often involve forcibly enhancing the prediction weights of tail classes, which damages the prediction weights of head classes or significantly increases the complexity of the model. In response to this issue, a new method for long-tail age estimation called Balanced Prediction Constraint (BPC) method has been proposed, which is used to rebalance long-tail age estimation by imposing prediction constraints on the original dataset. This method neither increases the complexity of the model nor affects the head classes while enhancing the prediction probabilities of the tail classes. Experimental results on the Morph II dataset achieved an Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.32, which is a better result compared to methods like OR-CNN and CORAL, and it remains competitive when compared to other advanced methods.

articleTitle: Wavelet-Enhanced Transformer for High-Fidelity Image Colorization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the field of image colorization, we propose an enhanced model based on the VQGAN-Transformer framework, incorporating wavelet transforms to better emulate the hierarchical structures of human visual perception and improve the quality of unconditional colorization. While the traditional VQGAN-Transformer framework effectively captures global information in image generation, it still exhibits limitations in detail fidelity and color consistency. To address these issues, we introduce wavelet transforms between the image encoding and quantization stages, leveraging their multi-scale analysis capability to extract hierarchical features, allowing the colorized images to more closely resemble natural human perception. In our method, wavelet transforms are embedded between the image encoder and quantizer, decomposing image features across multiple scales to construct a hierarchy aligned with the human visual system, while re-quantization enhances color and detail fidelity. In summary, this study validates the effectiveness of wavelet transforms in unconditional image colorization, providing a new approach to improving model performance in colorization tasks.

articleTitle: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage Assisted Diagnostic Based on Attribute Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Subconjunctival hemorrhage is a common ophthalmic disease. It usually does not cause serious visual impairment, but it may be an early sign of serious diseases such as leukemia, hemophilia and septicemia. Traditional manual diagnosis relies on the subjective judgment of doctors. The traditional digital image processing algorithm is only used to classify multiple eye diseases and is not targeted. This paper proposes an auxiliary diagnostic algorithm for subconjunctival hemorrhage based on attribute recognition. The algorithm processes and analyzes a dataset that has been annotated under the guidance of ophthalmologists. By introducing an attention mechanism to the original ResNet50, it enhances focus on effective spatial locations and semantic information channels. Using a multi-task joint training approach, the network can simultaneously recognize nine attributes of subconjunctival hemorrhage, obtaining specific symptoms. To enhance the overall recognition accuracy of the multi-task network, a weighted penalty mechanism is introduced into the loss function. Validation on the test set shows that our algorithm performs exceptionally well in recognizing the nine attributes, with an average accuracy of 92.87% and a highest accuracy of 98.96%.

articleTitle: EdgeFlow: Combining Local Feature Enhancement and Sobel-Based Channel Attention for Optical Flow Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: High-precision optical flow estimation is critical for achieving precise self-localization and environmental mapping. Existing optical flow approaches, however, struggle with accuracy issues when dealing with regions of high gradient variation, such as edges. This paper introduces a new optical flow estimation framework named EdgeFlow, designed to enhance the detection accuracy of edge pixel motion and to coherently extract high-gradient features, all while keeping computational complexity low. By integrating multi-scale local detail feature extraction with a Sobel-Channel Attention mechanism, EdgeFlow seeks to improve performance in these challenging areas. The experimental results indicate that our model surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods on the KITTI optical flow benchmark, exhibiting particularly notable advancements in the movement estimation of edge areas. These findings affirm the method's efficacy and practical viability.

articleTitle: A Novel Iteration Method for Large-Scale Rotation Measurement Using Phase-Based Motion Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The utilization of computer vision in non-contact measurements has garnered substantial attention now, particularly phase-based motion estimation (PME), which stands out for its low computational complexity and high precision in small amplitude motion assessment. However, PME exhibits significant limitations when applied to large-scale rotation measurement. To address this, a novel iterative large-scale rotation measurement method (LR-PME) is proposed in this study. This method breaks large-scale rotation motions into small-amplitude movements frame by frame, dynamically updating the orientation parameter of Gabor wavelet and the coordinates of measurement points. It utilizes Otsu method for threshold evaluation to ensure update accuracy and employs the invariance of pixel distances between measurement points and the rotation center for correction, thereby enabling continuous measurement of large-scale rotation motions. Numerical simulations and laboratory test confirm the robustness of LR-PME, demonstrating superior computational performance.

articleTitle: Small Target Detection Algorithm Based on SDBNet and Multiple Detection Heads
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Despite the great success of deep learning in object detection at present, its performance and efficiency for small target detection in UAV images are still unsatisfactory. In order to improve the performance of small target detection, which proposes an algorithm MS-YOLO based on the YOLOv8 algorithm to improve the backbone network and the detection head. Firstly, the SPD (Space-To-Depth Convolution), which is a feature extraction layer suitable for low-resolution images and small target images, is integrated into the shallow layer of the backbone network, which does not use stepwise convolution and pooling to better retain the small target feature information. This layer does not use step-width convolution and pooling, which can better retain the small target feature information. Secondly, a detection header specialized for the small target feature layer is added. The improved algorithm achieves state-of-the-art detection results on the VisDrone dataset with an average precision (AP) of 46.5 and 28.0, respectively, and a model parameter count of 16.8M, which improves the detection accuracy while maintaining lightweight.

articleTitle: Exploration of an Attention based Two-Stream Dual-Path Networks for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Deep neural networks are incapable of tackling inter-frame correlation information within speech sequences, which is important for speech enhancement task. Based on this consideration, attention mechanisms are designed to learn long-term temporal dependencies information from input features. This paper proposes an attention based Two-Stream Dual-Path Conformer Networks (TSDPCNet) for speech enhancement work, which can effectively extract both amplitude and phase information from speech signals. In this network, self-attention mechanism is employed to focus on the global information of the speech sequence, while the dual-path attention enables simultaneous extraction of sequence information from both the time and frequency domains. Experimental results on the VoiceBank + DEMAND datasets shows that the proposed TSDPCNet outperforms the conventional speech enhancement methods.

articleTitle: Coarse-to-Fine Multi-View 3D Reconstruction with SLAM Optimization and Transformer-Based Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The complexity of reconstructing 3D scenes from multi-view datasets continues to challenge the field of computer vision due to variations in viewpoint and overlapping regions among images. This study proposes a coarse-to-fine structured light framework that integrates sparse and dense feature matching techniques to enhance both the efficiency and accuracy of multi-view 3D reconstruction. By incorporating a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)-based approach and parallel bundle adjustment, our model demonstrates superior performance on key metrics—feature matching accuracy, reprojection error, and camera trajectory precision—compared to existing frameworks. Notably, our approach introduces a Transformer-based multi-view matching module to bolster robustness and optimize reconstruction accuracy with a hybrid loss function. Experimental results on public multi-view datasets confirm substantial improvements across standard evaluation metrics, indicating the framework’s efficacy in addressing multi-view inconsistency.

articleTitle: Ultrasound Placenta Image Segmentation Based on TransCDnet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The placenta is essential for fetal growth, making its health assessment critical during pregnancy. Ultrasound, despite being the primary diagnostic tool for placental evaluation, presents challenges like noise, low contrast, and artifacts, complicating image segmentation. This paper introduces an advanced TransCDnet model tailored for ultrasound segmentation hurdles, enhancing feature extraction through ResNet, Deformable convolution, and Depthwise separable convolution. These technologies allow dynamic receptive field adjustments and efficient multi-scale detail capture. The decoder leverages depthwise separable convolution, optimizing local and global context processing, thus boosting image detail reconstruction and accurate target segmentation. Tested on a dataset from the Women's and Children's Health Hospital of Wuhan City, the TransCDnet model demonstrated superior placental segmentation performance, achieving a mean_dice of 0.873 and a miou of 0.771. This study not only advances medical image segmentation technology but also significantly contributes to prenatal diagnostics, offering a robust tool for placental health evaluation in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Advanced Object Detection and Pose Estimation with Hybrid Task Cascade and High-Resolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the field of computer vision, 6D object detection and pose estimation are critical for applications such as robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. Traditional methods often struggle with achieving high accuracy in both object detection and precise pose estimation simultaneously. This study proposes an improved 6D object detection and pose estimation pipeline based on the existing 6D-VNet framework, enhanced by integrating a Hybrid Task Cascade (HTC) and a High-Resolution Network (HRNet) backbone. By leveraging the strengths of HTC’s multi-stage refinement process and HRNet’s ability to maintain high-resolution representations, our approach significantly improves detection accuracy and pose estimation precision. Furthermore, we introduce advanced post-processing techniques and a novel model integration strategy that collectively contribute to superior performance on public and private benchmarks. Our method demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art models, making it a valuable contribution to the domain of 6D object detection and pose estimation.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv11 Model for Rose Detection and Counting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study addresses the problem of automatic detection and counting of roses for yield estimation, presenting an enhanced YOLOv11-based model to overcome the time-consuming and error-prone nature of manual counting. To improve detection accuracy for small targets in complex environments, we introduce three key modules into YOLOv11: CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module), BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network), and LMPDIoU (Log-Mean Polynomial Distance IoU). The CBAM module refines feature selection under variable lighting by utilizing spatial and channel attention; BiFPN enables efficient, bidirectional multi-scale feature fusion for dense flower detection; LMPDIoU optimizes bounding box regression, enhancing localization accuracy in occluded and small-target scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv11 significantly outperforms other mainstream algorithms across various lighting conditions and complex scenarios, offering high application value.

articleTitle: Real-time RGBT Tracking Algorithm Based on Multi-modal Interactive Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A real-time RGBT tracking method based on multimodal interaction fusion is suggested to address the issue that multi-domain network-based RGBT target tracking algorithms find it challenging to concurrently consider robustness and realtime performance. It is designed with an information interaction fusion module that can use multi-level features to get more information. Global information from both channel and space dimensions is then fused using a channel space fusion module, which effectively fuses two modal information to enhance tracking performance. The algorithm in this paper is experimentally validated on the GTOT, RGBT234 and LasHeR datasets. The results demonstrate that the algorithm can guarantee robustness while achieving real-time performance, with PR/SR reaching 90.5%/73.2%, 84.9%/61.8%, and 48.1%/34.3%, respectively, and a running speed of 41.07 fps.

articleTitle: Structure Alignment Resampler: More Structure for the Specific ID Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The text-to-image generation methods based on diffusion models have generated a strong response in both industry and academia. As an important application scenario, ID-Driven Generation has become the focus of many researchers' efforts. However, most current methods often encounter the issue of structural misalignment. This is specifically demonstrated by the reference ID image's structural information influencing the structural details of the target image during the generation process. To enhance structural control over generated images, we introduce a novel structure in the image generation process called the Structure Alignment Resampler (SAR). This structure aligns the main subject ID information from the reference image with the structural information contained in the target text description, thereby improving structural control during image generation. To fully utilize the potential of this structure, we also propose a dataset construction method to avoid the occurrence of "copy-paste" phenomena. Additionally, we incorporate a structure-loss during training to further align the ID injection effects in subject-related regions. We evaluated our method on a self-constructed test dataset, and the results indicate that our approach shows promising performance in both extracting ID subject features and controlling target structures.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Based Embedding Adaptation for Few-Shot Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The feature extraction part in existing few-shot learning models often uses simple four-layer convolutional or residual networks, which are not optimized for few-shot contexts. This can lead to extracted features being influenced by parts of the image unrelated to the labeled class, reducing the efficiency of many few-shot learning algorithms. To address this, we proposed the Self-Attention Based Embedding Adaptation (SAEA) method. SAEA introduces a new convolutional layer called Detail-Focused Convolution (DFConv) for better feature extraction without increasing the number of parameters or inference time. Additionally, an embedding adaption function built upon the self-attention mechanism is designed to eliminate the influence of the background part, ensuring that the extracted features belong completely to the labeled class. SAEA has shown promising results on the fine-grained benchmark CUB, as well as the commonly used benchmarks mini-ImageNet and tiered-ImageNet.

articleTitle: An Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Image Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the object detection task of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images, the object distribution is dense and the size is small. It is challenging to extract feature information from the UAV images, resulting in low detection accuracy. To solve these problems, we proposed an improved UAV image object detection algorithm based on YOLOv8. Firstly, the P2 detection layer is introduced to the model, so as to enhance the model's perception of small objects and improve the detection performance. Then, the improved BiFPN is used to fuse the shallow and deep feature information through rich feature information branches. Finally, the RCS-OSA module is introduced to the model to enhance the feature learning ability and inference speed of the model through reparameterized convolution and one-shot aggregation. The experimental results on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that the improved YOLOv8 algorithm that we proposed has a 6.4% increase in mAP50, and mAP50-95 is also improved by 4%. The overall performance is pretty excellent which verifies the effectiveness of the improved methods proposed in this paper in UAV image object detection.

articleTitle: Water Surface Highlight Compensation Method Using Feature Fusion and Improved Criminisi Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In surface-floating debris detection tasks, intense highlights on the water surface can degrade images and occlude floating objects, leading to missed and erroneous detections that compromise the accuracy of detection algorithms. This study proposes a highlight detection and compensation method utilizing feature fusion and an improved Criminisi algorithm. First, the mechanism of water surface highlights is analyzed, and a water surface highlight dataset is collected. The color and positional information of highlighted pixels are combined to train a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) model for identifying highlight areas, excluding highlights in the sky. For the detected highlight regions on the water surface, an improved Criminisi algorithm is applied to compensate and restore the water surface images. Finally, the accuracy of floating debris detection is validated using the YOLOv8 algorithm. Results show that the mean Average Precision (mAP) after highlight compensation reaches 88.7%, representing an increase of 1.7% compared to images without highlight compensation, with mAP@0.5:0.95 improved by 2.2%. In water surface multi-object detection, significant improvements have also been achieved.

articleTitle: Roberta with Low-Rank Adaptation and Hierarchical Attention for Hallucination Detection in LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The prevalence of hallucinations in responses generated by large language models (LLMs) poses significant challenges for the reliability of natural language processing applications. This study addresses the detection of such hallucinations through an enhanced Roberta-base model, specifically targeting hallucination responses produced by the Mistral 7B Instruct model. By implementing Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for fine-tuning and incorporating hierarchical multi-head attention and multi-level self-attention weighting mechanisms, we aim to improve both the accuracy of hallucination detection and the interpretability of the model’s decisions. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms baseline models across various metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and area under the curve (AUC). Future research directions will explore the integration of larger-scale models and additional fine-tuning techniques to further bolster the model’s capacity for detecting hallucinations, thereby enhancing the reliability of LLM outputs.

articleTitle: Human Pose Estimation Method Based on Spatial-Aware Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In multi-person pose estimation tasks, keypoint grouping methods based on embedded labels are widely used. However, in complex scenarios such as occlusion and crowding, the results of keypoint grouping are often suboptimal. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a spatial-aware labeling method for multi-person pose estimation. During label initialization, different initial values are assigned to the labels based on the body part to which the keypoint belongs. Additionally, a coordinate encoding method is designed to transform keypoint coordinates into numerical vectors embedded within the labels, forming multi-dimensional labels. The labels generated by this method carry spatial information from the image, enhancing the model's spatial perception. A corresponding loss function is designed to preserve these features during model training. The effectiveness of this method is validated by testing the model's performance across various scenarios on the COCO dataset.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Conditional Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Under-sampled MRI Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is extensively used in medical clinical diagnosis due to its excellent performance in medical imaging. However, the disadvantage of slow imaging speed has hindered the further application of MRI in medical clinical diagnosis. Diffusion probabilistic models (DPM) have achieved impressive results in image restoration due to the extraordinary ability to generate highly realistic images. However, DPM needs to be set up with a long number of diffusion steps to obtain excellent results, leading to the training and sampling process to consume a lot of time. This paper presents a high-frequency conditional diffusion Probabilistic Model (HFC-DDPM), which defines the diffusion and inference process in wavelet domains rather than image domain. On this basis, the Wave-DiffNet, a network for solving MRI reconstruction tasks is presented, which recovers the high-frequency and low-frequency components of MR image by diffusion model and encoder-decoder structure, respectively. Notably, to prevent conflicts between frequencies caused by optimizing objectives at different stages, the Frequency Cross-attention Alignment module is designed to align and normalize the frequencies at each iteration of the denoising process. Our model has been evaluated on the MICCAI Grand Challenge dataset and has significantly improved the quality and speed of MRI image reconstruction.

articleTitle: PP-UNet: Improved Road Crack Segmentation Method Based on U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Addressing the issues of the basic U-Net model's insufficient segmentation effect on road cracks, inadequate fine segmentation of crack contours, difficulty in recognizing narrow cracks, and low segmentation accuracy, this paper proposes an improved road crack segmentation method based on U-Net. Firstly, an enhanced encoder is designed to improve feature extraction capabilities. Secondly, Polarized Self-Attention mechanism is introduced to refine the skip connections of U-Net. Finally, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling module is added before feature fusion to obtain the improved model. Experiments conducted on the public dataset Crack500 show that compared to the original network, the improved model's Kappa coefficient, MIoU, and Dice coefficient have increased by 4.79%, 3.26%, and 2.42% respectively. The method proposed in this paper better adapts to the task of road crack segmentation.

articleTitle: Abnormal motion-triggered field of view restriction as a tool to alleviate symptoms of Cybersickness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Adjusting the field of view is an effective way to reduce the symptoms of cybersickness. In virtual environments, discomfort symptoms are alleviated by limiting the amount of visual information generated by motion. However, frequent changes in the field of view during task completion can hinder the user's task execution and immersion experience. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness and impact of a field of view restrictor, triggered only by abnormal motion, on alleviating CS and maintaining immersion. Compared with previous methods, the field of view restriction triggered by abnormal motion has a significant effect on alleviating CS symptoms while maintaining immersion.

articleTitle: A Study on the Impact of Automated Essay Scoring System Feedback on L2 Writing Quality of Chinese College Learners: A Visual Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study employs text quantitative indicators provided by Natural Language Processing (NLP) technology to conduct a visual analysis of the second language (L2) writing quality of Chinese college learners under the intervention of an Automated Essay Scoring (AES) System from four dimensions—lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, accuracy, and fluency—using eight language feature factors. Visualization techniques such as heatmap, density plot, and box plots were utilized to reveal the interplay between these linguistic features and L2 writing quality. The findings reveal that Average Word Length (AWL), Word Difficulty Average (WDA), and Document Token Count (DTC) are the primary factors influencing AES scoring. The intervention of AES has had a positive effect, as evidenced by improved performance in grammar and spelling accuracy in L2 essays after AES intervention. Meanwhile, challenges remain in the intervention of AES, as L2 writing in terms of lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, and fluency remain in a medium-low range post-intervention. There is considerable variability in vocabulary diversity and syntactic complexity, suggesting a need for more targeted manual instruction and guidance. This study provides a new perspective for exploring the linguistic features and L2 writing quality of Chinese college learners, paving the way for the development of teaching intervention and assessment models.

Author Keywords: the feedback of automated essay scoring

articleTitle: Research on Communication Delay Mechanism of Intelligent Network Connected Vehicle Data Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology and the increasing maturity of intelligent vehicle network technology, the Internet of Vehicles system is an important part of intelligent transportation, and the real-time and accuracy of its data transmission is very important to improve road traffic efficiency and safety. This paper discusses the mechanism of communication delay in automobile intelligent network data transmission system in detail, analyzes the key factors affecting the transmission distance, transmission speed and network congestion of communication delay signal, and proposes an optimization method of cache strategy based on popularity and location prediction. The effectiveness of the strategy is verified by simulation experiments and practical tests, which provides strong support for the further development of automotive network systems.

articleTitle: A Secure Keyword Spotting Scheme Based on Complex Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the privacy risks associated with intelligent voice assistants, this paper proposes a non-interactive, end-to-end keyword spotting scheme in the encrypted domain. The scheme introduces an innovative complex-valued residual neural network (CR-NN) and leverages low-degree polynomial approximations to enable encrypted computation of complex activation functions. By supporting single instruction multiple data (SIMD) operations, the scheme significantly enhances computational efficiency while reducing ciphertext size. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches across multiple performance metrics, balancing efficient keyword spotting with robust privacy protection and offering new insights for the application of deep learning in the encrypted domain.

articleTitle: Hite-HRNet:A High-Performance High-Resolution Human Pose Estimation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In human pose estimation, high-resolution networks have demonstrated remarkable multi-scale feature extraction capabilities, achieving impressive results. However, balancing computational efficiency and performance remains challenging, especially in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel lightweight high-resolution network, Hite-HRNet. This network combines the advantages of global context modeling and multi-scale feature fusion. Specifically, we introduce an enhanced channel-spatial attention method, implemented through two functional modules: Global Pose Attention (GPA) and Multi-Scale Convolution for Pose Estimation (MSC). These modules are embedded into the stem and IterativeHead, respectively, to improve the network’s ability to represent human pose and small targets, such as keypoints, while maintaining low resource consumption. Our work highlights the potential of multi-scale features in advancing pose estimation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Hite-HRNet achieves performance on the COCO dataset that is competitive with state-of-the-art methods, enhancing pose estimation accuracy while maintaining low resource demands.

articleTitle: YOLO-Human: A Simple and Effective Anchor-free Network for Dense Pedestrian Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Pedestrian detection is a crucial aspect of human centered services. However, detecting dense pedestrian scenes presents several challenges, such as pedestrians obstructing each other. Although CNN-based cascaded networks with anchor boxes and Transformer-based networks have achieved excellent results in dense pedestrian detection, their structures are complex and require substantial computational resources. To solve this problem, we propose a simple and effective CNN-based single-stage anchor-free network for dense pedestrian detection called YOLO-Human. First, we design a new anchor-free detection head that can predict the full-body boxes and visible boxes of pedestrians. Additionally, we consider pedestrians' visible box and full-body box information when using the SimOTA positive and negative sample assignment and computation loss methods. Finally, we propose a new weighted IOU loss to allow the network to focus more on pedestrians that overlap within classes and are difficult to detect. The experimental results showed that the proposed YOLO-Human method achieved high performance on the CrowdHuman val dataset. It obtained 93.44% AP, 34.96% MR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, and 86.28% JI.

articleTitle: A Real-time Preprocessing Method for Mixed Heterogeneous Meteorological Remote Sensing Images in Orbit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To solve the real-time generation of level 1 data for meteorological satellites in orbit and improve user experience, this paper proposes a mixed heterogeneous meteorological satellite in orbit real-time preprocessing method. This method receives 0-level data from meteorological satellite payloads and processes it in real-time in orbit to generate 1-level positioning and calibration result data. The positioning and calibration operation of Level 1 products is a repeated operation of the load detector pixel by pixel. This method adopts the hardware acceleration idea to transplant the repeated simple addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division operations into FPGA, realizing real-time processing of remote sensing data in orbit. Before and after hardware acceleration, the processing speed of the FY-3 spectral imaging instrument payload level 1 product increased by 4.5 times, and the positioning accuracy was better than one pixel compared to the standard coastline. The hybrid heterogeneous core processor adopts ARM+FPGA architecture, which consumes 17% of FPGA resources for hardware acceleration compared to CPU processing. The time indicators can meet the real-time processing requirements of various meteorological satellite payloads.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy in Textile Inspection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The textile industry demands rigorous quality control and material analysis to meet stringent standards and consumer expectations. Spectroscopic techniques have emerged as indispensable tools in this domain, offering rapid, nondestructive, and increasingly sophisticated methods for textile inspection. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the evolution and application of spectroscopic techniques in textile inspection. We begin by tracing the historical progression from manual inspection methods to the adoption of spectroscopic techniques. Subsequently, we delve into the principles, advantages, and limitations of prominent spectroscopic techniques, including NIR, UV-Vis, Raman, FTIR, highlighting their specific applications in fiber identification, dye and pigment analysis, fabric structure and performance assessment, and defect detection. Furthermore, we explore the transformative impact of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with spectroscopic methods, enabling advanced data analysis and automation for enhanced accuracy and efficiency. Finally, we address the challenges and future directions of spectroscopic techniques in textile inspection, emphasizing the ongoing pursuit of enhanced sensitivity, portability, and eco-friendly solutions to meet the evolving demands of the textile industry.

articleTitle: More Efficient Text Detection for Chips Based On Loss Weighting Module
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text detection has always been an important branch in the field of deep learning, with applications in tasks such as character detection and recognition for industrial chips. Most deep learning-based text detection algorithms require a large amount of training data, and their detection accuracy remains relatively low for images with complex backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose a loss-weighting module based on a text detection network to improve the detection accuracy of the network. We name this enhanced network "LWNet" which focuses on handling complex, small-sample chip images and effectively enhances character detection precision. Experimental validation on a real-world chip image dataset shows that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 90.4% for chip character detection tasks. Compared to other character detection methods, LWNet demonstrates significant advantages in both accuracy and robustness, contributing to the automation and intelligent advancement of chip inspection processes.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 Orchard Fruit Object Detection Algorithm Based on Enhanced Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Smart agriculture is becoming increasingly popular with the development of computer and artificial intelligence technology. The use of artificial intelligence technology to improve orchard management and enhance harvesting efficiency is an important technology. The current target detection algorithms based on YOLO can preliminarily complete the construction of the system. However, in these detection methods, the feature fusion part did not fully consider the actual contribution differences of different resolution feature maps to the final output, which may become a performance bottleneck when dealing with targets of different sizes and complexities. In response to the above issues, this article proposes an orchard fruit object detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8. This algorithm improves the feature fusion part in YOLOv8 by introducing the BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network) module. This method improves the accuracy and efficiency of the model in detecting objects of different sizes through a more refined feature fusion strategy. Through experiments, it has been proven that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the accuracy of object detection while ensuring computational efficiency, especially when dealing with challenging multi-scale objects. The improved algorithm improved accuracy by 16.5 percentage points, recall by 23.3 percentage points, mAP50 by 16.5 percentage points, and mAP50-95 by 20 percentage points on the avocado dataset. This research achievement has promoted the development of YOLOv8 in terms of performance in practical applications from a new perspective, and laid the foundation for future research on object detection.algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhancing Pneumonia Images: A Comparative Experiment of Image Processing Through 5 Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Pneumonia is an inflammatory lung disease that mainly affects tiny air sacks such as alveoli in the human body. Its mild symptoms may cause inflammation, cough and fever [1]. The classification and detection of common lung images and pneumonia images are helpful in improving the efficiency of disease diagnosis and treatment. The image detected herein is a chest X-ray. In this paper, the transfer learning method and the visual geometry group (VGG), a kind of convolutional neural network (CNN), are used to detect lung images on a multi-scale and lightweight basis. The model proposed in this paper is applied to the original CXR image dataset, and the data enhancement is conducted. Meanwhile, an automatic pneumonia detection system based on a CNN is created [2]. Traditional pneumonia image classifications are difficult and time-consuming, but in this paper, we solve this problem and process images more quickly and efficiently. After data enhancement, the dataset in this paper can achieve 96% classification accuracy using the pretrained model.

articleTitle: Small Target Detection Methods in Complex Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Small target detection is of great significance in military and civilian fields, so the problems of small target aggregation and scale diversity under scene complexity, this paper proposes a small target detection method under complex scenes for small target aggregation and scale diversity under scene complexity. Firstly, we design a multiscale grouping efficient convolution module, Multi-ScaleGroupEfficientConv, to replace part of the C2f module, so as to extract multiscale features efficiently; secondly, we construct a feature pyramid network for small targets and construct a CSP-OmniKernel feature fusion module based on the idea of CSP and OmniKernel to retain the information of small targets to a greater extent. The intent is to retain the information of small targets and improve the target detection ability. Finally, on the VisDrone2019 dataset, comparison experiments are conducted with mainstream algorithms, and the experimental results show that the method in this paper improves 1.2%, 2.1%, 2.6%, and 1.3% in the detection rate, recall rate, mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>, and mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50:95</inf>, respectively, in comparison with the original yolov8n, and the model size and the number of parameters are only 6.1MB and 3.02M, which are better than other mainstream methods.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection Method of Target Axis and Mark Ring Based on Edge Optimization and Line Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional target contour and central axis detection algorithms are easily affected by factors such as non-uniform backgrounds, incomplete target imaging, and tail flame interference, which can lead to deviations in the central axis and mass center, an automatic detection method for the object central axis and mark rings based on edge optimization and line screening is proposed. Firstly, the frame difference algorithm is combined with canny algorithm to initially locate the ROI region of the moving target. Then, an improved edge detection algorithm based on the OTSU method is used to automatically extract the effective edges. Firstly, the frame difference algorithm is combined with the canny algorithm to initially locate the ROI region of the moving target. Then, an improved edge detection algorithm based on the OTSU algorithm is used to automatically extract the effective edges. After that, the target attitude interval and length threshold are calculated using EDLines algorithm, and the central axis is selected based on hough transform and line screening criteria. Finally, the mark rings are detected through RGB image segmentation and morphological operations, and their intersections with the central axis are used as the feature points. The experimental results show that the proposed method has obvious advantages over the traditional algorithms in engineering application, detection efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Automatic Measurement of Human Ear Parameters Based on Object Detection and Landmark Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: How to efficiently obtain human ear parameters is one of the key challenges in personalized HRTF (Head-Related Transfer Function). Traditional methods using 3D laser equipment for human ear parameter measurements require significant manpower and cost investment, while edge detection and contour extraction suffer from a large margin of error in measurement accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose an automatic measurement method for human ear parameters based on object detection and landmark extraction only from a side face image and a frontal ear image. Firstly, to address the issue of scale variations in human ear parameter measurements, a side face image containing both the iris and the human ear is collected. MediaPipe FaceMesh is used for iris detection and an improved YOLOv5s model is used for human ear detection. By utilizing the approximate invariance of human iris diameter, the actual height of the human ear is obtained. Secondly, to calculate human ear parameters more accurately, a frontal ear image is collected, and 55 landmarks of the human ear are extracted. Suitable landmarks are selected to calculate the pixel distances of ear parameters. Finally, based on the actual height of the human ear and the pixel distances of ear parameters, the actual distances of ear parameters are calculated. Experiments show that the margin of error of the proposed automatic measurement method for human ear parameters is about 6%, which meets the requirements of practical applications. Our code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/zzb010221/Automatic-measurement-of-human-ear-parameters.

articleTitle: Robust Object Detection Based on YOLOv8 by Snow Removal Augmentation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In adverse weather conditions, particularly in snow, autonomous driving systems face significant challenges in accurately detecting objects like vehicles and pedestrians. This paper presents an enhanced snow detection model based on YOLOv8, integrating a snow removal module to improve detection performance in snowy conditions. The model addresses the challenges of snow-induced noise through data augmentation and snow removal techniques, optimizing YOLOv8 for various intensities of snowfall. Contributions include the development of a headlight detection approach that utilizes HSV color space adjustments to separate headlight regions from snow noise, preserving critical features during snow removal. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv8 with the snow removal module performs significantly outperforming baseline models like YOLOv5 and YOLOv11 in identifying vehicles and road elements in snowy environments. These improvements enable the system to maintain higher accuracy and robustness in adverse conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Engraving Recognition Method of Nodular Cast Iron Pipe Bearing End Based on Improved YOLOX
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study proposes a method for recognizing the engravings on the spigot ends of ductile iron pipes based on an improved YOLOX model. Ductile iron pipes, known for their excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance, are widely used in critical fields such as municipal water supply, drainage, and gas transportation. To ensure product quality and achieve traceability, identification information is typically engraved on the spigot ends of ductile iron pipes during production. However, traditional manual recognition methods are inefficient and prone to human error. To address this issue, this paper proposes an automated engraving recognition system based on an improved YOLOX model. By integrating techniques such as Depthwise Separable Convolutions, a multi-scale feature extraction network, and an adaptive attention mechanism, the YOLOX model structure is further optimized to enhance recognition accuracy and robustness in complex industrial environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLOX model surpasses traditional models in both recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, proving its effectiveness and reliability for industrial production applications.

articleTitle: Defects of Injection Molding Parts Based on the Improved YOLOv7 Algorithm Research on Detection Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In view of the problem of manual visual inspection and difficulty in ensuring accuracy. Using YOLOv7 add SE attention mechanism module (Squeeze-And-Excitation) to replace the convolution layer, by improving the target detection algorithm of YOLOv7 to various defect image training, through the data shows that the improved model in accuracy (Precision) increased by 5.3%, recall rate (Recall) increased by 5.5 percentage points, the algorithm average accuracy mAP @ 0.5 increased by 8% the detection method can realize automatic detection, with high detection rate and detection accuracy.

articleTitle: An Enhanced YOLOv5-seg Based Digital LAMP for Polydisperse Droplets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Digital nucleic acid amplification technology plays a pivotal role in medical diagnostics. Polydisperse droplet-based nucleic acid detection may be compromised by factors such as varying droplet sizes, impurities and uneven lighting. This paper proposes a enhanced YOLOv5-seg model for polydisperse droplets. The Shuffle Attention mechanism is introduced into the network to improve feature extraction. Wise-IoU (WIoU) is used as the bounding box regression loss function, improving both convergence speed and detection accuracy. Pruning techniques are used to optimize and streamline the model. The enhanced model accurately distinguishes between positive and negative droplets and pillars in complex scenarios, with a mean average precision (mAP) of 97.7% and a 3.3ms reduction in detection time. This improved model offers a highly efficient and cost-effective solution for real-time nucleic acid detection in droplet-based systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of 3D Object Detection Based on Adam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This Optimization theory is a branch of mathematics that studies finding the most reasonable solution under certain conditions and is an important part of operations research. Optimization theory is now widely used in various fields of life, such as machine learning, finance, engineering, etc. Optimization models and methods are also widely used in transportation, national defense, communication and many other fields, so optimization theory has an important role in practice and can help people solve various practical problems. Adam algorithm is an optimization algorithm based on gradient descent, which combines the advantages of AdaGrad and RMSRrop algorithms with adaptive learning rate and momentum, can converge faster and avoid the problem of gradient disappearance or explosion, and plays an important role in the training of deep neural networks. In this paper, we use the Adam algorithm to optimize the selection of more reasonable parameters for the complex scenario of deep neural network and the difficulty of optimization, so that the neural network can accurately identify and localize 3D object targets.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Network for Vehicle Identification: Dense-Inception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: For future intelligent transportation, vehicle classification can provide driver assistance systems, traffic flow statistics, and intelligent parking systems. With the increase in the number of vehicles in cities, it is necessary to develop effective vehicle classification methods for better traffic control, intelligent parking, and electronic toll collection. In order to further optimize the accuracy of identification, this study is based on a self-collected dataset. Based on existing networks, the study adopts the Inception module and the DenseNet network structure. The Inception module combines different convolutional layers in parallel before the image enters the network. Before entering the network, an STN layer is added to preliminarily filter out interference in the image using the attention mechanism. Finally, before entering the fully connected layer, an SPP layer is added to construct a new network structure: Dense-Inception. Due to the relatively small overall amount of data collected, in order to increase the training volume, this project uses mixup and color augmentation, and color inversion to process the original images, further enriching our own dataset. To verify the practical effect of this research, this project compared various deep learning networks that performed well and found that compared to those networks, the network in this research showed significant improvement.

articleTitle: Towards Robustness Against Common Corruptions for Text-based Person Search
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text-based person search (TBPS) retrieves images of individuals based on natural language descriptions. This technology is frequently deployed in complex environments such as video surveillance, where it is susceptible to various visual corruptions, including snow, frame compression, and motion blur. Current TBPS models lack robustness studies against these corruptions. This paper examines the impact of different types of corruption on TBPS models through frequency domain analysis. We introduce two innovative approaches to enhance robustness: hybrid adversarial training and image distribution adaptation. Hybrid adversarial training merges conventional and noise-based adversarial training methods, bolstering the model's resistance to high-frequency corruptions during the training phase. Concurrently, image distribution adaptation adjusts to the low-frequency characteristics of corrupted images, reconciling distribution discrepancies between training and corrupted testing datasets. By integrating these strategies, our enhanced models achieve significant improvements, with at least a 2.02% increase in average Rank@1 accuracy in common corruption tests on the CUHK-PEDES dataset.

articleTitle: Research on Retinex-Gamma Image Enhancement Algorithm Based on Lab Space in 3D Reconstruction Scene
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To deal with the problems such as uneven illumination and unclear modelling in 3D reconstruction, an image enhancement algorithm combining improved Retinex and improved bilateral gamma in Lab color space is proposed. At first, the image is converted from RGB color space to Lab color space. The original images were enhanced with the improved Retinex algorithm, the improved bilateral gamma algorithm and the L-channel enhancement algorithm respectively to obtain three images. Finally, these three images are weighted and fused to obtain the final image. Experimental results based on both visual inspection and objective data are given to demonstrate that the algorithm achieves satisfactory results in preserving color constancy, improving image clarity, and enhancing the performance of 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Predicting and Enhancing Ductility in X2YZ-type Heusler Alloys Using Machine Learning and Abinitio Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>YZ-type Heusler alloys, such as Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnGa, exhibit promising properties like magnetic shape memory, thermoelectric effects, and superconductivity, making them ideal for smart sensors and refrigeration. However, their inherent brittleness limits their mechanical performance, especially in applications requiring elastic or shape memory effects. This study utilizes machine learning (ML) to predict the ductility of these alloys, applying a random forest model combined with advanced feature selection techniques. By training the model on a dataset Heusler alloys from Materials-Project, the study identifies key factors influencing ductility. First-principles calculations validate the predictions, revealing that alloys like Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TaAl show exceptional ductility, surpassing other known Heusler alloys.

articleTitle: Improved CNN Automatic Identification Algorithm for Food Foreign Bodies Based on LeNet-5 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to improve the speed and accuracy of foreign body identification in food. An improved Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was constructed by adding a batch normalization layer and a dropout layer to the LeNet-5 network architecture, and a recognition system was built to realize the automatic identification of foreign objects in food images. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional model, the improved model has significant advantages in detection accuracy and recognition speed, and its recognition accuracy for food foreign bodies can reach 99.75%, and the recognition time is only 0.332 seconds, indicating that the constructed dumpling image foreign body recognition model has excellent performance in detection speed and recognition accuracy, and has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: ADMC: An Attention-based Dense Multi-scale Convolutional architecture for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is crucial for many healthcare applications, and deep learning networks have shown great potential in performing semantic segmentation tasks effectively. However, existing methods often suffer from the loss of important local features. To solve this problem, We introduce an innovative approach: a multi-scale and multi-connection feature adaptive fusion method guided by an attention mechanism. The proposed method emphasizes adaptive fusion of multi-scale and multi-connection features, effectively capturing meaningful features at different scales, while also utilizing attention mechanism to enhance feature representation. Specifically, Our approach leverages dense multi-scale skip connections to bridge the semantic gap between the feature maps of the encoder and decoder, where the feature map in each decoder module is connected with each feature map in encoder module. Besides, our network incorporates a deep attention block (DCS) in the encoder to capture meaningful local features. In the decoder, we introduce an efficient multi-scale convolution block (MSDC) to refine feature maps by performing deep convolution across multiple scales. Experimental results in the well known The ISIC dataset results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the baseline method in the task of medical image segmentation.

articleTitle: Occluded Gait Emotion Recognition Based on Interpolated Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, gait-based emotion recognition has been widely applied in the field of computer vision. However, existing methods for gait emotion recognition typically rely on complete human skeleton data, and their accuracy significantly declines when faced with occlusion. To improve the accuracy of gait emotion recognition under occlusion, this paper proposes an Interpolated Graph Convolutional Network(IGCN). Compared to the original graph convolutional network, the joint interpolation module employs a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) interpolation method to fill in the occluded skeleton joints in space, thereby reducing the negative impact of occlusion on emotion recognition outcomes. On the occluded dataset ELMB, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 71.6%, significantly outperforming other methods, and alleviates the performance degradation caused by occlusion.

articleTitle: Parallel Three-Layer Coupled Bi-GRU Algorithm for Image Caption Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the limitation of Bi-GRU models in capturing fine-grained semantic information when relying solely on forward and backward text modeling, this paper proposes a three-layer parallel structure to capture semantic information more effectively. Each of the three GRU layers extracts semantic information at different scales, enriching the semantic depth of the generated image captions. Furthermore, to integrate the semantic information captured by the three parallel GRU layers, a coupling mechanism is designed to merge the parallel hidden states, allowing interlayer interactions at each time step to enhance the semantic granularity of the fused image captions. Finally, extensive experiments on public datasets are conducted to verify the model’s effectiveness, and the experimental results are analyzed to evaluate the model’s feasibility comprehensively.

articleTitle: HE-Floc: Federated Learning Fingerprint Indoor Localization Method Based on Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Indoor positioning WiFi fingerprint signals and federated learning positioning models can easily lead to user privacy breaches. This article proposes a federated learning fingerprint indoor localization method based on homomorphic encryption. Firstly, federated learning technology breaks down data barriers, realizes the monetization of isolated data value, and utilizes differential privacy to reduce user privacy concerns. Furthermore, by integrating homomorphic encryption into federated learning, the privacy of both data and model parameters is ensured through the homomorphic encryption of the model’s weight parameters. The experimental results show that the scheme can effectively protect the privacy of RSS data and positioning model while ensuring the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: A Tibetan Ancient Uchen Text Line Dataset for OCR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Characters written by hand that represent distinct writing styles are referred to as handwritten text; these are especially common in ancient texts. In the field of digitizing ancient literature, Tibetan ancient document image recognition is a focus of both domestic and international research. However, technological advancement in this field has been hampered by the absence of a specific recognition dataset for image recognition systems of Tibetan ancient documents. This paper addresses this by proposing a dataset for Uchen style text line recognition in Tibetan ancient documents. This dataset includes basic synthetic images of multi-style Uchen text lines as well as real-world images of multi-format Tibetan Uchen text lines that have been manually annotated. Cross-Validation and several rounds of annotation by various people guarantee the quality of the data. Additionally, three popular text line recognition models are used to assess the dataset and validate its usability.

articleTitle: RecOpt: A Recommender-Based Optimization Framework for Enhanced Multi-Objective Decision-Making in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Autonomous driving systems operate in highly complex environments, necessitating real-time, balanced decisionmaking across multiple objectives such as safety, efficiency, and passenger comfort. This study introduces RecOpt, a novel framework that combines recommender algorithms with advanced optimization techniques to enhance multi-objective optimization (MOO) in decision-making. RecOpt tackles the challenges of large-scale mixed-integer MOO by identifying and restructuring key decision variables, thereby reducing the optimization scale and increasing efficiency. By integrating recall and finesorting technologies inherent in recommender systems, RecOpt efficiently screens and selects optimal solutions, surpassing the speed and scalability limitations of traditional MOO methods. Experiments utilizing the NGSIM dataset validate RecOpt’s efficacy in balancing safety, comfort, and efficiency, minimizing decision-making latency, and adapting to dynamic environments. Furthermore, RecOpt offers data-driven insights into explainable decision-making, providing a robust and transparent model for autonomous vehicle decision processes.

articleTitle: EEIE-YOLO: Enhanced Edge Information Extraction YOLO for Electric Bicycle Detection in Elevator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the challenges of low detection accuracy caused by obstructed and overlapping targets in elevator detection of electric vehicles, recent research efforts have proposed various methods to address these issues. Examples include incorporating Transformer-Based VIT attention mechanisms or altering the structure of feature fusion pyramids to enhance network performance. However, these improvements often come with a significant increase in computational costs, thereby reducing the feasibility of deploying real-time object detection algorithms in subsequent stages. Therefore, this paper presents an approach that tackles the aforementioned challenges with an improved YOLOv8 model, which integrates Efficient Multiscale Attention module (EMA)and Involution block indicates to enhance the networks’ ability to extract objects’ edge information , termed EEIE-YOLOv8. Validation on a custom-built dataset of elevator electric vehicle scenarios demonstrates that the EEIE-YOLOv8 algorithm achieves an average precision improvement of 1.1% and a 7.3% increase in precision compared to the original YOLOv8 algorithm. These experimental results affirm that the proposed enhancements effectively meet the detection requirements for electric vehicles, bicycles, and passengers inside elevators under real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Gait Analysis and Prediction of Human Skeleton Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of science and technology, it has become an important research direction in the field of computer vision to use deep learning to estimate human motion. In the field of artificial intelligence, deep learning is a method of learning the characteristics of data and building the model by the information obtained. It analyzes and learns by simulating the neural network of the human brain, and makes machines learn the rules from a large number of data, which can realize the machine’s recognition or prediction of new samples.

articleTitle: Research on Identification of Security Hazards and Risk Control of Low-level Windshear Based on Dual Prevention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Based on the construction of the dual prevention mechanism of China's civil aviation, this paper aims at the unavoidable sudden civil aviation security risk of low-altitude windshear, and combines the TF-IDF-LDA theme identification model based on Gaussian function (TG-LDA), Apriori algorithm, and System Dynamics (SD) simulation to carry out the research on the identification of civil aviation hazards and security risk control. Firstly, the TG-LDA model and Apriori algorithm are used to identify the hazard factors under low-level wind shear and initially calculate the influence weights of some factors on the security level; Then, based on the results of hidden danger identification, we constructed the civil aviation security level flow diagram under low altitude wind shear, identified the key risk factors through SD simulation, and analyzed the control strategy of the key risk factors based on the dual preventive mechanism of civil aviation, so as to provide a reference for the civil aviation safety management.

articleTitle: Deepfakes Video Detection Based on Landmark Calibration and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, deep synthesis video technology has also made significant progress, which has blurred the boundaries between original videos and fake videos. Highly realistic deepfake videos cover multiple aspects such as faces, voices, and scenes, and their authenticity is difficult to discern with the naked eye. Although deep fake videos bring new fun to the entertainment field, they also pose a potential threat to personal privacy protection and social order stability. Therefore, the research on deep forgery technology and its detection technology will be a long-term topic. Currently, most deepfake video detection methods mainly focus on single-frame images and appearance features, which results in a complex model training process and is more sensitive to noise interference. How to effectively utilize the time series characteristics of videos is still an urgent problem to be solved. This paper proposes a model that combines landmark calibration and long short-term memory network (LSTM), aiming to mine the geometric and temporal features of fake videos. The model first preprocesses face images to obtain facial landmarks, and then calibrates these landmarks. The calibrated landmarks are subjected to key feature extraction through the Transformer layer, and then the LSTM layer is used to deeply mine the time series features between landmarks, thereby significantly improving the accuracy of forged video detection. This method not only improves the accuracy of detection, but also provides new perspectives and solutions for the identification of deep fake videos.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Speed Prediction Based on RD-DW-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of future information leakage in traditional hybrid methods in wind speed prediction, a Rolling Decomposition data preprocessing method is proposed. By observing data characteristics, a fixed window length is determined, and the data within the window is subjected to real-time variational mode decomposition. The decomposition results are then input into the BiLSTM model for prediction. Additionally, a Dynamic Weighting method is introduced to assign different weights to the prediction results at different time points. Experimental results show that the RD-DW-BiLSTM model can effectively mitigate future information leakage while maintaining good predictive accuracy, enabling accurate wind speed predictions.

articleTitle: Classification of Glass Artifacts Using the Black Widow Optimized Backpropagation Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: By optimizing the selection of initial weights and bias parameters, as well as the Adam optimizer and network architectural parameters using BWOA, we addressed issues related to local optima and overfitting encountered in the BP optimization process. Subsequently, within the context of classifying ancient glass artifacts, we compared the performance of the BWOA-optimized BP neural network with that of the Genetic Algorithm (GA) BP neural network and the traditional BP neural network. Our results demonstrated that the BWOA-optimized BP neural network achieved an average prediction error of 14.6% on the test set. Notably, the BWOA-optimized BP achieved ideal adaptability in the second iteration, 83 generations earlier than the GA-BP. The average absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), mean square error (MSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of the BWO-BP on the test set were calculated to be 1.442, 1.977, 3.909, and 0.145, respectively, outperforming the other two algorithms. Overall, compared to the traditional BP neural network, the BWOA-BP neural network significantly improved prediction accuracy and had a higher convergence rate, thereby providing valuable insights for the optimization and enhancement of BP neural networks.

articleTitle: Aided Application of Neural Network-Fuzzy in Human Vision Refraction Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of auto-refractor technology, refraction services have become readily available in most optometry stores. While auto-refractors offer speed and convenience, the measurements they provide are subject to a notable margin of error influenced by psychological and physical factors. Consequently, repetitive testing is required to obtain more accurate mean error values. Therefore, it is crucial to explore research on measurement methods that can complement auto-refractor measurements and validate refraction results. This will help ensure more reliable and precise outcomes in the field of refraction. The Liou eye model is employed to simulate the human eye and facilitate the development of optometric techniques. In this study, CODE V optical design software was utilized to calculate the visual imaging generated by personalized, individual human eye models. Subsequently, an innovative algorithm combining fuzzy logic and backpropagation neural networks was proposed for category recognition. The experimental results using this new approach achieved a recognition accuracy rate exceeding 98%, thereby enhancing the precision of optometry and enabling dual confirmation through computer-aided optometry.

articleTitle: Attention-Based Adversarial Multi-Task Comment Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text classification and analysis play a crucial role in today's society, with multi-task learning emerging as a key research direction. In addressing the shortcomings of conventional multi-task text classification models, which struggle to extract text features effectively and often disregard the significance of input information. This paper introduces a novel method that combines attention mechanisms with adversarial multi-task learning for text classification. Focusing on text input, the attention mechanism aids in feature extraction by emphasizing important textual information. Through weighted calculations and appropriate representation, the attention mechanism improves subsequent learning tasks. Comparative analysis of four multi-task text classification models validates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model. The model's generalizability and accuracy in multi-task text classification are demonstrated, showcasing significant advancements over traditional models in text feature extraction and importance recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Vulnerability Assessment of Rainwater and Flood Disasters in Urban High speed Railway Stations Based on Machine Learning
