publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, extreme rainstorm weather has occurred frequently under the global climate change environment, and urban rainstorm flood disasters have shown a trend of increasing frequency and severity. Urban high-speed rail stations are closed and densely populated. Once a rainstorm flood occurs, it will be extremely dangerous. A large amount of rainwater pouring into the station in a short time will not only affect the travel of urban residents but also cause huge economic losses, and even threaten the life safety of urban residents. This study used a composite model constructed by entropy weight TOPSIS and neural network to evaluate the risk of rain and flood disasters at High-speed railway station. The entropy weight TOPSIS method was used to assess the vulnerability and risk exposure of high-speed railway stations to rain and flood disasters, and the neural network model was used to simulate and evaluate the disaster risk. Overall, Nanjing station belongs to level II. A comparison with metro station shows that there are the most metro stations with a vulnerability of Level II, accounting for more than one-third of the total, while metro stations with a vulnerability of Level III or above account for more than half of the total, and there are certain regional and line vulnerability differences.

articleTitle: Research on Optical Character Recognition for Nuclear Power Components in Underwater Environment Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Nuclear underwater fuel assembly OCR can recognize and interpret characters, signs and symbols in the underwater environment of high radiation and low visibility, which is of great significance to ensure the safe operation of nuclear power plants. Four batches of fuel assembly images in different nuclear power environments are collected. According to the character recognition requirements, a one-step character recognition method is proposed. The character detection model of the one-step character recognition method has a mAP50 of 0.963 on the test set, and there are many character misrecognition problems in the prediction results. The reason for character misidentification is that the ratio of the character area to the size of the captured image is less than 1:5000, so the character area target is too small. Aiming at the problem of one-step character recognition, this paper proposes a two-step character recognition method. The mAP50 of the character detection model of the two-step character recognition method can reach 0.994 on the test set. The two-step character recognition method can effectively solve the problem of one-step character recognition method, but there is a problem of misidentification of fuel assembly characters in other nuclear power plants in the prediction results. According to the problems existing in the two-step character recognition method, the paper puts forward the three-step character recognition method at last. The character classification model of the three-step character recognition method can reach top1_accuracy of 0.996 on the test set. Using the fifth batch of fuel assembly images in nuclear power environment to test the three-step character recognition method, the test results show that the three-step character recognition method can effectively suppress the problems existing in the one-step character recognition method and the two-step character recognition method, improve the generalization ability of fuel assembly character recognition, and have better field application value.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv8 Model for Drug Detection in Compound Robot System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The sudden emergence of the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) has had a catastrophic impact on global populations, with healthcare workers (HCWs) facing unprecedented challenges due to the high infection rate among this group. The deployment of composite robots, which combine the functions of fast movement and flexible grasping, can potentially address the shortage of HCWs and facilitate the delivery of essential medical supplies and other tasks in isolation environments. This paper presents a key technology for composite robots to perform the function of picking up and delivering medicines. The identification and detection of medicines is a crucial aspect of this technology. To enhance the accuracy and real-time performance of composite robots in detecting medicines, a target detection algorithm based on the improvement of YOLOv8 for medicines boxes is proposed. Firstly, a global attention mechanism (GAM) is incorporated into the backbone network to enhance the network's focus on crucial information through cross-latitude information interaction and to retain channel and spatial information to a greater extent, thereby improving the ability of the backbone network to extract features. Secondly, the weighted bidirectional feature pyramid network(BiFPN) is integrated into the neck network, which facilitates multi-scale feature fusion by assigning appropriate weights to each input feature and refining the feature fusion process. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an average detection accuracy (mAP) of 99.20%, a recall of 98.90%, and an F1 score of 99.05%, while maintaining a detection speed of 158.73 FPS. In comparison to YOLOv6, YOLOv8n, and YOLOv8s, the proposed model exhibits the highest accuracy index and satisfactory overall performance, aligning with the requirements of composite robots for rapid and precise identification of medicines. The model enables the composite robot to accurately detect and identify medicines in real time within an isolated ward environment.

articleTitle: A Method for Predicting the Gel Point of Mixed Crude Oil Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Accurately predicting the gel point of mixed crude oil is crucial for efficient pipeline transportation and blockage prevention. Traditional manual methods are inadequate for real-time monitoring. This study introduces an accurate prediction model for the gel point of mixed crude oil using a hybrid deep learning model that combines Graph Connection-Skip Neural Networks (GCSGCN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). Using physical properties data (gel point, viscosity, density) from an oil mixing station in China (2009-2023), the proposed model outperforms empirical formulas and machine learning models like XGBoost.

articleTitle: Convergence of Plug-and-Play ADMM with Adaptive Linear Symmetric Denoisers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Plug-and-Play alternating directions method of multipliers (PnP-ADMM) is an emerging paradigm for image reconstruction. It is obtained by replacing the proximal operator (associated with the regularizer) in ADMM with a powerful denoiser. Remarkably, it has exhibited great success in many imaging applications. Owing to its iterative manner, convergence analysis has been an active research topic. Recently, the convergence of PnP-ADMM with fixed linear symmetric denoisers has been proved. Notably, an adaptive denoiser generally achieves superior performance compared to its fixed version. Inspired by this observation, we extend the fixed linear symmetric denoisers to adaptive ones in this paper. Under a mild assumption, the convergence of PnP-ADMM with adaptive linear symmetric denoisers is proved for inpainting, deblurring, and superresolution. Experimental results on the above three tasks demonstrate our convergence theory. Meanwhile, PnP-ADMM with adaptive linear symmetric denoisers displays an enormous improvement over the one with the fixed version.

articleTitle: The Residential Rat Monitoring and Detection System based on Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the popularity of automatic monitoring systems in home environments, animal detection techniques based on computer vision have gradually become a research hotspot. In this article, a rat detection method based on the improved YOLOv5 algorithm is proposed, aiming to improve the detection accuracy of the model in complex environments, especially in low-light and occlusion situations. Firstly, to address the limitations of YOLOv5 in small object detection, this article employs data enhancement techniques and incorporates high-resolution image inputs to improve the detection of rat, a small target. Second, a post-processing method based on adaptive thresholding is proposed to reduce the false detection of low-confidence targets while enhancing the robustness of the model in complex backgrounds. In addition, the feature extraction capability of YOLOv5 is optimised by introducing a new attention mechanism model, which improves the accuracy of rats detection. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5 model exhibits higher accuracy and stronger robustness in the rats detection task, providing an effective solution for mouse monitoring in home environments.

articleTitle: Asphalt Pavement Crack Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the issues of low efficiency and high cost in asphalt pavement crack detection, a low-cost solution using smartphones is proposed. First, to improve the overall detection performance of the model, a FreqSpatialFusion module is designed and implemented to extract both spatial and frequency domain features from images. Additionally, the original module is replaced with a WIoUv3 loss function and a dual-channel Spatial Pyramid Pooling Faster Cross Stage Partial Channel (SPPFCSPC) layer to enhance the model's recognition ability. Secondly, to reduce model redundancy, a Layer Adaptive Magnitude Based Pruning (LAMP) technique is employed for channel pruning, thereby reducing the model's size and computational load. Finally, the improved model, YOLOv8n-Crack, is deployed on smartphones to enable low-cost crack detection. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves a 4.2% increase in mAP@50 on the self-built Crack-5514 dataset, while reducing the model size and computational load by 36% and 8.6%, respectively. This approach enables real-time crack detection, significantly improving efficiency and reducing costs.

articleTitle: Research on Wheat Ear Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Deep learning techniques are of significant importance in the detection of wheat ears in the field of smart agriculture, bringing innovation and improvement to the agricultural sector. How to accurately detect wheat ears has become a challenging task due to the high density, diversity, and complex growth cycle of wheat ears, as well as the complex background of the detection process, which may result in false positives, false negatives, and low detection rates. In this paper, a novel wheat spike detection technique is proposed, which is optimized on the basis of YOLOv8. First, RepNCSPELAN4 is introduced into the backbone network to replace the original C2F convolution, which enhances the feature extraction ability of the model. Second, a new MSAM module is introduced into the Bottleneck of the neck C2f module to construct a new C2fMSAM module; finally, the original loss function is replaced by the normalized Wasserstein distance loss. The experimental results show that the accuracy, recall and average accuracy of the improved YOLOv8 model are improved by 1.1%, 3.5% and 2%, respectively, compared with the baseline model.

articleTitle: An End-to-end Framework for Graph Clustering: Semantic Fusion of Graph Convolutional Network and Variational Auto-encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Attribute graph clustering is a fundamental and challenging task in graph data mining, requiring the adequate utilization of both node attributes and graph structure. Recently, a series of graph clustering methods have been proposed, integrating both graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and autoencoders to capture structural information and node attributes, respectively. However, most existing methods either employ a complicated summation mechanism in the unaligned representation space from GCN and auto-encoder, or select a certain module (e.g. results from GCN) as a biased target selftraining signal. To address this, we propose a new end-to-end graph clustering framework that integrates a GCN and a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a more efficient and reasonable fusion mechanism in the semantic level. To better supervise the clustering, we select a high-confidence set of nodes based on the consensus of two encoders, further boosting the performances. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, highlighting its efficacy in graph clustering.

articleTitle: Development Process of Django-based Database Management System for Small and Micro Project
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Based on Django, this paper designs and implements a database management system for small and micro projects of Shanghai Post and Telecommunication Design and Consulting Research Institute Co. Ltd, which mainly adopts Django framework for Web development. Requirements analysis of the database management system, followed by a description of the system design and specific system implementation. Finally, the realized database management system was tested and concluded that it meets the requirements. The thesis realizes a simple interface, perfect function of small and micro-projects database management system, administrators can according to the needs of data management, improve the security of small and micro-projects data, management simplicity.

articleTitle: PCASNet: Polarized Cross-scale Attention Self-attention Network for Lightweight Ultrasound Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: U-Net and its extensions have achieved significant success in medical image segmentation but face limitations in capturing global context and transferring cross-scale features. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight network, PCASNet, which integrates the Polarized Cross-scale Attention Module (PCAS Module) and the Dynamic Multi-scale Attention Gate (DMAG). The PCAS Module enhances global context modeling by fusing features from distant spatial positions, while the DMAG improves segmentation performance by filtering redundant features and emphasizing critical information, thereby strengthening global information modeling and feature selection capabilities. Experiments on breast and thyroid ultrasound datasets demonstrate that PCASNet outperforms traditional image segmentation algorithms in both accuracy and efficiency, highlighting its potential for applications in ultrasound medical imaging.

articleTitle: Real-time Open-vocabulary Sentence Decoding from MEG Signals Using Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) hold immense potential for restoring communication to individuals with severe speech impairments. This paper investigates the feasibility of real-time open-vocabulary sentence decoding from magnetoencephalography (MEG) signals using deep learning with a Transformer architecture. We propose a novel end-to-end model that leverages the high temporal and spatial resolution of MEG and the powerful sequence-to-sequence learning capabilities of Transformers. Our model is trained and evaluated on a large dataset of MEG recordings paired with natural language sentences. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving real-time, accurate, and flexible communication, significantly outperforming existing methods. Our findings pave the way for the development of more practical and user-friendly BCIs for individuals with speech disabilities.

articleTitle: Utilizing Quantum Variational Circuits to Perform Quantum Convolutions in Hybrid "Quanvolutional" Neural Networks for Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. Mutations in humans can alter oncogenes or tumor suppressor genes, leading to uncontrolled cell growth. The most common form of cancer is skin cancer which if caught early, is much easier to treat, highlighting the importance of a sophisticated skin cancer detection system. In this study, we propose a novel method to detect skin cancer early, utilizing quantum variational circuits to perform a quantum convolution as a pre-processing step on image data for classical Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to create a hybrid "Quanvolutional" Neural Network. Utilizing a dataset of over 8,100 images which included images of other skin conditions including Herpes Simplex, Burns, Xerosis, folliculitis, and more, our model obtained a validation accuracy of 99.30% for the classification of Skin Cancer. This performance surpasses that of similar, purely classical CNNs, despite the presence of noise from other skin conditions. Our study not only demonstrates significant potential for skin cancer detection, but also the efficiency and effectiveness of quantum pre-processing layers in hybrid Quanvolutional Neural Networks. Future work can utilize our Quantum Machine Learning methods, leading to further breakthroughs within the medical field and quantum computing as a whole.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstruction of Large-scale Head Surface with a Binocular Camera in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In image-guided TMS navigation, markerless registration methods use the head surface to match the tracking system space with the image space. Large-scale head surface is beneficial for improving registration accuracy. Currently, most 3D cameras have a limited view field and cannot reconstruct large-scale head surface with a single shot. Extra tracking devices are needed to stitch several single-shot 3D surfaces into a large-scale one. To simplify the above point cloud stitching process, an automatic 3D reconstruction method for awake TMS patients is proposed to obtain head surfaces without extra tracking devices. Experimental results show the accuracy of the reconstruction can reach 1.39 mm and registration is quicker and simpler in repeated TMS treatment sessions.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings Based on CNN-BiLSTM-SE Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study proposes a rolling bearing fault diagnosis model called CNN-BiLSTM-SE, which integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks (BiLSTM), and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism. The method is validated using the CWRU dataset. Experimental results show that CNN-BiLSTM-SE model achieves a recognition accuracy of 100% for fault recognition, with a recognition accuracy of 96% for different fault types. The results demonstrate that this approach possesses strong capabilities in rolling bearing fault diagnosis and holds significant application value in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Role-Wise Spatially-Aware Joint Information Extraction with Vocabulary Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Information extraction is the process of transforming unstructured text into structured information. We have observed that entities, events, and relationships within a sentence can be effectively decoded using only the starting and ending pointers. Therefore, we introduce a novel paradigm that treats information extraction as a unified task: span extraction, where relationships are identified by the starting position of one span and the ending position of another. Based on this, we propose one pointer for joint information extraction, which models all tasks using only the head-to-tail pointer. Additionally, we incorporate vocabulary expansion to address the class imbalance problem in the training set, and implicitly models multiple tasks by introducing role-wise spatially-aware subspaces. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms both task-specific and previous unified models, confirming the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: MRZegCLIP: Combine Multi-Scaled Region with ZegCLIP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the remarkable zero-shot learning capabilities demonstrated by large vision and multimodal models, applying such models to zero-shot segmentation has become a mainstream research focus in this field. Among these methods, the ZegCLIP model enhances CLIP's image-level zero-shot classification capability by integrating visual prompts, relationship description modules, and a segmentation decoder, enabling pixel-level zero-shot segmentation with notable performance. However, although ZegCLIP achieves pixel-level segmentation, its decoder operates at the block level and relies on upsampling to produce pixel-level outputs from these block-based predictions. We propose that enhancing ZegCLIP's block-level classification capability through the use of multi-scale image blocks for training visual prompts and the segmentation decoder can provide richer visual information, thereby improving zero-shot segmentation performance. In this work, we introduce a method that selects multi-scale blocks from the input image to train both the visual prompts and segmentation decoder. Given that the introduction of multi-scale block cropping significantly reduces training efficiency, this paper employs a region proposal network to select blocks with greater training value, thereby significantly accelerating the training process. Experiments on the PASVOC 2012 Aug dataset show a 2.95% mIoU improvement, demonstrating that incorporating multi-scale image blocks enhances ZegCLIP's zero-shot segmentation capabilities.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Pure-Electric Vehicle Retention Rate Based on TabTransformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As China's NEV industry develops on a large scale with accelerated vehicle replacement, the speed of vehicle replacement has significantly accelerated, strongly promoting the development of the new energy second-hand vehicle market. This research targets low retention rates and hard valuation of pure electric vehicles. It proposes an evaluation method for pure electric vehicle retention rate using a deep learning model via variable screening, model construction (based on TabTransformer), and model performance evaluation. The research content and algorithm aim to be an important reference for entities like second-hand vehicle dealers, financial and insurance institutions, and consumers for evaluating pure electric vehicle retention rates.

articleTitle: An Improved Swin Transformer-based Model for Fine-grained Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Fine-grained classification is a challenging task. Different from traditional classification, there frequently arises the issue of significant intra-class variation and minor inter-class variation in fine-grained classification, which poses great difficulties for classification. Recently, the attention-based Swin Transformer has surpassed traditional CNN models in various visual tasks. It can effectively capture global features and achieve better classification performance. In contrast, convolutional neural networks are adept at extracting local features. However, fine-grained classification tasks rely more on local features. Therefore, this paper attempts to further improve the features extracted by the Swin Transformer and subsequently fuse them with the low-level features extracted by CNN, thereby forming a feature representation more suitable for fine-grained classification. Eventually, competitive results have been obtained on common fine-grained classification datasets.

articleTitle: An OpenMV-Based Intelligent Manipulator For Pill Sorting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In this study, an intelligent pill sorting machine based on OpenMV and Manipulator is designed to solve the problems of inefficiency and manual errors in traditional pill sorting. The system is able to accurately sort pills through real-time colour recognition by OpenMV, and automate the gripping and encapsulation operations by a six-degree-of-freedom Manipulator controlled by STM32. The system combines computer vision and servo control to achieve efficient sorting of different coloured pills, improving the accuracy and efficiency of drug management. Experimental results show that the machine has significant advantages in sorting efficiency and accuracy, has a wide range of application prospects, and provides an innovative solution for the medical automation field.

articleTitle: VM-UNet++: Advanced Nested Vision Mamba UNet for Precise Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the realm of medical image segmentation, the U-shaped structure comprising an encoder and a decoder has been demonstrated to be an extremely effective approach. They can be classified into models based on convolutional neural network (CNN), such as U-Net, and models based on Transformer, like Swin-UNet. Nevertheless, methods based on CNN are naturally constrained by the receptive field and have limitations in their capabilities. Although methods based on Transformer can capture global information, their computational complexity is extremely high and demands sufficient computing power support. Recently, state space model (SSM) exemplified by Mamba have emerged as a promising solution. They exhibit excellent performance in modeling long-range interactions, and maintain linear computational complexity, as well. Consequently, numerous works have employed Mamba to address computer vision tasks and achieved remarkable results. Among these, researchers combined U-Net with Vision Mamba (Vim) and proposed Vision Mamba U-Net (VM-UNet) to tackle the problem of medical image segmentation. Building on VM-UNet, we referred to the design concepts of UNet++ and implemented Vision Mamba UNet++ (VM-UNet++). Moreover, we conducted experiments on two public datasets, the ISIC17 and ISIC18 datasets, and the results indicated that our method shows a significant improvement over VM-UNet in medical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Integration of Deep Learning and Time Series Decomposition for Enhanced Short-Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study aims to improve the accuracy of short-term power load forecasting through deep learning to ensure the dynamic balance and stable operation of the power grid system. In response to the poor prediction accuracy of traditional serial combination models and the issue of data leakage in modal decomposition prediction models, this paper proposes a parallel combination model based on deep learning. The model integrates a self-developed time series decomposition (TD) module, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA). First, the time series decomposition module decomposes power load data into trend and periodic components to extract long-term and short-term features. These features are then fed into parallel BiGRU and TCN deep networks for processing. The multi-head self-attention mechanism is incorporated to further enhance the model’s expressive capabilities. Additionally, the model leverages the Beluga Whale Optimization (BWO) algorithm to optimize hyperparameters, fully exploiting the complex correlations within the data. Experimental results show that the proposed BWO-TD-BiGRU-TCN-MHSA deep learning model significantly outperforms baseline models in terms of MAPE, RMSE, MAE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This verifies the model's high accuracy and practicality in power load forecasting, providing reliable support for the planning and stable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Anmaly Detection Technology in Educational Big Data Based on Deep Neural Networks and Classroom Management Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the context of educational informatization, the rapid growth of educational big data has provided new data support for classroom management and educational decision-making. However, anomaly detection in this data still faces both technical and theoretical challenges. This paper explores the anomaly detection methods in educational big data based on deep neural networks from a theoretical perspective, analyzing the characteristics of educational data and the difficulties associated with detecting anomalies. By combining traditional anomaly detection models with deep learning methods, this paper outlines the theoretical advantages of deep neural networks in anomaly detection and discusses their potential applications in educational management. Finally, the paper proposes theoretical directions for further optimizing deep neural network models in the education sector, offering support for classroom management and educational optimization.

articleTitle: Feature Fusion Dehazing Network Based on Parallel Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Images captured in haze-affected weather frequently exhibit many issues, including the degradation of image features, distortion of colour, and the loss of local detail. Previous deep learning based image dehazing models have shown unsatisfactory performance on real-world non-uniform haze datasets. Most existing models are unable to combine features of different scales, resulting in poor performance on real datasets. In this paper, we proposed a parallel attention-based feature fusion dehazing network. We designed a multi-scale feature fusion module and a parallel attention module to improve the ability to handle haze of different concentrations and thicknesses. A comparison of the dehazing experiments conducted on different models with synthetic haze images and real haze images reveals that our model is more effective in handling haze of varying densities and thicknesses while retaining greater detail in the images.

articleTitle: Review on the Development of Image Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Image transfer has been a significant question in the field of computer vision. This passage aims to have a review on the most important algorithms through the development on image transfer. The passage mainly talks about the some representative algorithms based on conventional image transfer algorithms, CNN, GAN and Diffusion and compared the advantages and disadvantages of them in the end of the article as well as proposes some problems and research directions for the current development of image transfer.

articleTitle: Urban Waterlogging Disaster Level Assessment Method Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, extreme weather incidents such as heavy rainfall and frequent typhoons have led to the intensification of urban waterlogging disasters, which has constituted a major challenge to urban safety. In order to cope with this challenge, accurate and efficient disaster assessment and early warning technology have become particularly important, and it can provide solid support for disaster prevention and mitigation in cities. Therefore, this article uses the advanced framework of YOLOV8-SEG to develop a set of urban waterlogging disaster evaluation systems. The system uses accurate instance division technology to quickly identify and extract key elements in the affected area, including the scope of water, affected people, and important infrastructure. In addition, this article uses YSPOSE human posture analysis to achieve a quantitative assessment of disaster levels by capturing key points of the skeleton, providing a scientific basis for disaster warning, emergency response and post -disaster reconstruction.

articleTitle: RsCU-Net: Multi-scale Features Based U-Net for Skin Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the diversity, blurred edges and hair noise in skin lesion areas, a multi-scale feature network (RsCU-Net) with U-Net as the baseline model was proposed. Firstly, the CA module is introduced to enhance the network's spatial awareness. Secondly, the RS module is incorporated to extract multi-scale features and adaptively adjust the weights of each feature channel. Finally, the fusion of BCE loss function and Dice loss function addresses the issues of class imbalance in skin lesion image samples and enhances difficult sample mining. We validated our proposed network on the ISIC2018 dataset. Compared with the baseline U-Net, RsCU-Net demonstrated respective improvements of 3.42%, 2.14%, and 4.92% in MIoU, Dice score, and Precision metrics. Additionally, it achieved reductions of 0.175 in HD95 and 0.1126 in RVD.

articleTitle: AMCU-Net: Adaptive Multi-Scale ConvMixer U-Net for Breast Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common malignant tumor affecting women globally, with early detection crucial to improving patient outcomes. Traditional segmentation methods, while proficient in global feature extraction, often fail to capture fine-grained local features across varying scales, resulting in missed detections and inaccurate segmentation of small lesions. To tackle these challenges, a network architecture, AMCU-Net, is proposed, which is designed to enhance segmentation accuracy for lesions of diverse scales and shapes. AMCU-Net adopts a multi-module structure to improve sensitivity to lesions at different scales, thereby enhancing small-lesion capture and optimizing segmentation across multiple resolutions. Furthermore, AMCU-Net integrates Convolutional Block Attention Module and Multi-Scale Attention Gate, dynamically focusing on essential spatial and channel features to bolster feature extraction and ensure effective small-lesion delineation. This approach enables precise boundary segmentation and high accuracy under various resolutions. Additionally, the ConvMixer module is employed to effectively merge multi-scale features through mixed convolution operations, boosting the model's capability to accurately segment complex heterogeneous lesions and adapt to images of different sizes. Experimental results demonstrate that AMCU-Net excels in multi-scale segmentation tasks, significantly advancing small-lesion delineation and overall segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Metabolite-disease Associations Prediction Based on Multi-kernel Learning and Graph Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A growing number of scholars have confirmed through research that there is a strong correlation between changes in metabolite levels in the human body and various complex diseases. In this study, we propose a new framework (MKLGAT-MDA) that integrates multi-kernel learning and graph attention network (GAT) for enhanced metabolite-disease associations prediction. First, the study employs multi-kernel learning to combine different similarity matrices to capture feature information from different perspectives of metabolites and diseases. Then a GAT network with a path-learning graph space operator is employed to generate meaningful spatial convolutions from the paths in GAT to improve the prediction performance. The average AUC at 5-cv is 0.9562 and the average AUPR is 0.9575. The experimental findings indicate that our model surpasses current methods regarding prediction accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Recognition of Marine Products Based on SA-YOLOv10
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Current object detection technology still faces several challenges, including low image clarity, complex backgrounds, and blurred targets when identifying marine products. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an enhanced object detection model based on YOLOv10, named SA-YOLOv10. Firstly, the downsampling method is optimized by replacing SCDown with ADown, which not only reduces model size but also improves object detection accuracy. Secondly, a sliding window mechanism is introduced to restrict attention computation within a window while allowing the model to learn across-window information, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, through a hierarchical design of downsampling layers, the model is capable of focusing on both global and local information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 83.6% precision, 78.4% recall, and 85.6% mAP@0.5 in real marine life recognition. Compared to YOLOv10n, these results show improvements of 1.5%, 1.8%, and 1.7%, respectively, with only a 0.3 ms increase in inference time. This indicates that, with a minimal increase in inference time compared to YOLOv10n, the model achieves a substantial improvement in accuracy.

articleTitle: A High Fidelity Optical Remote Sensing Image Compression Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the defects of existing remote sensing image compression methods, this paper proposes a high-fidelity optical remote sensing image compression method. Firstly, through preprocessing, the grayscale distribution characteristics of the image are changed, and then the compression method based on JPEG2000 is used to realize efficient image compression processing. By comparing with the traditional compression method, the proposed method has better compression performance, the PSNR is comparable to JPEG-LS and higher than JPEG2000 by at least 0.5dB under low compression ratio, and the PSNR is comparable to JPEG2000 and higher than JPEG-LS by at least 4dB under high compression ratio, which is especially suitable for the compression processing of optical remote sensing images with low grayscale and narrow dynamic range.

articleTitle: A Road Surface Disease Identification Model Based on Visual Semantic Segmentation and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of small sample road pavement distress recognition, the article proposes a road pavement distress recognition model based on visual semantic segmentation and conditional generative adversarial network. An adaptive histogram equalisation method with restricted contrast is used to enhance the high-precision pavement image. Multi-channel feature map extraction, response map computation and feature fusion are performed on the enhanced image to obtain the pavement disease salient map. A visual semantic segmentation framework fusing hybrid dilated convolution and channel attention network is established to segment the salient map. Based on the conditional generative adversarial network, a disease recognition model is established to complete the disease type recognition. The experimental results show that the F1 value of the proposed model for road pavement disease recognition results remains above 0.95, which improves the accuracy of pavement disease detection.

articleTitle: Cross-modal Frequency-aware Transformer for Multimodal Medical Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Fusing multimodal medical images seeks to amalgamate their unique informational strengths, thereby enhancing the precision of clinical diagnostics and the accuracy of surgical navigation. The resulting image quality in multimodal fusion is contingent upon the characteristics derived from individual modalities and the strategies employed for integrating this diverse data. Nevertheless, current deep learning-driven fusion techniques, although adept at harnessing the semantic aspects of each imaging mode, struggle to differentiate between the beneficial low-frequency and high-frequency details within each modality. This limitation hinders their ability to capture comprehensive global insights and to achieve dynamic, context-aware fusion. To address these issues, we introduce an innovative fusion framework that utilizes Fourier transforms and incorporates a cross-modal frequency-aware transformer. This framework includes a frequency-aware cross-attention mechanism for adaptive feature fusion across modalities by exchanging keys and queries between spatial and frequency domains. It also computes cross-attention scores to facilitate the integration of spatial and frequency data. Additionally, we employ a hybrid approach of gradient preservation and transformers for feature extraction, capturing both local specifics and global information. Our model surpasses existing methods assessments, markedly improving fused image quality.

articleTitle: Study on YOLOv5 Algorithm for Fruit Sorting and Discriminating in Complex Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: It is of great significance to realize the classification and discriminant detection of fruit in the assembly line under complex environments, change the current situation of high cost, long time and uneven sorting of fruit manually, and improve the efficiency and accuracy of fruit detection. This study designed a discriminating system based on YOLOv5 that can automatically, efficiently and accurately sort fruits in complex scenarios with different light, partial overlap, multiple fruit still photos and video shooting situations. Raspberry PI 5 was equipped with YOLOv5 as the visual recognition part, and STM32f407 development board was used as the control system for pipeline sorting part. Receiving and processing the recognized data to control the stepper motor, digital steering gear, coding motor for sorting operation, not only has the function of recognizing the type and shape of fruit, but also can efficiently distinguish the superior and inferior fruits and classify them. With the position sensor, the sorting pick for different kinds of fruit sorting accuracy of more than 98.9%, because the system implementation method is relatively simple, greatly improve the sorting efficiency of fruit production line and fruit quality after sorting, reduce labor costs, promote the development of fruit industry, has a good market application prospects.

articleTitle: Computing Power Network Resources Prediction Based on GRU-FFT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Predicting computing resources can provide scientific basis for the precise allocation of resources and real-time scheduling of computing tasks, thereby optimizing resource allocation and system performance. This paper proposes a model of Computing Power Network resource prediction based on Gated Recurrent Unit and Fast Fourier Transform to address the heterogeneous ubiquity and dynamic time-varying characteristics of computing power resource data. The model analyzes the time-domain and frequency-domain features of computing power data to predict computing power resources. GRU is responsible for capturing the characteristics of data in the time domain, and then converting the time domain data into the frequency domain through FFT to extract the features of the data in the frequency domain. Based on the Alibaba open-source dataset, experimental analysis was conducted, and the results showed that the proposed computing power resource prediction method reduced the Mean Absolute Error by 49.44%, 53.79%, and 72.11%, compared to GRU, LSTM, and RNN models respectively; the Mean Squared Error decreased by 52.87%, 61.13%, and 74.37%, respectively. the Root Mean Squared Error reduced by 31.35%, 37.66%, and 49.38%, respectively.

articleTitle: Implementation of 2D-to-3D Prediction Network for Point Cloud Clothing Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The virtual try-on of garment requires to capture the outfit of the three-dimensional human body with the true measurement. Point-based modeling can estimate the geometry of diverse clothing outfits in point clouds with the modelingof human body shapes. In this paper, a 2D-to-3Dhuman pose prediction network is used to estimate 3D human shapes. To account for the absence of scale parameters, a scale optimization module is introduced to regress the scale value using the vertices generated by I2L-MeshNet and point-based modeling. Additionally, a pelvis center alignment step is incorporated to ensure the human body is accurately aligned with the center of the image. A dataset with human models in T-pose and random pose are collected for evaluation. The appearance reconstructionresults are then compared with manually cropped images and auto-center positioning images using YOLOv8. Measurement metrics such as Intersection over Union and ratio of overlap are used to identify the effectiveness of three different clothing alignment techniques. This paper demonstrates the proposed pipeline can accurately aligns the outfit to the target human body and deliver the best appearance reconstruction result.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Solve the Shrinkage Problem of Targets in Infrared Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Infrared small target detection methods based on the local contrast have attracted much attention. For some larger targets with clearer outlines, along the direction of the target center pixel to the edge pixel, the contrast calculated using the sliding window will gradually decrease to a value that tends to zero, resulting in a shrinkage of the target in the final saliency map, which fails to achieve the expected detection effect. For this reason, this paper proposes a novel method based on local contrast to solve it. First, a strategy to suppress the background based on multi-directional gray-scale jumps is proposed after analyzing the gradient characteristics of the target and the edge clutter. A method is designed to generate a zero region of the target, which can make the pixel value of the neighborhood background of the target in the image where the background is suppressed to zero. Then the contrast is calculated in the zero region using the nested protection window mechanism, which can expand the area of the real target. Finally, the target is re-extracted from the enlarged target area by using the perceptual prior obtained by the mean filter. Extensive experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper has high detection performance.

articleTitle: Chaotic Image Encryption Algorithm Based on 2DLSCS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents a digital picture encryption technique that utilizes a two-dimensional Logistic-Sine Improved Chaotic System (2DLSCS). Initially, channel separation is executed for color images. Furthermore, the newly proposed enhanced chaotic system, in conjunction with an initial key, is utilized to construct distinct disruption and diffusion sequences for each channel. Next, the image is encrypted by utilizing the chaotic sequences that were formed, resulting in a cipher image for each channel. Ultimately, the cipher images from the three channels are merged to acquire the ultimate cipher image. The technique employed in this work demonstrates excellent performance in several tests, including histogram analysis, picture correlation assessment, key sensitivity evaluation, UACI and NPCR analysis, and information entropy measurement. Hence, the encryption technique is capable of withstanding numerous common attacks, thereby enhancing the security of the image.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Multiple Models for Lung Cancer Detection in Chest CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Lung cancer is among the most prevalent malignant tumors affecting the lungs. Traditional methods of medical imaging diagnosis heavily rely on the expertise and judgment of radiologists, thereby introducing elements of subjectivity and significant time expenditure. This study aims to compare the efficacy of various deep learning models in lung cancer CT image analysis, specifically focusing on the MedMamba model, several conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, and Transformer models. Through rigorous experimentation and comparative analysis, this paper elucidates the strengths and limitations of these models and, for the first time, provides an in-depth exploration of the Mamba model’s application potential in lung cancer CT image recognition and diagnosis without necessitating pre-training on extensive datasets. The experimental outcomes indicate that the MedMamba model achieves remarkable accuracy and low computational complexity even in a non-pretrained state, whereas pre-training markedly enhances the performance of all models. This investigation not only aims to optimize existing models but also seeks to explore the future potential of the Mamba model, thereby contributing to advancements in lung CT image classification and enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of early lung cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Fixation Guided Integrity Enhancement Network for Salient Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Although significant progress has been made in current salient object detection (SOD), the issue of integrity overflow in complex scene detection remains to be solved. The saliency map can accurately locate salient regions. Therefore, we propose the fixation guided integrity enhancement network (FGIEN). We utilize the fixation guidance module and the integrity enhancement module to achieve accurate localization and salient object integrity learning. The proposed method (FGIEN-F) exhibits better performance on five benchmark datasets. In addition, on the DUTS-F dataset, the proposed method fusing fixation information shows significant improvement in all metrics, with the MAE decreased by 0.015, S-measure, E-measure, and Weighted F-measure increasing by 3.02%, 3.88%, and 6.76%, respectively. This paper verifies the feasibility and superiority of fusing fixation.

articleTitle: Automated Defect Detection in Cigarette Manufacturing Using Improved YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cigarette defect detection is a critical process in tobacco manufacturing to ensure product quality and reduce defect rates. This paper presents a comprehensive study on automated defect detection for two popular cigarette brands: Furongwang and Changbaishan. The dataset used in this study contains six common defect types, including puncture, foam inclusion, wrinkle, misalignment, open end, and powder attachment. To address these challenges, we propose a deep learning-based approach utilizing the YOLOv8 object detection model, which is specifically fine-tuned to automatically identify these defects with high precision and efficiency. The YOLOv8 model, equipped with advanced feature extraction capabilities, has shown remarkable performance in accurately detecting multiple defect types in real-time production environments. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a detection accuracy of over 98%, showcasing strong generalization performance across various defect types. This study highlights the practical value of using advanced AI solutions to enhance quality assurance in cigarette manufacturing, ultimately reducing labor costs and minimizing human error.

articleTitle: Research on Image Segmentation Based on Deep Learning Algorithm using Fusion Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Skin lesion segmentation is a prerequisite for the intelligent and automated development of skin disease diagnosis, and its segmentation effect directly affects the quality of subsequent skin disease identification. Therefore, achieving accurate segmentation of skin lesion areas is of great significance to the intelligent diagnosis of skin diseases. In view of the problems of different sizes of lesion areas, low contrast with surrounding skin, and blurred edges, this paper proposes a skin lesion segmentation method that integrates attention mechanism. This method consists of ParNet block (PNA) and FaPN segmentation network. The PNA module is placed after each convolution layer in the FaPN network, which can not only enhance the model feature extraction ability, but also alleviate the loss of detail information caused by continuous convolution, which is very helpful for accurate lesion segmentation. To verify the performance of the improved model AFaPN, this paper compares it with other advanced models on the public dataset ISIC2016. The results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper is better than other popular algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Localization and Attention Mechanism for Fine-Grained Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Fine-grained image classification tasks present a notable challenge, images within the same class can exhibit substantial intra-class variation, while the differences between distinct classes are often minimal. As a result, identifying the key distinguishing features in the images is essential for tackling this issue. This paper introduces an Attention Object Localization Module (AOLM) that predicts object locations, combined with a Weakly Supervised Part Localization Module (WPLM) to identify informative parts of the image. Additionally, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is applied to highlight important features and suppress less relevant ones. To enhance the model's classification accuracy, a multi-class ResNet backbone is used. Evaluations on three well-known benchmark datasets—CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and FGVC-Aircraft—resulted in accuracies of 90.5%, 95.0%, and 95.0%, respectively, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed method in fine-grained image classification.

articleTitle: Low Power Image Display Technology Based on Adaptive Histogram Correction and Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Most of the battery power in portable consumer electronics is consumed by AMOLED display panels, making these products need to be charged frequently, which reduces the user experience. Therefore, an adaptive low power scheme is preposed. Firstly, the histogram correction factor is generated adaptively according to the overall brightness of the image, and then the low power processing is realized by the combination of histogram correction and matching. Due to the larger power reduction space of the brighter image, a histogram correction factor is generated adaptively according to the brightness characteristics of the input image, so that the histogram of the brighter image can be corrected significantly. In addition, in the process of correction, the low-segment histogram is kept unchanged, and only the high-segment histogram is corrected, so that the corrected histogram can take into account both the power reduction and the visual effect preservation. The experimental results show that this method can improve the comprehensive power reduction index by 16.58%, indicating that this method can reduce the display power while maintaining the visual effect.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Detection of Key Components of Transmission Lines Based on the Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The detection of key components in transmission lines faces challenges such as significant variations in object scales, complex backgrounds, and difficulties in detecting small targets, leading to low detection accuracy and missed detections. In this study, we propose an improved YOLOv8 algorithm for detecting key components of transmission lines. First, we incorporate Deformable Convolution (DCNv3) to improve the backbone network's feature extraction capability and mitigate accuracy degradation caused by occlusion and angle variations. Subsequently, we use the Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) to progressively fuse features of different scales and add same-layer skip connections, enabling efficient feature fusion and strengthening the model's ability to detect small objects. Finally, we replaced the original CIoU with the RIoU to further boost the detection capability for small objects. The modified algorithm achieves an mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> of 96.5%, an mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50:95</inf> of 79.2%, representing a 3.1% and 4.8% improvement compared to the original YOLOv8 model.

articleTitle: Automated Deep Learning Framework for Retinal Disease Classification from OCT Images: A Large-Scale Study Across Four Categories
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: OCT imaging, which produces high-resolution cross-sectional images of the retina that are vital for identifying a variety of retinal illnesses, has emerged as a critical diagnostic technique in ophthalmology in recent years. However, it takes a lot of effort and specialized knowledge to analyze OCT pictures manually, hence automated techniques are needed to help doctors. This work introduces a deep learning-based framework that uses a sizable dataset of 84,495 retinal OCT pictures to automatically classify the images into four different illness categories. Our model provides a highly accurate, effective approach for automated diagnosis by utilizing convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures to efficiently capture the complex characteristics present in OCT pictures. High classification accuracy is attained by the suggested approach, indicating its resilience and ability to expedite the diagnostic procedure.

articleTitle: Small Target Detection in UAV Aerial Images Based on Sliding Window and Improved Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Target detection in drone aerial images is widely used in agriculture, urban management, military defense and other fields. Aerial images have problems such as small targets, dense targets and complex backgrounds, which bring difficulties and challenges to target detection. This paper uses YOLOv8n as the benchmark model to realize target detection in drone aerial images. First, each image is divided into multiple overlapping small areas through a sliding window, and the labels are regenerated, all areas are trained and predicted, and finally the prediction results are restored to the original image; secondly, a lightweight attention module (CBAM) and a bidirectional feature pyramid network (BiFPN) are added to YOLOv8. CBAM introduces channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms, which can enhance the model's attention to important features. BiFPN introduces bidirectional connections and weighted feature fusion, which can better utilize the features of multi-scale targets at different levels. Experimental results show that on the DOTA2.0 dataset, the improved algorithm with CBAM and BiFPN improves the mean average accuracy (mAP) by 1.1% compared with Yolov8n; after the sliding window is introduced, the mAP is increased by another 0.3%.

articleTitle: Interim Connection Space Based on Polynomial Models for Multispectral Image Compression and Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of multispectral image reconstruction, this paper proposes an interim connection space called PMLabPQR, which is an improvement of LabPQR. The first three dimensions of this space are the three-dimensional chromaticity information of a given spectrum S in a specified light environment. Compared with LabPQR, which uses the "R matrix" as the mapping matrix for converting the triple-stimulus values to the estimated spectra, PMLabPQR establishes the mapping relationship between the triple-stimulus values of CIEXYZ and the original spectra through polynomial regression, and then obtains the coefficients of the polynomial model by the least-squares method to obtain the coefficients of the polynomial model. The coefficient matrix of the polynomial model was obtained by the least-squares method as the mapping matrix, and the error between the estimated spectra and the original spectra obtained from the mapping matrix was analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA) to obtain the first three principal components as the last three dimensions of interim connection space. The reconstructed spectra are composed of the estimated spectra from the mapping matrix and the polynomial model consisting of the three stimulus values, and the spectral errors obtained by doing the inverse PCA variations. The experimental statistical results show that the new method is significantly better than LabPQR, MlabPQR, and tD65A in spectral reconstruction accuracy, and slightly lower than tD65A in chromaticity reconstruction accuracy, but with reduced additional information. Therefore the new method can be better applied to the compression and reconstruction of multispectral images.

articleTitle: Compact Neural Field Representation via Multi-scale Tensor Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: We propose a novel approach that leverages the principles of tensor decomposition to improve parameter efficiency in neural field representation. Previous grid-based methods typically densely distribute learnable features across grid points to represent underlying images or 3D shapes. While achieving promising results, most grids are redundant due to not fully leveraging the low-rank properties of underlying signals. To tackle this issue, we introduce multi-scale tensor decomposition to transform the high-dimensional spatial signal into a composition of multiple low-dimensional vectors. We observe that signals may contain varying levels of information at different scales, prompting us to adjust the rank of tensor decomposition accordingly for each scale. Subsequently, the queried feature undergoes further processing with multi-frequency sinusoid functions to distinguish signals at different frequencies. Our representation achieves state-of-the-art results in the final reconstruction quality while notably reducing the number of parameters. We will open-source the code after the paper is accepted.

articleTitle: A Multi-Modal Image Matching Approach Based on Nonlinear Anisotropic Filtering and GMS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Nonlinear Radiometric Distortions (NRD) between images from different sensors will lead to image matching difficulties. The KAZE algorithm is a robust method to NRD effect between multi-modal images, but the matching quality is sensitive to the parameter settings. To solve this problem, a novel feature matching algorithm that is robust to parameter settings is proposed in this work. A novel conduction function based on the KAZE algorithm is utilized, enabling better preservation of edge information during the filtering process. Additionally, the integration of an enhanced GLOH descriptor improves the computational efficiency of the proposed method. In the matching stage, the RANSAC algorithm is applied alongside GMS motion smoothing constraints to effectively eliminate mismatched points. Different experiments with three groups of satellite images are conducted to verified the effective of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Optimized Multi-Feature Fusion Model for Video Homologous Inter-Frame Tampering Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Homologous inter-frame tampering forensic methods relying on a single feature has a large number of omissions and false detections for tampered videos where there are sharp movements and complex light changes. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a video inter-frame tampering detection method based on the genetic algorithm-optimized multi-feature fusion model. Firstly, using the video inter-frame continuity, the video grayscale correlation, gradient correlation, and information fidelity correlation are extracted to construct a multi-feature fusion model; then based on the genetic algorithm to optimize the model weight parameter, the change degree of the fused features is calculated as a judgment data point; finally, the change degree anomaly is judged by using Chebyshev's inequality. The experimental results show that this paper's method can effectively improve the detection effect under videos with sharp motion and complicated light changes, etc. Under VIFFD and KTH datasets, the average accuracy rate (precision/%) for the three types of tampering methods is 93.06, 93.61, 91.39, respectively, and the average recall rate (recall/%) is 93.84, 93.445, 92.42, respectively, 92.42. The method in this paper can be better applied in the detection of tampering between frames of the same source of Internet video.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Image Super-Resolution Based on Domain Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: For now, most Single Image Super-Resolution(SISR) tasks are based on fully supervised image pairs of high and low pairs (obtained from fixed downsampling on high-resolution images). However, the fixed degradation process can not simulate the real image degradation well, making the model ineffective in reconstructing real images. In this paper, a semi-supervised reconstruction network based on domain transformation is proposed, the network consists of a domain transformation network and a reconstruction network, the real low-resolution image first passes through the domain transformation network for domain distribution adjustment, and then the reconstruction network generates the matching high-resolution image. In the network, we introduce an attention module, use perceptual loss, and use a 1*1 parallel convolution in the reconstruction part to increase the network nonlinearity, which in turn improves the image reconstruction quality. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on single real image reconstruction both qualitatively and quantitatively.

articleTitle: Comparative Research of Two Target Location Methods Based on Unmanned Remote Sensing Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to explore the use of unmanned remote sensing platform to accurately locate the target on sea surface, this paper compares the target location methods of coordinate transformation and collinear equation. Firstly, we determined the coordinate transformation relationship in the process of target positioning, and derived the target positioning model, and then analyzed the influence of each parameter in the process of target positioning on the final positioning results by simulation. Finally, we validated the feasibility of the algorithms by flight experiments. The results show that the collinear equation method has higher positioning accuracy than the coordinate transformation method.

articleTitle: Co-attention-based Multi-modal Feature Alignment for Cancer Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cancer incidence and mortality rates are increasing rapidly, making accurate survival prediction for cancer patients is a critical issue in cancer research. With advancements in digital pathology and genome sequencing technologies, the integration of pathology images and omics data has become the focus of cancer diagnosis and survival prediction studies. Previous studies have insufficiently explored the optimization and calibration of features between omics data and pathological image characteristics, which affects the performance of models in patient survival prediction to tackle these challenges, we developed a co-attention-based multi-modal feature reconstruction and alignment (CMFRA) framework that aims to uncover the connections between different data modalities and efficiently optimize and align modal features. We construct feature extractors for both pathology and omics that utilize the attention mechanism to identify potential links between omics features and the cellular morphology of pathology images. Additionally, feature decoders are utilized to reconstruct the multi-modal fusion features, facilitating the optimization of unimodal features. Our experimental results demonstrate that this modality alignment method not only improves the accuracy of the model's survival prediction, but also offers the way for personalized medicine and precision therapy.

articleTitle: Decoupled Distillation-Based Emotion-Oriented Trailer Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition(MER) refers to the process of inferring emotions expressed by individuals using text, audio, and image training samples, Currently, many multimodal models have achieved state-of-the-art performance on sentiment analysis datasets. However, current research mainly focuses on training and recognition on datasets, while neglecting its application in the industrial sector. This article proposes a video synthesis algorithm, used to generate movie trailers, Ultimately applied to future TV recommendation systems. Firstly, the CMU MOSI dataset is used to train a multimodal model. The input video is split into shots and sampled at equal intervals on a frame by frame basis. Then, optical character recognition (OCR) technology is used to extract subtitles, and the extracted subtitles, audio, and video frames are input into the model, and emotional scores are given to each shot. Finally, the desired movie emotional shots can be adjusted by setting emotional thresholds, and combine these candidate shots into a complete trailer. The experimental results show that the output movie trailer can meet the emotional needs of users, which is of great significance for the application of artificial intelligence in video editing.

articleTitle: Research on Radioisotope Identification of Nuclear Pulse Sequence Based on CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the statistical limitations of isotope identification Methods by gamma spectroscopy, this paper studies a method of isotope recognition based on improved Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) combined with convolutional bidirectional long short-term memory neural network (CNN-BiLSTM), which does not require spectrum formation and directly analyzes nuclear pulse sequences. Results show that the model can achieve 96.98 per cent recognition accuracy. In addition, the model shows a good recognition effect in different pulse number and pulse sequence time, which further verifies the feasibility of isotope recognition based on nuclear pulse sequence, and provides a new idea and method for radioisotope recognition technology.

Author Keywords: convolutional bidirectional long-short-term memory neural network

articleTitle: PillarDANet: An Improved PillarNet with Dual-Attention Mechanism for Ship Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes PillarDANet, an improved 3D point cloud ship detection method based on PillarNet, specifically targeting ship detection in high-head large ship locks. The method introduces a dual attention mechanism on PillarNet, including Position Attention Module (PAM) and Channel Attention Module (CAM), enhancing the perception of complex ship geometric structures. Additionally, multi-scale dilated convolution strategy is adopted in the neck network, significantly expanding the receptive field and improving the detection performance for large ship targets. Experimental results on the nuScenes dataset and a self-built ship dataset show that compared to the baseline PillarNet model, this method achieves 3.1% and 3.9% improvements in mAP metrics respectively, demonstrating effective detection performance.

articleTitle: CrossTransFuse:A Colorectal Polyp Segmentation Approach Using Multi-Scale Cross-Attention and GiFusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper introduces a polyp segmentation method named CrossTransFuse, designed to tackle the challenges posed by the varying sizes, shapes, and blurred boundaries of colorectal polyps, which increase the risk of misdiagnosis. By implementing a multi-scale interaction strategy, CrossTransFuse captures the subtle variations and complex characteristics of polyps. The proposed GiFusion module integrates features from both the Mask R-CNN and Transformer branches and uses residual blocks for connection. These integrated features effectively capture both global and local contexts at the current resolution, enabling more precise segmentation of polyp boundaries and accurate target localization. Evaluations on five common polyp segmentation datasets demonstrate that CrossTransFuse outperforms advanced networks, achieving more accurate segmentation of polyp boundary regions.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Breast Lesions in Ultrasound Images Based on Swin-Unet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a key role in the early detection and diagnosis of breast cancer. Based on the Swin-Unet model in this paper, combined with the Multi-Scale Dilated Fusion Attention (MDFA) module and the Simple, Parameter-Free Attention Module (SimAM) module, improvements and optimizations have been made for the breast cancer image segmentation task. The BUSI dataset is employed, which offers abundant breast cancer image samples to assist in evaluating the effect of the model in practical applications. The MDFA module enhances the model's ability to capture features of various scales through multi-scale dilated convolution techniques, overcoming the deficiencies of traditional convolutions when dealing with complex lesion areas. The SimAM module improves the recognition ability of key features by simulating the activation process of neurons and calculating the similarity between feature points and their expected states, further enhancing the accuracy of the segmentation results. Experimental results indicate that, compared with mainstream models such as FCN, UNet, SegNet, and ENC-Net, the improved Swin-Unet demonstrates a significant improvement in performance on the BUSI dataset. The introduction of the MDFA and SimAM modules endows the model with higher precision and robustness when handling breast cancer images. This research not only validates the effectiveness of the improved model but also provides a new direction for the application of deep learning in future breast cancer image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: A Novel Finetuned YOLOv8 Transfer Learning Model for Smoking Behavior Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper addresses the pressing need for smoking behavior detection in public health and safety monitoring, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing methods in real-time performance and accuracy, particularly in complex environments where precise monitoring is challenging. To this end, a transfer learning model based on YOLOv8 is proposed, where the pre-trained YOLOv8 architecture is fine-tuned to significantly enhance detection accuracy and real-time performance in specific scenarios, effectively adapting it to the task of smoking behavior detection.
