During training, data augmentation strategies such as random rotation, flipping, and brightness and contrast adjustments were employed to further optimize system performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy, recall, and detection speed, and shows exceptional robustness under complex backgrounds and partial occlusions. This approach not only substantially improves indoor smoking detection but also holds great potential for widespread application in public spaces and complex environments.

articleTitle: Research on Localization and Relocalization of Unmanned Vehicles Based on Multi-Line LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rise of autonomous driving technology, the ability to accurately localize and re-localize unmanned vehicles in complex outdoor environments has become a critical challenge. This paper proposes a solution to this problem by integrating the Normal Distributions Transform (NDT) matching algorithm for localization and the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm for re-localization. The proposed methods are tested and validated in real-world outdoor settings, with experimental results showing that the NDT algorithm ensures localization accuracy of at least 0.3 meters, providing stable and reliable results. Furthermore, the ICP algorithm demonstrates high precision in vehicle re-localization, confirming its practical applicability and accuracy in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Artificial Intelligence Technology in ADS-B Data Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Automatic Dependent Surveillance Broadcast (ADS-B) system is widely used in the field of aerial surveillance because of its accuracy and high efficiency. However, ADS-B system is easy to be spoofed and interfered because it broadcasts signals in plaintext format and lacks data encryption and message authentication mechanism. This article conducts research on this issue. Firstly, it analyzes the structure of the ADS-B system and discusses its data anomaly problems. It summarizes that researchers at home and abroad generally approach the solution to data anomaly problems from three directions: encrypting the data link, improving the ADS-B hardware and software, and analyzing from the perspective of the ADS-B data fields. Then, it particularly points out that artificial intelligence algorithms also build models from the perspective of the ADS-B data fields to complete ADS-B track data anomaly detection, including algorithms based on clustering, data reconstruction, and data temporal correlation. Finally, this paper compares the detection precision, recall rate, and F1 score of several deep learning algorithm models based on data time-related, and finds that they all have excellent ADS-B data anomaly detection effects, with detection precision all above 92.2%, recall rate all above 84.9%, and F1 score all above 86.8%.

articleTitle: Phenotypic Analysis and Variety Classification of Waxy Corn Seeds Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study aims to apply machine vision for phenotypic analysis and varietal classification of waxy corn seeds, addressing the challenges of varietal mixture that hinder industry development. High-quality imaging was used to capture seed images from three waxy corn varieties, and phenotypic features such as size, color, and texture were extracted by OpenCV. A comprehensive assessment of 15 phenotypic features for the three varieties has identified discernible variations in size, color, and texture features. To classify waxy corn seeds effectively, we applied a diverse set of machine learning algorithms, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Decision Trees (DT), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), each contributing unique strengths to the classification process. The five models achieved high accuracy rates, exceeding 90 % with the following values: KNN at 0.947, LDA at 0.986, DT at 0.922, SVM at 0.977, and ANN at 0.981. These findings highlight the potential of these algorithms, particularly LDA, for high-accuracy seed classification based on phenotypic features. This research has successfully developed classification models that enable the fast, impartial, and economical identification of waxy corn varieties. By expanding this methodology to include a wider range of varieties, future research could play a significant role in preventing seed and product adulteration in agriculture.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Transformer for Efficient CT Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes a super-resolution (SR) reconstruction method to improve the poor quality of low-resolution (LR) computed tomography (CT) images. Transformer-based methods have shown promising performance in image SR. However, there are two obstacles and key challenges: (1) The hierarchical information of images is not fully utilized; (2) The potential of the self-attention (SA) mechanism has not been fully exploited. To this end, we propose a Hierarchical Transformer for efficient CT image Super-Resolution(HTSR). Our HTSR can capture image hierarchical information from local, regional, and global. Specifically, to achieve efficient region modelling, we design a Content-Aware Transformer Block (CATB), which is a coarse-to-fine image block selection strategy to model long-range dependencies of semantically consistent information and eliminate interference from bad information. Moreover, we introduce Transposed Transformer Block (TTB), which can capture the long-range dependency and is applicable to large-sized images. Finally, combined with the Spatial window Transformer Block (SWTB), we design a network architecture of encoder-decoder, achieving an effective fusion of hierarchical information. Extensive experimental results have shown that the proposed method achieves good performance.

articleTitle: Research on Wheat Mold Degree Detection Based on Computer Vision Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Wheat, as one of the main cereals widely consumed globally, is the staple food for about one-third of the population in China. The production of wheat is closely related to people's lives and the development of society. Wheat kernels are known for their thin outer skin, loose tissue structure, and good storability. However, wheat kernels are susceptible to environmental factors, leading to heat-induced mold phenomena, which not only affect the quality of grain but also pose a threat to human health. Therefore, developing a rapid and accurate method for detecting the degree of mold in wheat kernels is of great significance for ensuring food safety. Wheat kernels with different degrees of mold were selected as the research subjects, and a dataset of their images was obtained using computer vision technology. Through preprocessing of the images, extraction of features, and training of the model, a classification model based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) was established. After the model underwent rigorous testing, it was found that it achieved a recognition rate of 97.3% for the degree of mold in wheat kernels. This finding indicated that the combination of computer vision technology with the SVM classification model could efficiently and accurately detect the degree of mold in wheat kernels, offering a new technical approach for food safety surveillance.

articleTitle: Harnessing Deep Learning Techniques for Lung Disease Diagnosis: A Comparative Study of CNN, Transformer and Mamba Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Pneumonia, an infectious lung condition caused by bacteria, viruses, or other microorganisms, significantly impacts both pediatric and geriatric populations. The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the necessity for swift and accurate diagnostic tools, with over 760 million infections reported. This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence in lung X-ray image classification by comparing the performance of three Convolutional Neural Networks, two Transformer models, and the Vision Mamba model using a standardized dataset. The study’s objectives were to (1) identify the most effective models, (2) examine the impact of initializing models using transfer learning, and (3) evaluate the Vision Mamba model’s performance relative to conventional models. Using a Kaggle dataset containing four X-ray image categories—COVID-19, normal, lung opacity, and viral pneumonia—six models were trained and tested with and without transfer learning. Results indicated that the Swin Transformer model outperformed others, and transfer learning significantly enhanced model accuracy. Although the Vision Mamba model exhibited lower accuracy, its computational efficiency highlights its potential utility. This study provides critical insights into artificial intelligence applications in lung disease diagnosis, supporting clinicians with accurate diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: Enhancing 3D Detection Accuracy in Autonomous Driving through Pseudo-LiDAR Augmentation and Downsampling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: 3D object detection is crucial for autonomous driving. Currently, most approaches depend on costly LiDAR sensors for acquiring precise depth information. Although pseudo-LiDAR techniques based on stereo cameras offer a more cost-effective alternative, their performance is still inferior to LiDAR-based methods. The objective of this paper is to improve detection accuracy using pseudo-LiDAR augmentation combined with downsampling. Specifically, in terms of pseudo-LiDAR augmentation, the GDC algorithm is employed to correct depth errors based on 4-beam LiDAR clouds, thereby improving pseudo-LiDAR quality. For pseudo-LiDAR downsampling, a 64-beam point cloud downsampling algorithm is utilized to improve the efficiency of PV-RCNN++ on dense pseudo-LiDAR clouds. Results from experiments on the KITTI 3D dataset indicate that our method substantially boosts detection accuracy across three object categories compared to traditional stereo detection algorithms. Notably, in the task of car detection, it surpasses the state-of-the-art stereo detection algorithm DSGN++ in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: ICP Registration Based on Overlapping Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To solve the problem that ICP(Iterative Closest Point), a widely used fine registration algorithm, can degrade good initial registration results, this paper introduces a step of overlapping region extraction between the initial registration and fine registration to further enhance the accuracy of ICP. Furthermore, a method for determining overlapping regions based on grid partitioning is proposed, which resolves the issue of longer consumption of time for overlapping regions in large-scale point clouds. Experimental results indicate that the improved algorithm process reduces angular errors by approximately 50% and translational errors by approximately 60% compared to the pre-improvement process.

articleTitle: Image Quality Assessment Characteristics for Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), Image Quality Assessment (IQA) techniques are increasingly used to evaluate the quality of images reconstructed through Super Resolution (SR). However, most IQA methods do not consider how the human eye assesses image quality; they primarily rely on complex networks for accuracy. This paper examines the relationship between humans and AI, arguing that IQA methods that integrate both top-down and bottom-up processes better align with human evaluation, whereas AI typically uses a solely bottom-up approach. We evaluate images generated by various SR algorithms using these two IQA methodologies. Experimental results show that humans prefer SR algorithms that emphasize global image features, while AI favors those focusing on local features. These findings highlight a divergence in image quality preferences between humans and AI, underscoring the need to select algorithms based on specific application scenarios.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cache Management for Complex Storage Systems Using CNN-LSTM-Based Spatiotemporal Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent cache management strategy based on CNN-LSTM to improve the performance and cache hit rate of storage systems. Through comparative experiments with traditional algorithms (such as LRU and LFU) and other deep learning models (such as RNN, GRU-RNN and LSTM), the results show that the CNN-LSTM model has significant advantages in cache demand prediction. The MSE and MAE values of this model are significantly reduced, proving its effectiveness under complex data access patterns. This study not only verifies the potential of deep learning technology in storage system optimization, but also provides direction and reference for further optimizing and improving cache management strategies. This intelligent cache management strategy performs well in complex storage environments. By combining the spatial feature extraction capabilities of convolutional neural networks and the time series modeling capabilities of long short-term memory networks, the CNN-LSTM model can more accurately predict cache needs, thereby Dynamically optimize cache allocation to improve system response speed and resource utilization. This research provides theoretical support and practical reference for cache optimization under large-scale data access modes, and is of great significance to improving the performance of future storage systems.

articleTitle: A Tea Buds Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLO11
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The detection and localization of tea buds are a critical part of the intelligent tea harvesting process, and using deep learning-based object detection technology to detect tea buds is of great significance for intelligent tea harvesting. This paper proposes an improved tea bud detection algorithm based on YOLO11, which uses the CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) attention mechanism to automatically adjust the focus on different areas, enhancing the model's ability to capture targets against complex backgrounds and improving the model's accuracy. Experimental results on the tea bud dataset show that the improved algorithm has an average precision mAP50 that is 1.4% higher than the original YOLO11, and the mAP50:95 increased by 2.2%, and there is also a significant improvement in detection accuracy compared to other YOLO detection algorithms, providing a technical foundation for the application of intelligent tea bud harvesting equipment.

articleTitle: Lightweight Model for Apple Leaf Disease Recognition Based on Haar Wavelet Downsampling and Focal Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of large number of parameters and high computational cost in disease recognition models, and the decline in model accuracy caused by image noise interference and sample class imbalance in apple leaf disease recognition, this paper proposes an improved model combining Haar wavelet down-sampling and focal loss function. The improved model uses MobileNetV3-Small as the base model and enhances its resistance to image noise in apple leaf disease recognition by applying Haar wavelet downsampling instead of the traditional downsampling method. Additionally, the focal loss function replaces the cross-entropy loss function, improving the model’s accuracy in recognizing minority classes of diseases. Experimental results show that the improved model, MobileNet-HWD-FL, achieves a recognition accuracy of 96.42% in the apple leaf disease recognition task, with 1.52M parameters and 68.19M FLOPs. Compared with classical models such as MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNet_v2_1.5×, and DenseNet121, the improved model offers higher accuracy and fewer parameters. The improved method proposed in this paper provides an effective approach for lightweight identification of apple leaf diseases and other plant diseases.

articleTitle: PVDiff: A Palm-Vein Data Augmentation Method Based on Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Palm-vein recognition has garnered significant attention recently due to its superior privacy and safety features. However, the public dataset for palm-vein is much less. Moreover, manually collecting palm-vein data from diverse individuals is challenging and complex. To tackle these problems, we propose a palm-vein data augmentation method based on diffusion model called PVDiff. We firstly introduce the diffusion model to effectively capture the distinct spatial distributions of palm veins, so that the brand-new palm-vein images can be effectively generated. Besides, we propose several augmentation strategies for integrating the generated palm-veins to a complete dataset with good diversity and robustness. Experiment results represent that our PVDiff can not only generate high quality palm-vein data compared with other generative methods, but also can effectively enhance the performance of the recognition model. For the same backbone, the augmented data supports the model mostly decreases 78.1% on the Fail Accept Rate at Fail Recognize Rate under 0.0001%. Furthermore, our PVDiff significantly benefit the robustness of the recognition model for the complex real-world scenes.

articleTitle: Prior Information Guidance for Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Restoration of images affected by severe weather conditions like heavy fog is indeed a current and significant topic within the field of computer vision. Despite the good performance of existing image dehazing methods, most rely on synthetic datasets due to the difficulty of obtaining real hazy images. These synthetic datasets lack the complexity found in real foggy conditions, leading to poor generalization of the dehazing algorithms. Moreover, existing end-to-end dehazing methods, which are often based on general frameworks for image inpainting or translation, do not adequately account for the unique characteristics of hazy images. This results in color distortion and incomplete dehazing with some fog remaining. To address these issues, we propose a novel image dehazing framework guided by prior information, comprising a physical prior module and an image prior module. Extensive experiments confirms that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across various dehazing datasets.

articleTitle: A Global-local Feature Interaction Network for Anti-cloud Interference Change Detection based on Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Bi-temporal change detection (CD) constitutes a vital task within the domain of remote sensing (RS). due to pseudochange caused by factors such as seasonal climate variations, temporary objects, and cloud interference. To address the pseudochange issue stemming from cloud interference, we propose a global-local feature interaction anti-cloud interference change detection network (ACCDNet) based on contrastive learning. To mitigate the scarcity of remote sensing datasets with cloud interference, we leverage contrastive learning principles, using remote sensing images of the same scene at the same time with and without cloud interference as positive sample pairs to pre-train anti-cloud interference capability of the feature extractor. The proposed CD network which bases on a CNN-transformer network, utilizes Resnet to extract multi-scale features from the original input images. We introduce transformer modules and attention mechanisms to effectively extract the contextual information within the input images. To address the pseudochange issue caused by cloud interference, we simulate the effect of thin cloud interference using Perlin noise and add it to classical datasets. Experimental results on LEVIR-CD and LEVIR-CD-cloud datasets augmented with cloud interference demonstrate the priority and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model-Based Framework for Depression Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Depression is a common mental health disorder that significantly impacts individuals’ quality of life and places a considerable burden on global healthcare systems. Accurate and timely detection of depression is crucial for effective intervention and treatment. In recent years, deep learning has shown promise in automating depression detection. However, due to the lack of high-quality and large-scale datasets, models often overfit the training data, resulting in poor performance on new data. To address this issue, we propose using a large language model (LLM) pre-trained on mental health counseling tasks to achieve depression detection. These pre-trained models possess extensive knowledge of mental health, which helps mitigate the overfitting problem associated with smaller datasets. However, when dealing with domain-specific expertise, LLM may produce hallucinations or fail to generate relevant content due to a lack of domain-specific information in their pre-training data. To address this limitation, we introduce retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques into the depression detection task. We use GraphRAG to structure domain-specific knowledge related to depression detection into a knowledge graph, and incorporate this knowledge during the inference process. This approach enhances the performance of large language models in depression detection. Notably, our method achieves satisfactory performance without training. This offers significant advantages, reducing the computational costs and resources required for model training while enabling rapid deployment in real-world applications. Furthermore, operating effectively without further training demonstrates good generalization to new data, enhancing the model’s practical utility in depression detection tasks.

articleTitle: DTS-YOLOv8n: A Lightweight Vehicle And Pedestrian Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In target-intensive detection environments, the detection of vehicles and pedestrians faces the problem of misdetection and omission of occluded objects and small target objects, as well as the challenge that the model is too complex to be lightweight. In this paper, the YOLOV8n model is studied and improved, and a lightweight vehicle pedestrian detection network DTS-YOLOv8n is proposed. Firstly, by introducing the C2f_DWR_DRB module, the reparameterised large convolutional kernel layer improves the performance without increasing the computational cost, which enhances the detection speed and accuracy of the model, and secondly, the Triplet Attention mechanism is added to improve the performance of the model under the lightweight architecture, and in order to further reduce the complexity of the model and to maintain the detection accuracy, the study also combines the GSConv and VoV-GSCSP modules and introduces the Slim-Neck method, thus achieving more efficient and accurate vehicle and pedestrian keypoint detection. The experimental results on KITTI dataset show that the accuracy rate is increased to 89.3%, the recall rate to 74.3%, mAP@0.5 increased to 84.3%, corresponding to a 0.6% improvement, and mAP@0.5-0.95 also increased to 56.7%, corresponding to a 0.3% improvement. Meanwhile, the number of parameters and the calculation amount of the model are reduced by 13.3% and 13.6% respectively. While reducing computational costs, the detection accuracy was significantly improved, and all performance metrics outperformed the original YOLOv8n model.

articleTitle: Identifying Indoor Natural Gas Work Targets with an Enhanced YOLOv8 Model Incorporating RMT Backbone
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study aims at the real-time recognition of indoor natural gas work targets utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8 model integrated with an Retentive Networks Meet Vision Transformers (RMT) backbone. The model is specifically designed to detect and recognize key work instruments and objects, including gas stoves, water heaters, flue pipes, valves, and more, from video footage captured by wearable devices equipped with cameras. To further improve the detection accuracy, we introduce the MPD-Inner-IoU loss function to better handle the positioning of bounding boxes. The enhanced model is trained and validated using a comprehensive dataset gathered from real-world indoor gas operation scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s capability for accurate and real-time identification of indoor natural gas work targets, highlighting its potential for improving safety and efficiency in gas operation environments.

articleTitle: Recognition of Autism Spectrum Disorder via Dual-Channel Feature Fusion and Multi-Resolution Brain Region Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by disruptions in brain functional networks. Current classification studies using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) often struggle with issues of model interpretability and incorporating multi-scale features effectively. This study proposes a multi-resolution brain network model that integrates degree-normalized graph neural networks with fully connected attention mechanisms to boost classification accuracy and identify critical brain networks related to ASD. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms traditional methods in accuracy, sensitivity, and other evaluation metrics. Furthermore, analysis of brain network correlations reveals functional networks closely associated with ASD, providing valuable insights and a strong reference for clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Optimization of U-Net Model for Liver Tumor Image Segmentation Based on Channel Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study focuses on exploring the role of channel attention mechanism in the improvement of U-Net model, especially in the field of medical image segmentation of liver tumors. By integrating channel attention mechanisms, the U-Net model can more accurately identify key features in images, significantly improving the accuracy of segmentation tasks. The experimental data shows that the optimized U-Net model performs consistently during the training and validation phases, demonstrating good generalization ability and low risk of overfitting. Especially in the 30th training cycle, the loss values of the model on both the training and validation sets decreased to the lowest and tended to stabilize, further confirming the stability and reliability of the model. On the test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.62% and a mean intersection to union ratio (Miou) of 83.27%, demonstrating its high predictive accuracy in liver tumor image segmentation tasks. The segmentation results of the test set further confirm the accuracy and strong generalization ability of the model. In summary, this study confirms that the U-Net model with improved channel attention mechanism has significant advantages in liver tumor image segmentation tasks. It not only improves segmentation accuracy but also enhances the model's generalization ability, which is of great significance for improving the automation level of medical image analysis. Especially in the fields of precision medicine and computer-aided diagnosis, this model can provide doctors with more accurate decision support assistance.

articleTitle: An expression robust 3D face recognition method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to address the issue of the poor robustness of 3D face recognition against expression changes, we propose a method for expression-robust 3D face recognition. Firstly, the ridge points on the entire 3D face surface are extracted based on the curvature information of the surface. The ridge points exhibiting the most significant alterations in concavity and convexity are then employed to characterise the face as a faithful representation of the 3D face surface. Secondly, the face is divided into four regions based on an analysis of surface deformation caused by expression changes, and ridge point sets in each regions are characterised using the 3D shape context descriptors. The matching cost is in each regions calculated using a Chi-square test, calculating its matching cost by regions and fusing the matching cost of each regions at the decision level to produce the final recognition result. The experimental results obtained from the CASIA database demonstrate that the proposed method effectively utilises the ridge points on the 3D face surface, incorporates the spatial topology information of the 3D data, and considers the overall facial structure while attenuating the influence of expression changes through the weighted fusion of subregions. This approach achieves high recognition rate and robustness for faces with various expressions.

articleTitle: RFCBAM UNet: Enhancing UNet with Receptive-Field Convolutional Block Attention for Brain Tumor Segmentation Based on MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Brain tumor is a common type of tumor, which is extremely hazardous to human health. MRI is the most widely used non-invasive imaging tool for diagnosing brain tumors. Accurate segmentation of lesion regions from MRI is of great significance for brain tumor diagnosis and treatment planning. However, existing automatic segmentation algorithms, such as UNet and Swin-Unet, rely on a large amount of manually annotated data and have poor generalization on independent test datasets. While interactive segmentation algorithm is an important way to improve existing automatic segmentation algorithms by modeling the dynamic change process of image annotation and significantly improving the accuracy of model segmentation with better robustness and generalization. Therefore, this study focuses on the design of interactive brain tumor segmentation models based on multipoint prompt. First, in order to effectively integrate the multipoint prompt coding information with the multimodal MRI images information, this study proposes the ConvM module, which is able to better handle 4-channel multimodal MRI images. Second, in the part of feature extraction backbone network, this study proposes a new backbone network RFCBAM Unet which stands for Receptive-Field Convolutional Block Attention Module based on UNet. RFCBAM UNet improves the ability of the network to perceive channel information and spatial information, as well as solves the problem of parameter sharing in the process of attentional computation. Finally, this study supplementally employs the Object Contextual Representations (OCR) module to enhance the contextual representation of the tumor ROI pixels, thus improving the segmentation effect. After a series of experiments, it is shown that the RFCBAM UNet designed in this study is able to segment the tumor region of brain tumor patients more accurately with less number of interactions. The model can achieve a Dice coefficient of 0.8, 0.85 and 0.90 in an average of 3.43, 4.61 and 6.74 clicks, which is a series of facts that validate the usability and effectiveness of the model proposed in this study.

articleTitle: Research on Rapid Detection and Identification Technology of Pavement Defects based on Target Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of road pavement detection in China, aiming at the problem of rapid identification of highway pavement defects, the research on rapid identification technology based on image processing and deep learning algorithm was carried out to realize the automatic identification and rapid diagnosis of defects. In addition to providing abundant and precise data support for thorough highway maintenance choices, intelligent analysis of pavement defect types and size factors offers extensive data sources for the creation of a sizable maintenance database.

articleTitle: Multimodal Infant Emotion Recognition Using Visual and Audio Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Infant emotion recognition can help infants grow better. Due to the limited availability of multimodal datasets and the insufficient use of multimodal data in current infant emotion recognition research. First, we constructed an audiovisual infant emotion dataset with 1,338 samples, following the standards of Baby FACS and SAEVD-R, achieving an inter-rater reliability of 75%. Then, we propose a multimodal method that integrates visual and audio information to better capture the temporal dynamics of emotions, addressing the limitations of single-modal methods and improving recognition by learning key emotional segments. This method incorporates a forward masked temporal attention mechanism and a temporal attention enhancement module, allowing the model to capture dynamic relationships between current and past time steps while focusing on the most important video sub-segments for emotion recognition. Experimental results show that this method effectively extracts key features from the infant emotion dataset and the public adult audiovisual emotion dataset, RAVDESS, and significantly improves emotion recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: An Iterated Local Search Method for Cluster-Analysis-Based Multibaseline Phase Unwrapping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The accuracy of the cluster-analysis-based multibaseline phase unwrapping (CA-MBPU) algorithm is primarily influenced by the effective formulation and solution of intercept term constraint equations. However, the presence of local extrema during the discrete optimization process lead to suboptimal solutions, thereby compromising both accuracy and efficiency of the process. To overcome this issue, an improved solution strategy for the intercept term constraint equations is proposed. An iterated local search method integrating neighborhood operations is proposed in this paper, enabling dynamic adjustments to both step size and solution space. This enhancement improves the algorithm’s ability to explore the global solution space and prevents premature convergence to local extrema. Experiments results on both simulated and real data verified the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Drone Small Target Detection Based on YOLOV8-RAWM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the widespread use of drones, detecting small targets in aerial images captured by drones poses significant challenges. Issues such as small size and low resolution make these targets difficult to detect. In response to this, this paper proposes an improved object detection algorithm based on YOLOv8. Firstly, a lightweight convolution and Manhattan self-attention mechanism were introduced into the backbone network, along with a feature fusion module in the neck, and the loss function was optimized to enhance the model's performance and robustness in small target detection. Experiments show that the model achieved a 6.2% improvement in mAP@0.5 and a 5% increase in recall on the VisDrone2019 dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting small targets in drone applications.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Vision Based Flapping Height Measurement of Helicopter Rotor Blade
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents a novel measurement method of helicopter rotor blade flapping height, which takes catadioptric images as a principal sensor. Lifting the restrictions of sensor installation precision, this method applies with good flexibility. The measurement procedure starts from camera calibration, and achieves measuring the flapping height differences with high precision by sensing the three-dimensional information of calibration pattern corner points. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: TA-YOLO: A Task-aligned YOLO Detector with Even-sized Kernel Convolutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, the YOLO series has become the most popular paradigm in real-time object detection due to its excellent performance and detection speed. Researchers have made significant achievements by exploring network architecture design, data augmentation, loss functions, and other strategies. In terms of architecture design, researchers tend to favor odd-sized kernel convolutions as computational units for expanding the receptive field and performing downsampling operations. In contrast, even-sized kernels are rarely adopted because they introduce receptive field misalignment. Furthermore, researchers have overlooked that odd-sized convolutions can introduce the offset during downsampling. In this work, we primarily address the misalignment issues introduced by convolutions during feature extraction. Firstly, we design the C2BottleNeck module, which achieves better parameter utilization while addressing the offset issue caused by even-sized kernels. Subsequently, we develop the Task-Aligned Downsampling (TADown) block which mitigates the offset problems associated with C3 during down-sampling. Finally, by adjusting the network's width and depth, we design a high-performance task-aligned object detection model based on YOLO (TA-YOLO). Extensive experiments demonstrate that TA-YOLO achieves state-of-the-art performance on the VOC dataset, as shown in Fig. 1. For example, our TA-YOLO-S achieves a 0.9% AP improvement under a similar parameter count and computational load to GELAN-S. Compared with YOLOv8-X, our TA-YOLO-X has 56% fewer parameters for a 0.5% AP improvement.

articleTitle: Cognitive Method for Apple Grading Based on Convolutional Attention and YOLOv8s Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Manual sorting of similar fruits is greatly affected by the subjective factors of the sorting personnel. To address this issue, a cognitive approach for apple grading utilizing convolutional attention and the YOLOv8s network was investigated. A convolutional attention mechanism is designed within the convolutional block for apple feature extraction. This mechanism automatically learns and weights the importance of different spatial positions and channel features, helping the model to capture key information from input apple images better, suppress irrelevant data, and enhance feature extraction. First, a cognitive approach for apple grading utilizing convolutional attention and the YOLOv8s network is proposed to clarify the structure and function of the model. Secondly, considering the material transportation characteristics of the apple sorting site, image enhancement technology is used to preprocess the original input image to construct an apple sample dataset. Finally, the structure of the convolutional attention module is explained, and a cognitive algorithm for apple grading based on convolutional attention and YOLOv8s is provided. To determine how well this method works, a series of comparative experiments was performed. Experimental results show significant cognitive accuracy and calculation speed advantages, providing theoretical support for subsequent online sorting systems.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis Model for Cadmium Based on Energy-Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Energy-Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence (EDXRF) faces challenges in trace cadmium (Cd) quantification, including high interference and low sensitivity, which affect detection accuracy. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), known for their strong feature extraction capabilities, offer a promising approach to improve EDXRF's performance in quantitative analysis. This study explores the effectiveness of a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN) in predicting Cd concentrations in soybean X-ray fluorescence spectra, with a focus on how convolutional layer configuration and hyperparameters influence model convergence. We tested 16 different scenarios, varying the number of convolutional layers and filters per layer, and identified the optimal architecture as four convolutional layers with 16, 16, 32, and 64 filters. With a learning rate of 0.01 and 80 training epochs, the model achieved a 92% prediction accuracy on unseen soybean spectral data. These results demonstrate that 1DCNNs can effectively process EDXRF data, providing a novel method for Cd quantification.

articleTitle: CNN-Transformer Feature Aggregation Networks for Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper introduces the CAT model, achieving 98.9% accuracy on the ShipsEar dataset by combining CNN and ViT with a fusion and separation mechanism for underwater acoustic signal processing. The model captures both short-term and long-term dependencies through integrated feature extraction and utilizes multi-spectral preprocessing to enhance performance. CAT shows potential for applications in speech recognition and environmental sound classification, with future work focusing on real-time monitoring and additional input features.

articleTitle: Research on the Image Model of Substation UAV Inspection Based on the Improved YOLO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the gradual expansion of China's power grid, the traditional substation inspection method can no longer meet the practical needs. In view of the defects of YOLO algorithm in target identification, such as low accuracy, false detection and poor timeliness, the paper integrates the lightweight network and attention mechanism, improves the YOLO algorithm, and constructs a lightweight image model of UAV inspection in substation. The results show that the method to improve the loss function and non-maximum suppression of the YOLO algorithm is effective, with its target identification accuracy improving more than 5.37% and the average accuracy by 2.14%. The detection accuracy and detection time of the YOLO model integrating the lightweight network and attention mechanism are improved, and the frame rate is more than 20.67% higher than that of the traditional model, realizing the purpose of the lightweight model. The research has important application value in the inspection of small UAV in substation.

articleTitle: Apple Leaf Disease Detection Algorithm Based on an Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To improve the precision of recognizing apple leaf diseases in real-world applications, a detection model for apple leaf diseases is proposed, utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8 architecture. A Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), incorporating both channel and spatial attention mechanisms, is introduced to enhance the extraction of disease-specific features while effectively ignoring irrelevant information in the images. A DyHead detection head replaces the original head in the YOLOv8 model, integrating scale, spatial, and task attention mechanisms to further enhance the model's detection performance. Compared with the original YOLOv8 algorithm, the improved YOLOv8 model increases mAP@0.5 by 1.6% and mAP@0.5:0.95 by 1.2%. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed improved YOLOv8 algorithm achieves high recognition accuracy and detection speed, providing a precise real-time detection method for apple leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Research on Helmet Wearing Detection for Dense Cycling Crowd Based on Improved YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: An improved YOLOv8n algorithm is proposed to address the issue of low helmet detection accuracy caused by the high density of electric bike riders in complex scenarios. Introducing Channel Prior Convolutional Attention (CPCA) mechanism to enhance the feature extraction capability of the model; Introducing Symmetric Positive Definite Convolution (SPDConv) to enhance ordinary convolutions; Replace the bounding box loss function with a Weighted Intersection over Union (Wise IoU) function to improve the model’s ability to locate small targets. The experimental results showed that the improved model improved the mAP accuracy detected on the self-made dataset by 4.4%, with only a slight increase in the number of model parameters, and has the potential to be used as a solution in practical applications.

articleTitle: Capsule Network Model-Based Fracture Recognition in X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In modern medicine, X-ray images are widely used as an important diagnostic tool for detecting and evaluating a variety of diseases such as bone fractures, lung diseases, and tumors. However, traditional X-ray image recognition relies on the experience and expertise of doctors, which involves the risk of misdiagnosis and missed diagnosis, especially in areas with limited medical resources or inexperienced doctors. In order to improve the accuracy and efficiency of diagnosis, the application of deep learning techniques becomes increasingly important. In this study, a capsule network-based fracture recognition model for X-ray images is proposed, and the advantages of capsule networks in capturing complex features of images are verified by training and testing the model on X-ray images from different anatomical regions. The experimental results show that the CapsNet model achieves an accuracy of 84.2% in fracture recognition, which is better than the traditional neural network model, demonstrating its potential and application value in medical imaging diagnosis.

articleTitle: Dynamic Weighting-Based Deep Learning for SLAM Loop Closure Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In LiDAR SLAM systems, loop closure detection is a crucial component to ensure localization accuracy and map consistency. OverlapNet, a loop closure detection algorithm based on image overlap rate, has demonstrated strong performance. However, the current loss function of OverlapNet does not account for the uncertainty differences between tasks, which may lead to insufficient adjustment of task weights. To address this, this paper proposes a dynamic weight-based SLAM loop closure detection method, DW-LoopNet. By introducing a dynamic weight mechanism, this method automatically adjusts the relative weights of overlap and yaw angle estimation tasks. Based on real-time evaluation of environmental feature importance, DW-LoopNet dynamically adjusts the weights of different features, ensuring that key features receive higher attention in loop closure detection. Experimental results show that DW-LoopNet significantly outperforms other baseline methods on the KITTI and Ford Campus datasets, providing a more accurate and robust loop closure detection solution for SLAM systems.

articleTitle: Application of Clothing CAD System Based on Virtual Reality Technology in Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Clothing CAD, as a technology originating from modern technology, has a profound impact on the clothing industry. This article takes modern clothing design as the starting point, discusses clothing CAD technology, briefly summarizes the application significance of related technologies, analyzes the requirements brought by personalized clothing development to design, and studies how to use CAD technology, related measuring equipment, and CNC equipment to achieve non-contact measurement of human body data collection for professional clothing customization. Studied how to improve the layout utilization of irregular fabrics, realize the possibility of quickly carving personalized buttons, meet consumer needs and respond quickly to production, and researched the wider application scope of CAD technology. Based on the CLO3D fitting software for 3D virtual fitting, virtual stitching is performed on clothing samples, and the appearance of finished clothing is presented through virtual models. Combined with clothing pressure testing, the rationality and feasibility of clothing sample design are verified.

articleTitle: Research on Fengyun-4A cloud base height estimation method based on Extreme Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Inversion model of Fengyun-4A (FY-4A) satellite cloud base height based on ensemble learning. The research contents include: data preprocessing, screening of influencing factors that are highly correlated with cloud base height, such as cloud top height, infrared brightness temperature, etc., and matching CloudSat and FY-4A data; The inversion model was constructed, the convolutional neural network was used to extract the cloud image features, and the cloud base height was inverted by combining the XGBoost algorithm. The inversion results are compared and analyzed with the CloudSat product. The key problems to be solved include dataset preparation, model training optimization, and model evaluation and validation. The aim of this study is to improve the accuracy of weather forecasting, improve the parameterization scheme of climate models, improve aviation safety, and explore the application potential of FY-4A satellite data in cloud base altitude retrieval.

articleTitle: Detection and Recognition of Poppy in UAV Imagery Based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study addresses the issue of poppy control by designing an improved YOLO algorithm based on UAV imagery for detecting and recognizing poppy targets in drone-captured scenes, enhancing its applicability in real-world scenarios. Traditional object detection models applied to poppy detection face challenges such as insufficient feature fusion, suboptimal attention mechanisms, and high false positive and false negative rates in complex environments. Additionally, these models struggle to balance detection accuracy with model efficiency. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved detection method, incorporating a custom-designed DC-C2f module to enhance feature extraction, an SD-attention detection head to focus on key target areas, and an SPD-Conv convolutional structure to optimize feature fusion and representation while reducing model complexity. In experiments, a DJI Matrice 300 RTK drone was used to collect 6,000 training images and 2,000 test images from rural landscapes under various lighting conditions, including sunny and cloudy days. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to mainstream algorithms, with a recall of 64%, precision of 84.8%, and mean average precision (mAP) of 72.9%, while maintaining a lightweight model architecture. These results significantly reduce false positives and false negatives, validating the effectiveness, superiority, and practical application potential of the proposed approach in poppy detection.

articleTitle: MAHSNet: Multi-Scale Adaptive Hybrid Semantic Network for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Benefiting from self-attention, the Transformer-based methods excel in global context modeling. However, these methods have limitations in capturing local dependencies between pixels, making it difficult to accurately segment small lesions, small tissues, and complex target boundaries. To address this issue, we propose the Multi-Scale Adaptive Hybrid Semantic Network (MAHSNet) for medical image segmentation. The core of MAHSNet is the Efficient Pure Attention Cascaded Decoder (EPACD). Unlike traditional CNN-Transformer decoder architectures, EPACD introduces gate attention, coordinate attention, and boundary attention to accurately segment local details and target boundaries, while significantly reducing the model's parameters and computational complexity. Experimental results on six datasets across two modalities demonstrate that MAHSNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in multiple medical segmentation tasks. For example, the Dice scores on the Synapse datasets reached 83.76%. The parameters and computational complexity were reduced by 73% and 82% compared to TransUnet, achieving dual improvements in segmentation performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Graph Embedding-Based Fraud Nest Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the increasing severity of telecommunications network fraud, this paper proposes a graph embedding-based fraud nest detection method aimed at utilizing artificial intelligence and graph neural network technology to identify and prevent telecommunications network fraud. The article first analyzes the challenges in current telecommunications network fraud detection, pointing out the limitations of rule-based expert systems and machine learning-based models. Subsequently, it details a new algorithm design, including graph embedding modules, graph aggregation modules, and Graph Neural Network (GNN) modules, which work together to identify fraudulent activities. By constructing a graph composed of nodes (users or devices) and edges (user interactions), GNN can capture global structural information in the data, identify implicit connections between users and devices, track abnormal behaviors and similar user groups, thereby identifying potential fraud gangs. The experimental part was conducted in a specific telecommunications network call environment, where users were treated as nodes and call behaviors as edges to construct a graph data structure. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through data cleaning, feature extraction, standardization, and dataset partitioning. Compared with models such as GCN, GAT, and RGCN, the GNN designed in this paper demonstrated superiority in accuracy, AUC, and recall rate. Finally, the paper summarizes the research findings and prospects for future work, emphasizing the practical significance of this method in fraud prevention and intervention.

articleTitle: An Inspection Method for Sheet Metal Concave Features Based on Rules
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Sheet metal is the basic component of the vehicle shell, and its design has become an important part of the product development process. Aiming at the problems of low efficiency and easy omission in manual inspection of concave features in 3D models, an automatic inspection method of sheet metal concave features was proposed. Firstly, the topological information is extracted based on the B-rep model of sheet metal, and the adjacency between faces is combined to classify; Then, the sheet metal sag features are identified according to the topology and feature rule information, and the compliance of the part concave feature is inspected by extracting the corresponding feature parameters and comparing with the safety threshold; Finally, the inspection system is designed based on CATIA development environment, and the effectiveness of the automatic inspection system is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Power Generation Prediction Method Combining Spatio-Temporal Autocorrelation and Multi-Dimensional Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the problems of energy security and environmental pollution becoming more and more prominent, how to increase the diversity of power sources, enhance the proportion of renewable energy as well as solve the problems of difficult prediction of renewable energy power generation are crucial for grid stability and management. Traditional time series forecasting models are difficult to cope with the volatility and spatial-temporal correlation of renewable energy generation. In this paper, we propose an innovative integrated forecasting model that incorporates spatial autocorrelation convolutional long-short time memory network and variational modal decomposition model (AHA-VMD) improved based on artificial hummingbird algorithm. Firstly, the generation power time-series signal is decomposed into several sub-signals using the decomposition model. Next, the spatio-temporal autocorrelation of the sub-signals is calculated separately, based on which they are input into the prediction model. The model enhances the capability of capturing the generation power under different time scales and weather conditions through multi-dimensional clustering of the sub-signals as well as spatial statistical properties. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms other single or simply integrated models.

articleTitle: Few-shot Image Generation via Non-Local Feature Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Few-shot image generation aims to generate high-quality and highly diverse images for domains with limited training data. However, a small number of training samples often leads to overfitting of the model. Moreover, existing methods do not fully utilize the specific information of training images, resulting in a loss of generative diversity in the generated images. To address this issue, we propose a few-shot image generation method based on non-local feature constraints. This method employs non-local feature extraction to extract the style features of target-domain images, fully utilizing the style information of target-domain samples to guide the style transformation of generated images. To ensure that the non-local feature module extracts the common style features of real images, we propose the style consistency loss to constrain feature consistency. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Research on Sea Surface Temperature Prediction and El Niño Phenomenon Prediction Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As the impact of global climate change on human society and the natural environment becomes increasingly significant, accurately predicting the El Niño phenomenon has become crucial. The El Niño phenomenon is a natural event characterized by abnormal warming of sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, which has profound effects on global weather patterns and climate systems. Traditional forecasting models, such as statistical and physical models, perform well in short-term predictions but show a significant decline in accuracy as the time span increases. This study explores the application of the GraphSAGE model based on Graph Neural Networks (GNN) using sea surface temperature (SST) data to predict El Niño phenomena. By modeling SST data as a graph structure, GraphSAGE captures the latent relationships between grid nodes, improving long-term prediction accuracy. Experimental results show that compared to traditional machine learning methods, the GraphSAGE model demonstrates higher predictive accuracy over extended time spans.

articleTitle: PSD Analysis of Human Different Sleeping Stages EEG Signals in Various Band on MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent decades, researchers have categorized sleep into four distinct stages, primarily characterized by changes in different frequency bands of EEG signals. Studying brain wave signals can provide insights into the mechanism of sleep and the treatment of sleep-related disorders. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the power spectral density (PSD) of human sleep EEG signals, focusing on the relative power percentages of the Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma frequency bands. The experimental data were obtained from the study of C.I. Acı and M. Kaya. The subjects were healthy males aged 23 and 26 years old. Using MATLAB, this study analyzed the PSD of EEG signals over various time intervals to observe changes in frequency bands and their relative power percentages. This study found that during the first 10 minutes, both subjects were in the NREM phase, and both of their Delta waves were most pronounced during the first 10 minutes. At 10-20 minutes, subject 1 gradually shifted to REM, with an increase in the high-frequency component of the EEG signal, while subject 2's did not change significantly. At 20-30 minutes, both subjects gradually moved into wakefulness, with the high-frequency component dominating. These findings lay the groundwork for future research on the PSD of EEG signals across different stages of human sleep.

articleTitle: A Study on Improved Algorithms for Mid-to Long-Term Power Forecasting of New Energy Photovoltaics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Mid-to long-term photovoltaic power forecasting is of great significance for reducing grid dispatching difficulty, increasing the stability of new energy grid integration, and achieving optimal operation of power systems. In this regard, a Multiple Mixed Strategy Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (MMSWOA) is proposed. This algorithm uses a novel Chebyshev chaotic map to initialize the population settings, increasing the diversity and randomness of individuals in the population to better simulate actual conditions. Additionally, the convergence factor of the algorithm is improved by introducing adaptive weights, optimal neighborhood perturbation, and a spiral position curve, which helps the algorithm to more accurately adjust the search space, improve convergence precision, and prevent it from falling into local optima. The algorithm is further optimized with a CNN-BiLSTM model. Matlab simulations and experimental results show that the proposed method can be effectively applied to actual photovoltaic power forecasting.

articleTitle: Integration of 3D Attention Mechanism and Atrous Convolution for Lung Nodule Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Lung nodules, as an initial symptomatic indication of lung cancer, have been a significant concern for human health and well-being. In order to achieve more accurate segmentation of lung nodules in CT images, a 3D U-net segmentation method is proposed that incorporates the attention mechanism and dense cavity convolution to address the incomplete acquisition of spatial features of lung nodules by the U-net network. Firstly, a 3D Convolutional Block Attention Module is added after the jump connection to avoid the loss of spatial dimensional information due to the sequence-dependent channel attention by optimizing the parallel channel and spatial attention modules, and to improve the attention of the model to the key features, which helps the network focus on important lung nodule characteristics. Second, by adding the Residual-Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling block at the bottleneck of the network, the network can improve the receptive field while maintaining high resolution, and capture more information between layers of CT slices. In this paper, Luna16 and a case dataset from a hospital in Southwest China are used, and the experimental results show that the four metrics of Dice, Recall, Precision, and Jaccard have been improved by 3.14%, 2.06%, 1.67%, and 1.69%, respectively, and the segmentation results of the model in this paper are also closer to the gold standard compared to other mainstream methods.

articleTitle: Semantic-Guided Sampling and Multi-Head Shape Encoding for Enhanced 3D Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Currently, voxel-based 3D single-stage detectors have been widely studied, but point-based single-stage methods still require further exploration. This study proposes a novel single-stage 3D point cloud detector that fully utilizes point cloud shape information. In 3D point cloud object detection tasks, existing methods have the following shortcomings: failing to fully utilize semantic and shape information of points during the segmentation of foreground and background points; not effectively utilizing this information when generating high-quality candidate boxes; and neglecting the correlation between channels, leading to limited feature representation capability. These factors collectively result in reduced detection accuracy. To enhance shape information in candidate points, this study adopts the following strategies: introducing a semantic-guided farthest point sampling method during the downsampling stage to increase the sampling rate of foreground points and suppress the generation of background points; applying a multi-head attention mechanism during the shapeEncode stage to effectively encode object shape information; and using a channel attention mechanism to fuse candidate features and shape features, thereby generating higher-quality candidate points. Extensive experiments were conducted on authoritative datasets such as ScanNet V2 and SUN RGB-D. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods on multiple benchmark datasets, fully validating the effectiveness of this framework in 3D point cloud object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Simplified-Pix2Seq: A Simple Language Modeling Framework for Vehicle detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the development of intelligent transportation systems and the rise of autonomous driving, vehicle detection and classification have become increasingly important. Although Transformer-based object detection models[1] have achieved high accuracy, existing methods are often complex and rely on large-scale datasets, making them unsuitable for fast and efficient traffic scene detection. In this paper, we propose an improved Simplified-Pix2Seq model based on Google’s Pix2Seq [2], a simple, effective end-to-end detection framework—applied to vehicle detection and type recognition in traffic scenes. Experimental results show that the model maintains a balance between detection accuracy and speed while keeping low complexity, effectively addressing detection challenges in traffic scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Tobacco Leaf Color Classification Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Objective: This study explores the application of machine learning algorithms in tobacco leaf color classification to improve classification accuracy.Methods: Images of tobacco leaves of different grades were collected, and RGB color data was extracted. Six machine learning algorithms were employed for classification prediction, and the best algorithm and features were optimized.Results: After denoising, algorithm optimization, and feature introduction, the classification accuracy of the random forest algorithm improved from 75% to 90.77%.Conclusion: Machine learning effectively achieves automatic classification of tobacco leaf colors, with data quality, algorithm selection, and feature engineering significantly impacting model performance. This research provides technical support for intelligent grading of tobacco leaves, though attention must be given to the model's generalization ability and processing speed.

articleTitle: Accurate Detection of Pine Wood Nematode Disease Based on Deep Learning Model and UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Detecting pine wood nematode disease (PWD) in complex environments is challenging for forest managers. To address this, we develop an improved Faster R-CNN model called FRBG Faster R-CNN. Our model combines ResNet50 network, FRN normalization layer and the activation function TLU to improve the feature expression ability of Faster R-CNN backbone network. Additionally, we construct a bi-directional path aggregation network (BiPAN) to fuse the context information and design a receptive field augmentation module (GPC) to enhance the detection ability for the small targets. The proposed FRBG Faster R-CNN is demonstrated on self-established multi-size MS_PWD dataset. In this dataset, collected UAV images come from heights of 60m, 100m, and 220m. Eight data augmentation methods are applied to simulate PWD diversity and complex lighting conditions. Our model achieves 95.6% accuracy, outperforming Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8 at all tested heights.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Detection Method of Orbital Foreign Bodies in YOLOv10
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the issues of low accuracy, low efficiency and misdetection existing in current orbital foreign object detection methods, an enhanced YOLOv10 orbital foreign object detection approach was proposed, and a lightweight model for the improved YOLOv10 orbital foreign object detection was constructed. Firstly, the EMA attention mechanism was incorporated into the C2f and C2fCIB modules of the YOLOv10 backbone network to enhance the capture of spatial information at different scales and strengthen the model's ability to express multi-scale features. Finally, cross-scale horizontal jump connection combined with weighted feature fusion was introduced in the neck layer to optimize the feature fusion structure and reinforce the multi-scale feature fusion capability. The proposed model's mAP@0.5 can reach 97.4%, which is 3.1% higher than that of YOLOv10. Additionally, the frame rate, parameter number, computational effort and model volume of the model detection are also superior to those of most mainstream target detection algorithms. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model can effectively enhance the detection accuracy of orbital foreign bodies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Posture Estimation for Archery Consistency Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Consistency in archer’s posture is crucial to retain high precision and high reproducibility in the shooting movement. The current practice in measuring postural consistency is often limited to human visual inspection with biases and subjectivity. First, a camera is used to capture body posture of archer during anchoring. A series of body posture images are subsequently processed with a deep learning pose estimation model with the extraction of keypoints. The selection of joints keypoints for archery are grouped for postural consistency study during anchoring phase. This paper presents a study between the postural consistency and scoring performance using an automated posture estimation mechanism. The study consists of nineteen elite archers performing ten shots in every session. The posture of each session is recorded to study their joint profile and consistency. It shows that the consistency measures are correlated with the joint profiles. The measure of joint profile and consistency can help coaches and athletes in assessing and improving performance with their training strategy.

articleTitle: CFAF-YOLOv8pose: Improved YOLOv8pose with Channel Feature Aggregation and Asymptotic Feature Fusion for Multi-person Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In computer vision research, the task of human pose estimation has been widely concerned. However, the problems of multi-person occlusion and complex motion pose in complex scenes bring great obstacles to pose estimation. Therefore, we propose a CFAF-YOLOv8pose architecture based on channel feature aggregation and asymptotic feature fusion to solve these problems. Specifically, we propose to adopt the Asymptotic Feature Fusion Module (AFF) to enable the model to retain rich semantic information during human pose feature extraction, while capturing detailed information from a lower level. Furthermore, we propose a Channel Feature Aggregation Module (CFA-OSA), which aggregates the key channel feature information extracted by the multi-branch topology network with the channel attention at one time, so that the model can realize the information flow between channel features, and at the same time improve the ability to extract channel feature information, so as to improve the accuracy of key point detection. Our method has achieved competitive results on both the self-built motion dataset and the public dataset OCHuman. Compared with the baseline YOLOv8spose, CFAF-YOLOv8pos achieves improvements of 4.5% in , 2.2% in , and 2.3% in , showing better performance.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Foreign Object Detection Network Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low accuracy and poor robustness of transmission line foreign object detection in complex environments, a transmission line foreign object detection algorithm based on YOLOv8 is proposed. First replace the standard convolution in the backbone of YOLOv8n with a sensory wild attention convolution that incorporates SE attention, and embed it into the C2f module to construct a new lightweight backbone network; Secondly, a double-layer routing attention mechanism is added to the neck to improve the accuracy of recognizing small foreign objects; Finally, Shape-IoU is introduced to improve the regression rate and accuracy of the boundaries. Experiments based on the foreign object dataset expanded by Poisson mixing and geometric data enhancement methods show that the improved YOLOv8-CBS has an average accuracy of 92.1%, an accuracy of 94.6%, and a detection speed of 156 f/s, which are 3.5%, 4.3%, and 11.0%, respectively, compared to the baseline model, and the model volume is only 3.2 MB.

articleTitle: Salt-Pepper Noise Removal Approach Based on ANN and Directional Mean Filtering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To preserve the image details more precisely and fully after image filtering, a directional mean filtering algorithm based on the edge direction of noise points is proposed. Firstly, pepper and salt noise recognizer model based on single hidden layer neural network is established. Afterwards, pepper and salt noise recognizer is trained to detect noise points, respectively. Then, according to the neighborhood pixel value of the noise point, the direction with the smallest pixel difference is regarded as the edge direction. Finally, the pixel value of the noise point is replaced by the average value of the pixel in the edge direction. The experimental results indicates that the filtering effect of the algorithm is superior to other algorithms on low and medium noise concentrations, with a PSNR value up to 82.0dB. While for the high concentration of noise, the PSNR value and consumed computational time are less than 3.2dB and 3.91s, respectively. According to the experimental results, the proposed algorithm provides a better capability of filtering and displaying detailed information of the image, and significant guidance on promoting the construction of the energy Internet and digital grid.

articleTitle: Difficulty Prediction and Individualized Matching AKT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Knowledge Tracing is a crucial task in the domain of intelligent tutoring systems, which aims to predict a student's future performance based on their past records. However, existing research fails to explicitly model the relationship between question difficulty and response prediction tasks and lack a clear modeling of individualized student features. This paper addresses these shortcomings by introducing the Difficulty Prediction and Individualized Matching AKT (DPIM-AKT) model, aimed at effectively leveraging information about question difficulty and uncovering personalized student characteristics.
