Specifically, we propose the Question Difficulty Prediction (DP) task to predict the difficulty of questions, enhancing the learning of question representations. We propose the Individualized Knowledge State Matching (IM) task to explicitly extract personalized features from a student's history of responses. By mining individualized patterns in a student's performance, our model achieves a more nuanced understanding of each student's learning style. Extensive experiments conducted on three real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of DPIM-AKT over current state-of-the-art Knowledge Tracing models. Notably, DPIM-AKT also exhibits superior interpretability.

articleTitle: Automatic Measurement Method of Pig Body Size Based on Improved Point Transformer Segmentation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: At present, most of the non-contact body size measurement methods based on the complete point cloud of pigs are complex and susceptible to interference from other parts of the point cloud when selecting key points. Therefore, this paper proposes an automatic measurement method of pig body size based on improved Point Transformer point cloud segmentation network. Firstly, a point cloud acquisition channel for pigs was built to collect point clouds on the left and right sides of 56 Yorkshire pigs aged 80-110 days. Secondly, the point cloud is preprocessed to remove the noise outside the pig point cloud, and the pig point cloud segmentation data set including head, chest, abdomen, buttocks and tail is constructed. Then, based on the Point Transformer, the adaptive convolution (AdaptConv) is introduced into the upsampling module, and the ACPT network is proposed for pig point cloud segmentation by combining the offset attention mechanism and the Focal loss function. Finally, the key points of the five-part segmentation part of the pig are found for body size measurement. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the improved segmentation network is 88.5 %, which is 5.5 % higher than that of the original network and better than other networks. The absolute error between the automatic measurement results and the measured values was within 4.8 cm, and the average relative error was within 5.1 %. The research shows that this method improves the measurement accuracy and has a better application prospect in non-contact body measurement.

articleTitle: MTP: A Minimal Task Perturbation Framework for Mitigating Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Federated Learning achieves privacy protection by allowing different participants to jointly train models. However, this characteristic also makes Federated Learning susceptible to data poisoning attacks. Many existing defense methods can successfully defend against various data poisoning attacks, but they are often only effective against one of the independent and identically distributed (IID) or non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel minimal task perturbation framework named MTP for mitigating data poisoning attacks in both IID and non-IID scenarios. To efficiently identify potential attackers, MTP utilizes a weight similarity ensemble mechanism based on four distance algorithms and clusters clients according to the fused weight similarity. Moreover, MTP uses a clipped weight aggregation to minimize the impact on the performance of main task. Experimental results show that the proposed MTP outperforms state-of-the-art methods in stability and security, and maintain higher accuracy of the main task.

articleTitle: Research on Text Detection Algorithm for Work Ticket Images Based on Feature Enhancement and Multi Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The images of construction work receipts are filled with various noises, such as stains, scratches, handwritten handwriting, and seal images, which result in poor performance of traditional text detection methods. This article proposes a text detection method based on efficient feature enhancement and multi-scale feature fusion to address this issue. By integrating an efficient segmentation module and a learnable post-processing method, the performance of the detection method is enhanced by using the visual language pre training model oCLIP. The segmentation module adopts image segmentation method for text detection of construction work ticket images, including an efficient feature enhancement module and a multi-scale feature fusion, which together constitute the key components of the segmentation module. Experimental results have shown that the model achieves good text detection performance in low resolution and high noise work order images.

articleTitle: Research on Infrared Sequence Image Processing Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In response to the problems of low resolution, severe shaking, and blurred contours in infrared imaging of unmanned mobile platforms, the collected dynamic infrared sequence images were subjected to image enhancement processing in the spatial domain. The results showed that traditional spatial domain image enhancement methods had poor performance; Subsequently, based on the two-dimensional wavelet function, the infrared image is subjected to wavelet decomposition, and the wavelet coefficients obtained from the decomposition are analyzed; Based on the requirements of infrared image processing on mobile platforms, an adaptive segmented approach is adopted to enhance low-frequency coefficients and weaken high-frequency coefficients to enhance the acquisition of dynamic infrared sequence images. The results showed that the processed image had clearer contours and well preserved details, increasing the recognition of infrared images of unmanned mobile platforms effectively.

articleTitle: Eye Movement Analysis using Virtual Reality in Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Early detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is important at the initial stage to provide prior treatment and control. In traditional diagnostic methods, medical doctors perform manual AD checking by asking patients to repeat several round of text reading and game exercises. The quantification of this manual assessment can be subjective due to the profession experience and it requires a further verification using the brain imaging. In this paper, an automated digital AD assessment method using Virtual Reality (VR) console is proposed to evaluate patient’s condition by tracking their eye movement during text reading. First, the eye movement pattern is captured using VR console during text reading. The recorded eye movement is then converted into frequency domain to study its frequency components during reading process. The simulation of AD symptom is set up by prompting subjects to read their familiar native language and unfamiliar language. As a result, the experiment shows that there are significant differences in eye movement patterns between native and unfamiliar language reading. The group of subjects reading unfamiliar language have random eye movement in less efficient visual processing. This pattern is similar to the patients who suffer in the AD symptom. In addition, the frequency features are extracted to study its correlations with reading comprehension performance in order to detect the early AD condition.

articleTitle: Intelligent Leakage Inspection Method of Magnetic Mill Workshop based on Lightweight Yolov5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the process of mining company beneficiation, large rotating equipment, pipelines and electrical equipment have many complex inspection areas and diverse inspection contents. The lack of intelligent solutions to the problem of pipeline leakage will cause serious consequences such as equipment shutdown if it is not found in time. This paper proposes a lightweight yolov5 intelligent leakage inspection method for the magnetic mill workshop. The inspection robot is used to continuously collect images of possible leakage points and transmit them to the background server. The improved yolov5 algorithm simplifies the model structure and realizes rapid and accurate identification of leakage targets with limited computing resources. The computational efficiency is increased by 44.98% with almost no loss of model accuracy. The mAP_0.5 of identifying large targets at leakage points reaches 97.96%.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction Study of MOSFET Device Based on Optimized Neural Network on Spark Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Accurately predicting the aging failure time of MOSFET (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor) devices is of great significance to the health management of electronic components. In order to solve the problems of declining prediction accuracy and long algorithm running time during long-term prediction of MOSFET devices, this paper uses particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize the neural network of bidirectional gated recurrent unit combined with self-attention mechanism, and builds a Spark platform for data processing and parallel computing. The MOSFET thermal aging dataset disclosed by NASA Research Center is used for experiments to compare the model proposed in this paper with other models, and the experiments prove that the algorithm optimized by particle swarm has higher fitting superiority and prediction accuracy, and the relative errors of different prediction starting points are all less than 3%, and the parallel performance study of different cluster nodes is carried out in the Yarn environment, which verifies the advantages of the parallel computing performance of Spark. Parallel computing performance advantage, the method proposed in this paper can realize the long-term prediction of the failure of MOSFET devices with effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Handwritten Marking Localization Method for Hot Rolled Steel Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the handwritten markings of steel coils in the natural scenario of hot rolled steel coils warehouse in the travelling link using the existing text localization method have serious distortion and blurring, thus leading to a high leakage rate, a precise localization method for the handwritten markings of hot rolled steel coils is proposed. The method is based on Nanodet-m improved Coord-Nano steel coil handwritten labeling localization model. First, the backbone network perceives the spatial information of the feature map by introducing CoordConv and SAConc, which improves the adaptability and accuracy of the network in dealing with features of different scales and complexities. Then, the PfAAMLayer attention mechanism is introduced to produce a self-focusing effect on the features, which improves the architectural performance. Finally, the bottom-up path enhancement module is utilized to propagate the strong localization features in the shallow network to the deep network, so as to accurately locate the handwritten marking region of the steel roll from the complex environment. Experimental results show that the network model proposed in this paper achieves 97.7% localization accuracy for steel roll handwritten markers by training and validation on real steel roll handwritten markers image dataset.Compared with the basic Nanodet-m, YOLOv7tiny and YOLOv8n, the localization accuracy of handwritten marks on steel rolls is improved by 1.6%, 0.8% and 0.2%.

articleTitle: Light Teacher: Lightweight Semi-supervised Object Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A two-stage semi-supervised object detection algorithm based on the ResNet-50 backbone, featuring efficient feature extraction capabilities and excellent accuracy performance. However, this network still faces issues in practical applications, such as high computational costs and low-quality pseudo-labels. To address this, a more lightweight yet high-performance semi-supervised object detection algorithm, called Light Teacher, is proposed. Firstly, a lightweight backbone network, MobileECANet, is designed to reduce the model’s computational load and accelerate its running speed while ensuring accuracy. Secondly, a Context Adaptive Feature Pyramid Network (CAF-FPN) is designed as the feature extraction network to further harness rich contextual information and suppress inconsistencies across different scales. Finally, the Confluence method is employed to replace non-maximum suppression, which not only helps reduce false positives and missed detections in pseudo-labels but also simplifies the post-processing workflow. Experimental results show that under conditions using only 10% labeled data from the COCO dataset and on the VOC dataset, the proposed Light Teacher model improves accuracy by 1.35% and 1.53%, respectively, compared to the original Mean Teacher model.

articleTitle: Joint Adversarial Defense Based on Gradient Regularization Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to solve the adversarial defense issue for image classification, several researches have suggested different strategies to improve the robustness of neural networks. However, these techniques encounter challenges such as insufficient adaptability to sophisticated attacks and high computational overhead. In this work, we propose JGRD to employ gradient regularization and defense distillation strategies to improve the robustness against imperceptible perturbations. Furthermore, we jointly train the projection gradient descent strategy and class-specific maximization strategy to improve the accuracy on sophisticated adversarial samples and reduce the time cost of adversarial training. Experiments on the Cifar10 show that JGRD not only outperforms baselines, but also reduces the time cost of adversarial training.

articleTitle: Research on Sentiment Analysis of Ceramic Review Texts Based on BERT-BiGRU-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of product reviews can help both e-commerce shoppers and merchants make better decisions and promote products more effectively. However, existing sentiment analysis models that rely on word embeddings often overlook contextual relationships within sentences, and they face challenges such as metaphorical expressions and semantic variation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a feature fusion framework based on Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). The framework first uses BERT to pre-train the text and generate rich, dynamic word embeddings. A Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) is then applied to capture contextual features, while an attention mechanism is introduced to highlight key features. Experiments on a ceramic dataset demonstrate that the BERT-BiGRU-Attention-based sentiment analysis model significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, F1-score, and other evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Incremental Learning Model Based on Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Currently, deep learning neural networks have shown remarkable performance in the field of image classification. However, existing classification networks are typically applied within closed environments, where all collected samples are batch-trained to produce classification results. In practical applications, the categories of samples are not static but dynamically increase over time. With the continual addition of new classes, the current classification methods exhibit limited continual learning capabilities, making them unsuitable for applications with stringent real-time requirements. To address this issue, this paper investigates an incremental learning algorithm based on ensemble transfer learning to handle classification training for newly added categories. This algorithm leverages the strengths of ensemble transfer learning to enhance the network's ability to continually learn new categories, enabling fast and accurate classification of new samples. In this paper, the proposed algorithm is applied to the CUB-200-2011 dataset for class-incremental experiments and compared with other deep learning models. Experimental results demonstrate that the incremental learning classification algorithm based on integrated transfer outperforms other models.

articleTitle: Fast Correction and Stitching Algorithm for Fisheye Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Fisheye cameras, with their ultra-wide-angle field of view, can capture a larger scene in a single shot compared to traditional lenses. This capability makes them highly valuable in areas such as security surveillance, panoramic photography, autonomous driving, and robot navigation. However, building an efficient and accurate visual system is crucial for realizing these applications. This paper proposes an improved algorithm based on fisheye image correction and stitching. First, a fast fisheye image distortion correction method is introduced to eliminate the severe distortion caused by the fisheye lens. Then, the o-FAST algorithm is used for feature point detection, ensuring rotational invariance of the feature points, and the KNN algorithm is employed for initial matching. On this basis, the PROSAC algorithm is applied to remove incorrect matches and compute the homography matrix between images. Finally, seamless image stitching is achieved using a gradual weighted fusion method. The research results demonstrate that this method significantly improves both image quality and computational efficiency, making it effective for generating and processing panoramic images. Experimental results further confirm that the method enhances stitching accuracy while also increasing processing speed, showcasing its high practical value.

articleTitle: Research on Abnormal Lung Sound Recognition Method Based on S-ECA-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Respiratory diseases and traumatic infections are generally accompanied by lung infections. Lung sounds can effectively determine the pulmonary infection level. At present, the lung sound judgment is completed by professional physicians through auscultation. Real-Time detection and assessment of lung sounds in infected individuals represent a crucial clinical challenge. To address this issue, an abnormal lung sound recognition method based on S-ECA-Transformer was studied. The primary research components are as follows: Firstly, a real-time lung sound acquisition system was designed to collect lung sound data of different infection levels. Under the professional physician guidance, the collected lung sounds were annotated to establish a feature dataset (primary care, secondary care, tertiary care, healthy states). Secondly, the lung sound denoising algorithm based on Butterworth filter and wavelet decomposition was studied, the Mel spectrum feature information of lung sound was extracted after denoising. Finally, the improved channel attention mechanism ECA-NET was introduced, and the optimized CNN model was combined with the Transform-Er model to propose the S-ECA-Transformer classification model. This model combined the strengths of CNN spatial features and Transformer sequence coding, providing global feature perception and local feature extraction capabilities. Experiments show that the algorithm achieves 94.5 %, 94.5 %, 94.5 % and 0.94 in recognition accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score respectively. Compared with other deep learning models, this algorithm can effectively identify abnormal lung sounds and determine the infection level.

articleTitle: Improving Particle Swarm Optimization-Based Fuzzy PI Control for Photovoltaic Grid-Connected Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the issue of poor dynamic performance in the fuzzy Proportional-Integral (PI) control of photovoltaic (PV) three-phase grid-tie inverters, an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) based fuzzy PI control strategy is proposed. A mathematical model of the three-phase grid-tie inverter is established, and a dual closed-loop control system for the grid-tie inverter is designed based on this model. Fuzzy control is introduced into the outer voltage loop to adjust the PI parameters in real-time. The improved particle swarm algorithm is employed to optimize the quantization and scaling factors in the fuzzy PI control, enhancing the system's control performance. Simulations conducted on the MATLAB/Simulink platform, compared with fuzzy PI control, demonstrate that this method improves the dynamic process of grid-tie control in PV systems, ultimately achieving smooth grid-tie for the PV system.

articleTitle: A Contrastive-Representative-Learning-Based Method for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Time series anomaly detection is extremely important in many fields. Using a series of observation data recorded at a certain time interval can detect deviations from normal behavior in a timely and effective manner. Transformer-based time series anomaly detection methods perform very well due to their self-attentive mechanism that can capture long-range dependencies in time series, but when there are complex patterns in the data, reconstruction alone may not capture enough information. In this paper, we propose a contrastive representation learning model that utilizes a novel complementary mask design to generate augmented views, constructs pairs of positive and negative samples, and learns the similarity between them, enabling the model to learn representations that distinguish between normal and abnormal data. We use a joint training optimization method of contrastive loss and reconstruction loss to enable the model to maintain a high detection accuracy even in the face of unseen abnormal patterns, thus greatly enhancing the performance and generalization ability of the model. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the model attains leading results across various benchmark datasets for time series anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Stereo Image Fusion Based on Dome
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The dome system is capable of providing an all-around immersive visual experience and has been widely applied in various fields such as entertainment, education, scientific research, and more. This paper investigates the implementation method of stereo image fusion technology within the dome system, and resolves issues such as image chromatic aberration and tearing through signal frame synchronization and image frame synchronization. Practical verification has demonstrated that this research can create an immersive virtual reality environment, significantly enhancing the sense of stereo and immersion of the dome system, thereby enabling a more realistic and awe-inspiring visual experience.

articleTitle: Object Detection Algorithm for UAV Aerial Images Based on UAV-YOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Current methodologies face significant challenges in the detection of small objects within UAV aerial images, which often encompass a diverse array of complex morphologies. To tackle the issues of leakage and false positives in the context of small object detection, we propose an enhanced model called UAV-YOLO based on the YOLOv7 framework. First, we introduce an advanced MFE module, which is specifically designed to extract a more nuanced and comprehensive set of feature information. Second, we propose a multi-feature detection head, which is architected to augment the model's discriminative capacity for the perception of minute objects, thereby enhancing overall detection accuracy. Finally, the introduction of SIOU loss function enhances the regression capability of bounding box. We test the proposed model on the VisDrone2019 dataset and the UAVDT dataset containing UAV aerial images, and the empirical results reveal that our method achieves a significantly superior mean average precision (mAP) when contrasted with the performance of the predominant algorithms in the field. This enhancement successfully mitigates the occurrence of leakage and false positives for small objects within aerial imagery captured by UAVs.

articleTitle: Capsule Network for Pneumonia Classification: Enhancing Robustness and Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Pneumonia is a severe global health threat, causing around 4 million deaths per year. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and reducing mortality rates. This study introduces a deep learning model called Capsule Networks (CapsNet) for classifying pneumonia, which can capture complex spatial relationships in chest X- ray (CXR) images. We utilized a dataset from Guangzhou Women and Children’s Medical Center, which was processed through SMOTE techniques before training the model. In order to mimic the distortions that may occur when images are transmitted in real-life scenarios, we applied rotations and flips to the images in the test set to compare and verify the robustness of CapsNet. The results showed that CapsNet achieved an accuracy rate of 89.58% and 87.02% before and after test set distortion, demonstrating good robustness. In terms of evaluation metrics, CapsNet outperformed other models like ResNet, Xception, and ViT.

articleTitle: Oil Spill Detection in PolSAR Imagery Using Multi-Scale Hybrid Feature Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The issue of marine oil spills is receiving increasing attention, and polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) is an effective tool for detecting oil spills by distinguishing the backscatter differences between seawater and oil slicks. However, the inaccurate delineation of oil-water boundaries remains a challenge when using polarization features for oil spill detection. To address these challenges, we propose an oil spill detection framework based on Multi-Scale Hybrid Feature Fusion Network (MSHFFNet). This method combines polarization intensity information with the mixing pool module and feature fusion module to establish short-range and long-range connections between features of various sizes. This method enriches edge and semantic information by effectively utilizing contextual and detail information, significantly improving the recognition accuracy of oil-water boundaries. The experimental verification of Radarsat-2 fully polarized SAR data confirms the effectiveness of our method in improving boundary accuracy. Evaluation metrics including F1 and mIoU indicate that MSHFFNet surpasses two state-of-the-art methods and significantly improves the accuracy of oil spill detection.

articleTitle: Human Pose Estimation Based on Data Augmentation and Contextual Relation Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Human pose estimation is a critical research area in computer vision, aiming to predict key points' spatial coordinates in images. This paper introduces a novel network for human pose estimation that addresses performance issues caused by occlusion. To combat overfitting, we use data augmentation techniques like joint occlusion and instance pasting. We also propose a Contextual Relation Attention Module (CRAM) to enhance focus on important features, reduce background noise interference, and improve accuracy by handling limb occlusion challenges. Additionally, we incorporate a Transformer for inference to predict occluded joint positions more accurately by learning long-range dependencies between joints. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method over existing approaches.

articleTitle: Ordinary Tea Shoot Detection under Different Lighting Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Tea shoot detection is a crucial step in the automating tea plucking. Tea shoot detection needs to take into account changing light conditions due to unstable outdoor environments. To this end, an ordinary tea shoot detection algorithm under different lighting conditions based on super-green features and threshold segmentation is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the color features of tea shoots were analyzed, and the tea shoot regions was highlighted by the super-green feature index. Next, the tea canopy images were divided into low-light and highlight images based on the average grayscale, and the detection algorithm was performed separately. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in detecting tea shoots under different lighting conditions.

articleTitle: Multi-Network Stacking Architecture for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection in Magnetic Resonance Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Brain tumors present a significant health challenge, making accurate detection and classification via MRI essential for effective diagnosis and treatment. This paper explores a stacking ensemble of 16 neural networks to enhance classification performance across 16 tumor classes, aggregating outputs through maximum selection, averaging, and top-k methods to create a robust feature matrix. We evaluated two meta-classifiers, Random Forest and XGBoost, on these aggregated features, revealing improved classification accuracy. Additionally, we developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as an alternative meta-classifier, which achieved 100.00% accuracy on a test dataset of 460 images, demonstrating its effectiveness in synthesizing base model outputs. Overall, this research highlights the potential of stacking ensembles and neural network architectures to advance MRI-based brain tumor classification, contributing to more accurate and efficient clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Research on Image Sentiment Analysis Based on Feature Pyramid and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of images allows for a deeper understanding of the information conveyed by the images, better meeting people's needs in visual content comprehension and interaction. This paper proposes a model that integrates ResNet50 with a feature pyramid and attention mechanism. The model first improves upon the traditional ResNet50 by incorporating a feature pyramid module, which integrates multi-scale feature maps and enhances the accuracy of image sentiment analysis. Then, the CBAM attention module is introduced to enhance attention to key features. The model integrates both channel and spatial attention mechanisms to effectively capture key channel and spatial details in images. The proposed image sentiment analysis model, which incorporates feature pyramids and attention mechanisms, demonstrates high accuracy and reliability in feature extraction and sentiment analysis tasks.

articleTitle: A Sparse Channel Attention Model using 3D Mel-spectrograms for Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition has important applications in both military and civilian fields. However, the complexity of the underwater environment and the multipath nature of the acoustic channel pose great challenges to underwater acoustic target recognition. In this paper, we propose a sparse channel attention (SCA) model using 3D Mel-spectrograms for underwater acoustic target recognition. For feature extraction, we combine Mel-spectrograms features, Delta features and Delta-delta features to construct 3D Mel-spectrograms features. For model recognition, we propose a SCA model, which not only combines convolutional features to capture both local and global information in the spectrogram. Moreover, the sparse channel attention mechanism is adopted, which significantly reduces the computational complexity. The effectiveness of the method is verified by comparing the ablation experiments on the ShipsEar dataset. The experimental results show that SCA outperforms other recognition models with low computational complexity and achieving 98.66% recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Cyclic Angle Encoding and Angle-Embedded Attention for Robust Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Rotated object detection in remote sensing images is crucial for various applications, including surveillance, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. However, this task is challenging due to the diverse orientations and scales of objects, as well as the complex background in aerial images. Traditional regression-based methods often suffer from boundary issues, leading to significant loss values and reduced detection accuracy. To address these challenges, we introduces a novel method for oriented object detection. We propose a cyclic angle encoding approach that converts angle prediction from a regression problem to a classification problem, effectively mitigating boundary issues and improving angle prediction accuracy. Additionally, we introduce an embedded angle information deformable attention mechanism to better align features with sampling points, enhancing the model's performance in rotated object detection tasks. Experiments on the DOTA-v1.0 dataset, a large-scale aerial image dataset, demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Our approach achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 80.98%, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our method achieves a precision of 90.70% in the aircraft category and shows robust performance across various categories and challenging scenarios. The proposed innovations in angle encoding and attention mechanism significantly improve detection accuracy and model robustness.

articleTitle: An Efficient And Precise Fire Detection Model Based on Improved RT-DETR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: For fires, especially urban fires, early warning is crucial and can significantly reduce the loss of life and property among affected populations. Traditional fire detection algorithms suffer from issues such as missed detection, false detection, and inadequate real-time performance. Moreover, the scarcity of high-quality fire detection datasets severely limits the performance of these algorithms. To address these challenges, this paper presents a dual-pronged approach. On one hand, we develop the CFS fire dataset for model training. On the other hand, we propose a detection model called FDC-DETR, which based on improved RT-DETR architecture for detecting flames and smoke in complex environment. It incorporates Fasternet_Rep backbone, reconstruction of the Cross-Scale Feature Fusion Module(CCFM) component, Deformable Attention and WIoUv3 loss function. Experiments demonstrate that the detection model achieves an average precision (mAP) of 89.6% on the self-generated fire dataset. Compared to the original RT-DETR network, the model has reduced its parameters by 27.1%, increased accuracy by 2.7%, and improved average precision by 5.7%, without significant decrease in detection speed. These enhancements meet the requirements for practical security applications in fire detection.

articleTitle: Boosting the Transferability of Adversarial Examples with Dynamic Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to adversarial examples, which subtly alter benign images to mislead predictions. While white-box attacks are highly effective, black-box attacks suffer from limited transferability. To improve transferability, this paper introduces a dynamic gradient attack (DGA) that adaptively adjusts the update gradient by leveraging local data information. This approach, coupled with a smaller step size, stabilizes the optimization, reduces divergence risks, and enhances convergence smoothness. Experimental results on the ImageNet dataset show that DGA significantly outperforms existing gradient-based attacks in both standard and adversarially trained models.

articleTitle: Characterization on Imaging Properties of Optical Fiber Array Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The imaging qualities of optical fiber array were discussed in this paper by characterization with various self-developed instruments based on machine vision. The basic processes include extracting clear image transmitted by optical fiber array, transferring the extracted image to the calculation unit, processing it by digital methods such as gray value and binary system. And then the size, shape and color of defects will be judged according to the distribution, brightness and color of pixels. In combination with the standard for controlling various defects of optical fiber array, the characterization results will be further calculated and judged and finally output. The fiber-optic imaging element defect detection device is to detect and analyze dots, chicken wire and grids. The contrast ratio detection device is to measure the crosstalk among optical fibers within optical fiber array. Meanwhile, the imaging evenness could also be characterized by achieving the transmittance differences between periphery and central zone. The reproductivity reaches above 97%. The relative transmittance tester is to measure the relative transmittance located at any positions and compare the evenness among different locations. The precision reaches microscale. An automatic detector recently developed by our team is to detect scratches on sample surface with measurement accuracy exceeding 99%, solving the great challenge. It is because of application of machine vision that the corresponding characterization methods and equipment are innovated. This promotes the realization of digital, intelligent, automated and high précised characterization.

articleTitle: Contrastive Swin-UNet for Unpaired Image-to-Image Scene Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Unpaired image-to-image translation is a challenging task that requires mapping between source and target domains without paired examples. Conventional approaches rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and their variants to achieve reliable translation results. However, in applications where structural consistency is key, CNN-based models are unable to capture global and long-range dependencies. In this paper, we introduce Contrastive Swin-UNet, a framework that leverages contrastive learning with shifted window self-attention mechanism, structured in U-shaped encoder-decoder network. Our approach employs a fully transformer-based generation for effective local and global feature learning. Taking advantage of self-attention, we show that integrated contrastive loss significantly improves translation consistency and generative fidelity by maximizing mutual information between source image and translated output. Our findings indicate that Contrastive Swin-UNet sets a new benchmark for unpaired image-to-image translation tasks, particularly in scenarios requiring high precision and regularity.

articleTitle: ITH: Improved TopHat for Smear Suppression in Astronomical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: CCD-based detectors are widely used in astronomical observations, but non-instantaneous charge transfer can cause bright lines known as smear. This phenomenon affects both normal astronomical observations and subsequent image processing. Although TopHat-based methods can suppress most smears, they also distort the original distribution of bright sources. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage desmearing method. First, an improved TopHat (ITH) filter is designed for rough smear suppression. Then, a residue search and removal channel is employed to enhance visual performance. Experimental results on actual smeared images demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional approaches.

articleTitle: A Consolidated Volatility Prediction with Back Propagation Neural Network and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper provides a unique approach with AI algorithms to predict emerging stock markets volatility. Traditionally, stock volatility is derived from historical volatility, Monte Carlo simulation and implied volatility as well. In this paper, the writer designs a consolidated model with back -propagation neural network and genetic algorithm to predict future volatility of emerging stock markets and found that the results are quite accurate with low errors.

articleTitle: Multi-person Pose Estimation with Multi-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, multi-person pose estimation has emerged as a prominent research direction in the field of computer vision, holding significant importance in applications such as human-computer interaction, action analysis, and virtual reality. However, traditional methods are often complex and inefficient, particularly during the feature fusion process, which can lead to the loss of critical information and increased errors under occlusion and complex poses. To address this, multiple attention modules were introduced in the early stages of the network to enhance the modeling of dependencies between key points, ultimately overcoming the limitations of conventional heatmaps through a coordinate classification approach. The design utilizing multiple attention modules achieves a balance between maintaining a lightweight structure and improving accuracy. Furthermore, by introducing a multi-attention mechanism, information loss is reduced, thereby enhancing the model's robustness in handling occlusion and other challenges in complex scenarios. Compared to existing advanced methods, the approach presented in this paper achieves an average precision increase of 1.5 percentage points on the COCO dataset.

articleTitle: BOANN: Bayesian-Optimized Attentive Neural Network for Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study presents the Bayesian-Optimized Attentive Neural Network (BOANN), a novel approach enhancing image classification performance by integrating Bayesian optimization with channel and spatial attention mechanisms. Traditional image classification struggles with the extensive data in today's big data era. Bayesian optimization has been integrated into neural networks in recent years to enhance model generalization, while channel and spatial attention mechanisms improve feature extraction capabilities. This paper introduces a model combining Bayesian optimization with these attention mechanisms to boost image classification performance. Bayesian optimization optimizes hyperparameter selection, accelerating model convergence and accuracy; the attention mechanisms augment feature extraction. Compared to traditional deep learning models, our model utilizes attention mechanisms for initial feature extraction, followed by a Bayesian-optimized neural network. On the CIFAR-100 dataset, our model outperforms classical models in metrics such as accuracy, loss, precision, recall, and F1 score, achieving an accuracy of 77.6%. These technologies have potential for broader application in image classification and other computer vision domains.

articleTitle: Markerless Avatar Animation with Forward Kinematics using Depth Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Digital avatar is a graphical representation of a user in a virtual platform. To obtain an articulated and animated avatar, it is a labor-intensive job to perform pre- and post-processing for capturing body shapes and motions. The development of a markerless motion capture system has enabled the acquisition of body motion by eliminating marker attachments to the body. In this work, a markerless avatar rigging and animation pipeline is proposed. A deep learning-based rigging and skinning strategy is employed to automate the rigging process by estimating and aligning a virtual skeleton to the acquired 3D body shape and assigning the skin vertices to the skeleton. A depth sensor is used to capture the 3D pose by implementing a measurement-based approach. The performance measurement-based and estimation-based approaches are evaluated in term of motion capture. Subsequently, the motion of a user is streamed with the information of individual joint parameters, i.e. rotations in quaternion, to a web-based renderer for animation.

articleTitle: Low-light Image Enhancement Based on Conditional Generation Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Images taken in low-light environment generally suffer from issues such as high noise level, low contrast, and color distortion. These problems not only affect the visual quality of the image, but also hinder the completion of subsequent machine vision tasks. In this paper, we present a low-light image enhancement method based on conditional generation adversarial network. The network’s generator utilizes residual dense blocks coupled with channel attention mechanisms to boost feature extraction’s precision and swiftness. Residual dense blocks are employed to fortify feature propagation and reuse, whereas channel attention mechanisms selectively recalibrate channel weights, thereby enhancing the efficiency of image processing. Besides, we employ a PatchGAN architecture as the discriminator to assess image quality. For training optimization, we introduce a multi-module loss function that considers local texture, global content, structural clarity, content fidelity and color authenticity. The qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that our method balances processing time and effect, achieving tasks such as noise suppression, contrast enhancement, and color restoration.

articleTitle: MMFA-Net: Multi-Modal Feature Learning and Multi-Head Fuse Attention for Image Manipulation Detection and Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the advent of various advanced image processing techniques and the increasingly low manipulation threshold, Image Manipulation Detection and Localization (IMDL) has become a complex and challenging task. Previous studies have shown the importance of manipulation artifacts in the IMDL problem. However, existing methods often struggle to capture effective artifacts when addressing with refined forgery (post-processed forgery). In this paper, we introduce MMFA-Net, a novel approach for IMDL. We extract RGB features, Laplacian high-frequency features, Bayar statistical anomaly features, and manipulation imprint from the image through the Multi-modal Feature Extractor module, concatenating them as multi-modal feature inputs to capture manipulation edge artifacts, which are increasingly difficult to detect in image manipulation. In addition, we propose an innovative Multi-head Fuse Attention (MFA) module. Building on the backbone network's ability to model inconsistencies between original and tampered regions at coarse-to-fine granularities, the MFA module can more effectively capture contextual dependencies in the spatial dimensions and inter-channel correlations for more precise localization. The performance on several public datasets demonstrates that the proposed network outperforms existing SOTA models and remains robust against refined forgery.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Machine Learning in Visual Image Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, machine learning applications in visual design have become increasingly widespread, particularly in the field of image processing. This study presents an intelligent image generation platform based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) aimed at improving design efficiency and creative expression. The platform integrates Deep Convolutional GANs (DCGANs) with style transfer techniques to efficiently generate high-quality images with artistic and visual appeal. Experimental results demonstrate that the model outperforms traditional methods in terms of clarity (PSNR of 28.4 dB), realism (Inception Score of 7.5), and style consistency (Style Loss of 0.0025). User experience evaluations indicate that designers rate the platform highly for ease of use and image generation quality. This model not only enhances design efficiency but also serves as a powerful tool for creative visual tasks, advancing the automation and intelligence of the design process.

articleTitle: Adaptive Attention Context Network for Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Recently, deep convolutional neural networks provide an effective approach for polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images. However, most existing deep convolutional neural network-based methods tend to focus excessively on deep features, overlooking the shallow features that are crucial for accurately localizing small polyp targets, thus failing to achieve satisfactory segmentation performance. In this paper, we propose a novel Adaptive Attention Context Network (AACNet) that aims to automatically and robustly segment polyp lesions, with a specific emphasis on segmenting small polyp targets. Specifically, we introduce an Adaptive Hybrid Attention Module (AHAM) to replace traditional convolutional operations in the decoding stage. The module consists of a channel attention module and a spatial attention module, utilizing skip connections and upsampled feature maps as inputs. Compared to traditional convolutional operations, the AHAM adaptively selects more optimal segmentation results in both the channel and spatial dimensions, effectively preserving shallow features. To capture richer contextual information, AACNet incorporates a Context Extraction Module, which explores contextual information at each layer through global information compression and local information preservation. The results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing approaches in polyp segmentation, particularly for segmenting small polyp targets.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Iterative Diffusion Encryption Algorithm Based on Improved Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Chaotic systems are widely used in cryptography due to their traversability, unpredictability and sensitivity to initial values. However, the traditional low-dimensional chaotic system has the disadvantages of small key space, short iteration period and easy to be constructed, which affects the security of encryption. Therefore, in order to solve this problem, this paper constructs a new one-dimensional chaotic mapping, which is experimentally shown to have wider chaotic range, better unpredictability and larger key space. On this basis, this paper proposes an encryption scheme that can encrypt different images of different sizes by iteratively diffusing the pixels in both directions through chaotic sequences, and the experimental results show the security and effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Small Sea Suface Target Based on Lightweight Network Detection Model Research
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of high complexity and difficult deployment of sea surface ship model, a small target detection model based on YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed in this paper. In addition, Wise-IoU loss function is introduced, and Ghost convolution is used to replace the common convolution in the traditional algorithm. The experimental results on sea-ships data set show that compared with the original network, the detection accuracy is reduced by 1.3%, the number is reduced by 42.9%, and the floating point computation is reduced by 38.3%, which realizes the lightweight model.

articleTitle: Sea Ice Identification in Liaodong Bay Based on Semantic Segmentation and U-Net Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Liaodong Bay is one of the low-latitude ice-covered areas in China, where sea ice disasters occur frequently in winter. Accurate identification of sea ice is important for marine resource utilization and disaster prevention and mitigation. Currently, sea ice identification mostly utilizes traditional supervised classification, with cumbersome sampling steps and low identification accuracy. This article used Landsat 8-OLI images for creating the dataset, which includes 818 groups of data, of which 570 groups for the training set, 164 groups for the validation set, and 82 groups for the test set. Based on semantic segmentation with U-Net model, it achieved 92.77%, 93.03%, and 97.98% of accuracy, precision, and recall, respectively. On the testing set, the accuracy of this model is 91.67%, the precision is 92.09%, and the recall is 95.25%. Moreover, when the model was applied to identify the sea ice area in Liaodong Bay on January 19, 2018, the estimation results had small differences with the national published data. This study provides an important research idea for the identification and classification of sea ice, which can help to improve the accuracy and efficiency in the overall identification.

articleTitle: Enhancing Low-light Images Using a Coarse-to-fine Linear Mapping Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Conventional low-light image enhancement methods using linear mapping are simple but often result in poor visual quality due to their limited capability. While deep learning techniques have improved these outcomes, they usually depend on complex prior models, such as illumination and noise estimation. To address these challenges, we propose a new method that combines deep learning with traditional linear models, utilizing a coarse-to-fine linear mapping strategy. This approach avoids prior modeling and effectively tackles image degradation. Our experiments show that our model, guided by this strategy, is both simple and effective, and it competes well with existing deep-learning methods for low-light image enhancement.

articleTitle: Design of Flower Recognition System Based on PyTorch
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid growth of the Chinese economy and the improvement of living standards, flowers have become widely popular decorations and gifts. This design developed a flower recognition system founded on PyTorch to attain efficient and precise flower recognition. The Oxford-102 flower dataset offered by the University of Oxford was utilized for model training, which encompasses 102 categories of flower images, totaling 7,370 images. 88% of the images were chosen as the training set, while the remaining 12% were designated as the validation set. Image preprocessing and image enhancement techniques were employed to enhance the generalization capability of the model. A ResNet residual network was adopted to construct the classification model, and it was trained and verified using transfer learning approaches. The experimental outcomes demonstrated that the model achieved an accuracy rate of 93.41% in the flower recognition task, and API development was carried out to build a flower recognition system. This study indicates that machine vision technology can accomplish efficient and precise flower recognition, which will bring convenience to flower enthusiasts, gardeners, and even promote the development of the flower industry.

articleTitle: Classification of Students’ Classroom Learning States Based on Physiological Information and Classroom Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In classroom teaching, artificial intelligence technology can automate the analysis of students' classroom status. This enables teachers to efficiently and intuitively grasp students' responses to the classroom content and their level of understanding, thus enhancing the teaching program. Additionally, it can remind students to regulate their behavior in the classroom, ultimately aiding students in improving their learning performance. Currently, most research on students' learning status in the classroom relies on cameras, sometimes supplemented with other devices. However, this approach presents challenges such as complex equipment, limited recognition due to camera angles, and the inability to analyze the specificity of students' differences. This paper combines classroom behavior data with bracelet physiological data, which is convenient and enhances the comprehensiveness of the analysis simultaneously. The dataset on students' classroom status is established to serve as the foundation for the following research. The classification performance of KNN, RF, GBDT, and XGBoost is enhanced through Grid Search (GS). Furthermore, the XGBoost algorithm is further optimized using the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Experimental results demonstrate that the WOA-XGBoost algorithm chosen in this study can achieve an accuracy rate of 94.62%. This algorithm can significantly assist students in enhancing the quality of their classroom learning. Helping students improve the quality of classroom learning and assisting teachers in enhancing teaching programs.

articleTitle: Analysis of WeChat Mini Program Data Encryption Algorithm Based on Computer Network Security: AES Symmetric Encryption Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Computer network security is crucial to maintain system stability, ensure continuous business operation and prevent network attacks. With the continuous introduction of the Internet and WeChat, the number of WeChat applets continues to grow, and it is increasingly important to ensure the data security of WeChat applets. This article focuses on the research of AES data encryption algorithm, aiming to explore the overall process of its application in mini programs. By conducting process analysis, the superiority of AES data encryption algorithm in ensuring the security of WeChat mini program data is determined. This research result can provide valuable reference for decision-makers.

articleTitle: Multi-directional Local-Global feature Fusion Network for Building Segmentation in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing images can provide important information for building entity segmentation. However, the arbitrariness of building orientation makes it difficult to automatically segment buildings with high accuracy. Current algorithms mostly use horizontal strip convolution and vertical stripe convolution in the building extraction task, which is not sufficient to extract accurate boundary positioning information and complete footprints, especially in high-resolution images. In this article, we propose a novel Multi-directional Local-Global feature Fusion Network (MLGF-Net) based on multi-directional strip convolution. To better obtain edge localization information, we designed a multi-directional strip convolution joint module (MDSJ). This module extends the directionality of the extracted features to 0°, 45°, 90°, and 135° by parallel connection fusion so that the feature extraction capability of the model is enhanced. In addition, to improve the completeness of the building footprint, we proposed the local-global double-branch structure (LGS) module. These two branches are structured in parallel and utilize the self-attention mechanism to obtain more local-global information about the building. Extensive experiments on the Massachusetts dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Regression Prediction of Relative Separation Distance of Rockets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The assessment for the rocket separation process still stays in qualitative observation, and the research is based on the deep learning method to realize the relative separation distance regression prediction in the rocket separation process, and realize the shift from qualitative observation to quantitative assessment for the rocket separation process. Based on the data acquired from the rocket separation video and the separation stroke sensor, a deep regression neural network relying on the feature extraction capability of ResNet50 is constructed to learn the complex mapping relationship between the separation image features and the relative separation distance labels, in order to realize the accurate prediction of the relative separation distance of unfamiliar separation images. It is experimentally verified that the predicted separation distances are in good agreement with the measured values of the sensors (the average absolute error is 0.0404, the Pearson correlation coefficient is 0.9986, and the coefficient of determination is 0.9961), and the prediction results of the unfamiliar separation images show an average relative error of 11.97%, and the maximum relative error is 17.42%. The evaluation results show that the proposed method has good practicality for realizing the quantitative evaluation of the rocket separation process.

articleTitle: Road Trash Detection Algorithm of RT-DETR Integrated with State Space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As global urbanization progresses rapidly, the issue of urban road trash is becoming increasingly severe. Traditional manual cleaning methods are inefficient and struggle to meet the growing demand. This paper proposes an improved road trash detection algorithm based on RT-DETR (Real-Time Detection Transformer) and State Space Model (SSM) to enhance detection accuracy and robustness. The algorithm incorporates an innovative feature pyramid structure and a state-space-based internal scale feature enhancement module, effectively addressing object detection in complex scenes as well as challenges associated with occlusions and small object detection. We constructed a diverse urban road trash detection dataset comprising over 60,000 images, providing a solid foundation for the training and testing of the algorithm. Experimental results show that the proposed model improves the mean average precision (mAP) on the COCO dataset by 0.8 percentage points and achieves a 1.2 percentage point improvement on our custom road trash detection dataset, with a 2.1 percentage point increase in the precision of small object detection. The proposed algorithm achieves a favorable balance between real-time performance and accuracy, significantly enhancing trash detection in complex environments, particularly in terms of small object recognition and detection accuracy under occlusion conditions.

articleTitle: Tightly-coupled Lidar-Visual-Inertial SLAM for Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) enables robots to perform localization and mapping in unknown environments. Currently, mainstream single-sensor Lidar SLAM (Visual SLAM) tends to diverge and fail when faced with unstructured or textureless scenes. To address this issue, this paper proposes a robust tightly-coupled Lidar-Vision-Inertial Odometry framework (LRI-LVIO) that achieves high-precision and robust SLAM. LRI-LVIO consists of two subsystems: a visual-inertial system and a lidar-inertial system. These two subsystems are tightly coupled through an error-state iterative Kalman filter, allowing one subsystem to maintain stable operation even if the other fails, thus enhancing the robustness of SLAM in textureless and featureless environments. Additionally, the depth of visual feature points is recovered using lidar point cloud information, improving the algorithm's efficiency and accuracy. Finally, LRI-LVIO incorporates loop closure detection based on lidar point cloud keyframes, further reducing cumulative errors and enhancing localization precision. Experiments conducted in various indoor and outdoor environments show that by combining the advantages of each sensor, LRI-LVIO achieves higher accuracy and stronger robustness compared to single-sensor SLAM.

articleTitle: Research on Tea Bud Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The tea industry holds significant economic and social importance in China; however, traditional manual detection methods are inefficient and costly. To accurately estimate tea production and determine the optimal harvest time, this paper proposes a tea bud detection and counting model based on an improved YOLOv8. This model addresses the limitations of the YOLOv8 framework by adding deformable convolution modules to the backbone network, enhancing small object detection capabilities. It also integrates the CBAM attention module in the neck structure to focus on key features and replaces the original CIOU loss function with HIOU, dynamically adjusting component weights at different training stages. This adjustment allows small objects to regress more accurately to their true bounding boxes, further improving the detection accuracy of tender tea buds. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv8 model achieves higher precision and recall in tea bud detection tasks, demonstrating its superior performance. The outcomes of this research are of great significance for advancing intelligent harvesting and quality control in the tea production sector.

articleTitle: Adaptive Vehicle Recognition: Leveraging Channel Attention in InceptionV3 for Traffic Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: As traffic systems grow in complexity and vehicle numbers increase, traditional management methods struggle to meet real-time demands. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a solution by integrating information and communication technologies for efficient traffic flow monitoring. This paper presents an advanced vehicle classification model, based on the InceptionV3 architecture and enhanced by a channel attention mechanism, to address challenges in fine-grained vehicle recognition under varying conditions such as diverse lighting, multi-angle perspectives, and occlusions. Tested on a comprehensive vehicle dataset, the model achieved 97% classification accuracy, significantly surpassing baseline models. Key contributions include a refined vehicle classification model for ITS, enhanced strategies for handling occlusions and multi-angle scenarios, and robust experimental validation across classification metrics, providing a solid foundation for ITS-driven traffic optimization and safety management.

articleTitle: A Study of Lumbar Vertebral Body and Lumbar Disc Herniation Disease Detection Based on YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of diverse and complex structures of different tissues in lumbar spine MRI images. In this paper, an improved YOLOv8n lumbar spine and lumbar disc herniation detection method is proposed. The ODConv module is introduced in the backbone part to replace the traditional static convolution module to improve the feature extraction ability of the model; DySample is used to replace the nearest-neighbor interpolation upsampling to improve the ability of the model to convey semantic information to the feature maps; the LSK attention mechanism is used as a basic module and combined with ASFF to form LSK-ASFF, which is introduced into the multi-scale feature fusion structure of the network to realize the adaptive spatial feature fusion of different levels of features to improve the accuracy and generalization ability of the network. The experimental results show that the precision(P), F1 score and mAP of the improved YOLOv8n model in the lumbar MRI dataset reach 90.1%, 89.95% and 93.9%, which are 9.1%, 4.78% and 3.8% higher than those of the baseline model, respectively. The improved network model comprehensively increased the detection accuracy and provided an effective method for the detection of lumbar spine and lumbar disc herniation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Gesture Recognition for Seamless UI Interaction Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study presents an advanced gesture recognition and user interface (UI) interaction system developed using deep learning technologies, emphasizing its transformative impact on UI design and functionality. By employing optimized convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the system achieves high-precision gesture recognition, significantly enhancing user interactions with digital interfaces. Initial steps involve preprocessing collected gesture images to conform to CNN input standards, followed by employing sophisticated feature extraction and classification methodologies. We address class imbalance effectively using Focal Loss as the loss function, ensuring robust model performance across varied gesture types. The experimental results showcase notable improvements in model metrics, with the AUC and Recall increasing progressively as we evolve from simpler models like VGG16 to more complex ones such as DenseNet. Our enhanced model demonstrates a significant advancement with an AUC of 0.83 and a Recall of 0.85, surpassing standard benchmarks. More critically, this system's capacity to support real-time and efficient gesture recognition paves the way for a new era in UI design—where intuitive, natural user gestures can seamlessly integrate into everyday technology use, significantly reducing the learning curve and enhancing user satisfaction. The broad implications of this development are profound, extending beyond mere technical performance to fundamentally reshape how users interact with technology. Such advancements hold considerable promise for the enhancement of smart life experiences, highlighting the pivotal role of gesture-based interactions in the next generation of UI development.

articleTitle: A Combined Encoder and Transformer Approach for Coherent and High-Quality Text Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This research introduces a novel text generation model that combines BERT's semantic interpretation strengths with GPT-4's generative capabilities, establishing a high standard in generating coherent, contextually accurate language. Through the combined architecture, the model enhances semantic depth and maintains smooth, human-like text flow, overcoming limitations seen in prior models. Experimental benchmarks reveal that BERT-GPT-4 surpasses traditional models, including GPT-3, T5, BART, Transformer-XL, and CTRL, in key metrics like Perplexity and BLEU, showcasing its superior natural language generation performance. By fully utilizing contextual information, this hybrid model generates text that is not only logically coherent but also aligns closely with human language patterns, providing an advanced solution for text generation tasks. This research highlights the potential of integrating semantic understanding with advanced generative models, contributing new insights for NLP, and setting a foundation for broader applications of large-scale generative architectures in areas such as automated writing, question-answer systems, and adaptive conversational agents.

articleTitle: Transform-domain Image Enhancement for Underwater Visual SLAM based on Homomorphic Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Underwater visual SLAM algorithms play a vital role in autonomously localizing Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV) in challenging underwater environments. The low-light conditions underwater necessitate the use of artificial lighting sources. However, this can lead to issues such as overexposed or underexposed images, resulting in reduced image contrast and information content. This study introduces a transform-domain image enhancement technique aimed at bolstering the resilience of underwater visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) systems. Specifically, a homomorphic filtering method is implemented to alleviate the impact of low-frequency lighting variations on images, thereby enhancing overall image clarity and bolstering the performance of visual SLAM systems. The efficacy of this filtering approach is validated through experiments conducted on the AQUALOC dataset. Our findings demonstrate that this method enhances the success rate of visual SLAM tracking, thereby enhancing its utility in AUV localization tasks.

articleTitle: MSA-Net: MultiScale Attention Network for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is an ophthalmic complication caused by diabetes, leading to retinal vascular damage and is an important cause of blindness in patients. Deep learning-based lesion segmentation has shown great potential in assisting physicians in diagnosis and early prevention, but it is challenging to precisely segment DR lesions due to the large number of types, varying sizes, and intra-class variations of DR lesions, which occupy a small area in the fundus map. This paper proposes a novel lesion segmentation network to enhance segmentation accuracy. First, a proposed Multiscale Feature Fusion Block (MSFF) is applied in encoder to integrate and enrich multiscale features. Then, the proposed Dilated Attention Block (DAB) is used to optimize model's ability to extract global and local features, focusing on key information. Finally, the proposed Local-Global Attention Block (LGAB) is introduced in skip connections to effectively fuse deep and shallow features, enhancing the amount of information in the decoder while improving feature selectivity. We conducted ablation experiments on the IDRiD dataset to validate the effectiveness of each component and analyze them in comparison with existing methods. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in DR lesion segmentation.

articleTitle: Super-resolution Model Adaptation Based on Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The Stable-Diffusion model currently holds a dominant position in image generation technology. However, images generated by this model are influenced by training and can only produce images of a specific resolution. To enhance image resolution generated by the Stable-Diffusion model, this study investigates the combined impact of various mainstream Super-Resolution models with the Stable-Diffusion model. The experiment aims to enhance both the quality and speed of image generation. It evaluates the performance of different Super-Resolution models in boosting the resolution of images inferred by the Stable-Diffusion model while preserving image details. Research findings demonstrate that certain Super-Resolution models can significantly enhance image resolution while upholding high-quality images, offering an effective approach to achieve efficient image generation with limited computational resources.

articleTitle: Detection of Steel Surface Defects Based on Optimised YOLOv9 Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the production and processing of steel, numerous factors, such as process control, equipment condition, and raw material quality, can influence the occurrence of surface defects. These defects may present as cracks, inclusions, scratches, and other visible imperfections. Such flaws not only detract from the visual quality of steel but also significantly impact its mechanical properties and service life.
