Therefore, timely and accurate detection of surface defects is crucial for ensuring steel quality and improving product qualification rates. This paper proposes a steel surface defect detection algorithm based on YOLOv9. First, the InceptionV1 module is utilized in the backbone network to replace the RepNCSPELAN4 module, enhancing the understanding of image content and enriching the expressiveness of features. Second, the Dysample upsampling operator is introduced in the neck network, effectively improving image resolution by intelligently adjusting sampling points to avoid distortion and enhance detail performance. Finally, incorporating the P6 detection layer into the head network enables the model to better recognize small-scale targets while maintaining high accuracy for larger ones. This approach allows for a more comprehensive and detailed detection of steel surface defects. Experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced model achieves average precision and accuracy of 78.7% and 78.4%, respectively, representing improvements of 2.3% and 3.3% over the benchmark model. The findings of this study have substantial practical implications for enhancing industrial product quality and production efficiency.

articleTitle: Algorithm Design of Infrared Image Three-Dimensional Non-Stationary Noise Based on Time Series Statistics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the development of high orbit area array starting infrared imaging technology in China, the quality of its image directly affects the user’s use. Therefore, noise detection and supplementation of area array staring infrared images are becoming increasingly important. This paper presented a detection method of the infrared image of three-dimensional non-stationary noise based on Time Series Statistics to solve the effect of the three-dimensional non-stationary noise, which formed because many factors influenced the infrared image of staring Plane Array such as orbit time, the inherent flaw of detectors, and imaging conditions. Meanwhile, this paper also located and analyzed the non-stationary noise, and suggested a method of Local filtering by using the trend extrapolation theory. Based on the evaluation of the test result, the non-stationary noise recognition accuracy of this method could be up to 85% and the non-stationary noise image correlation coefficient before and after removal could be up to 95%, which could provide the satellite with real-time processing and improve the quality of the infrared image. This method can effectively improve the data quality and information product quality of high orbit array infrared remote sensing images, promote application level, and enhance application efficiency.

articleTitle: A Visual System for Blind Spot Detection and Warning for Mopeds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of computer vision, its related applications have been becoming more and more popular. One of the important reasons is that these applications can better assist people in various fields. In this article, the authors designed a novel blind spot detection system for mopeds. This article first described how to collect the data set containing cars and cycles, annotated the objects, and then converted it into YOLO (You Only Look Once) format. The authors then used the YOLOv5-Lite (You Only Look Once Version 5-Lite) model as the basic model for object detection. The authors used a cloud server to train the data set and obtained the optimal result, and then converted the optimal result into ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) format. After the authors implanted the ONNX format into the detection program, the program successfully realized the function of detecting specific objects in the blind spot areas for mopeds. The program also added a warning function, which will be activated when certain situations occur. Besides, the authors proposed a device called Blind Spot Detection and Warning Device (BSDWD), which is installed on mopeds and consists of two LED lights, a buzzer and a camera. After BSDWD is turned on, it will detect cars and cycles in the rear blind spot of the moped in real time. When the rear object enters the warning range, the warning system will be activated. Then the authors used BSDWD to conduct two sets of tests during the day and at night. The experimental results show that the accuracy of object detection is 71.7%. The real-time FPS (Frame Rate per second) of the camera is 6.37. Both sets of experiments can effectively detect objects in the rear blind spot areas, and the warning system can be activated successfully when the object enters the warning range.

articleTitle: Point-KGCN:A Point Cloud Target Detection Framework Based on GCN with KAN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the advancement of intelligent vehicle technology, target detection methodologies have become increasingly diversified. Traditionally, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) utilising the YOLO algorithm have dominated, but these methods suffer from the problems of costly point cloud computation and poor accuracy of small target detection. These problems affect the efficiency of target detection. To address this gap, this paper presents a novel graph neural network, Point-KGNN, designed to enhance category prediction using LIDAR data and graph representation techniques. Point-KGNN, primarily designed for autonomous driving applications, excels in predicting object categories and properties. The integration of the KAN algorithm during the graph iteration process is a key innovation. KAN has changed the way information is processed throughout the entire graph structure. Additionally, the framework incorporates multiple attention mechanisms and NMS probes to further improve performance. Experiments conducted on the KITTI3D dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Specifically, the results indicate improvements of 3.56% for car targets, 2.60% for cyclist targets, and 3.14% for passerby targets in medium difficulty scenarios, compared to the existing POINT-GNN model. These findings validate the efficacy of the approach introduced in this study.

articleTitle: Text-based Visual Question Answering Based on Text-Aware Pre-Training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text-based Visual Question Answering (TextVQA) is a subfield of Visual Question Answering (VQA) that is able to read the text in a given image. Existing work on TextVQA usually improves model performance by designing more powerful model architectures. However, the performance improvements of these custom methods are usually not significant. The text-aware pre-training method can enable the model to better understand the relationship between questions, scene text and visual objects in the image, thereby providing a new way to improve the performance of existing custom text-based visual question answering methods. In this paper, we propose a TextVQA method called TAP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> that improves the state-of-the-art text-aware pre-training (TAP) method in two aspects. First, a vision-language pretraining model VisualBERT is adopted as the base backbone network for multimodal fusion, significantly improving the accuracy of the model. Second, an attention module is introduced to filter out redundant or irrelevant features output from the fusion module, thereby further improving the accuracy of the model. Experimental results show that our model outperforms TAP model and other non-pretraining baselines, achieving an accuracy of 49.81% on the TextVQA dataset test set and an ANLS score of 0.569 on the STVQA dataset test set.

articleTitle: YOLOWEN:An Efficient Multi-object Detection Model for Cigar Appearance Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: An innovative YOLOWEN model has been introduced to automatically identify defects in full-leaf, handmade cigars, including bruises, holes, breaks, and tail breaks, which are critical quality concerns during production. This model enhances the YOLOv5 architecture by incorporating a WEN (Weighted ENhancement) module, which enriches the model's receptive field with a hierarchical structure. Additionally, the traditional C3 module has been swapped out for a fusion module, enhancing the model's ability to integrate features more effectively. The inclusion of a CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) at the detection head's forefront ensures that the model prioritizes significant image features while downplaying less relevant areas. Preliminary experimental outcomes indicate that the YOLOWEN model outperforms the standard YOLOv5 by 1.7 percentage points in mAP@0.5, achieving an impressive 96.40%. This advancement signifies that the YOLOWEN model is highly effective in detecting key cigar defects, thereby offering a robust solution for the intelligent quality control in cigar manufacturing.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Detection Technology in Agriculture: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is rapidly transforming agriculture by enabling rapid, non-destructive, and information-rich analysis of crops, soil, and agricultural products. This review provides a comprehensive overview of HSI, with a particular focus on its application in pesticide residue detection. We delve into the fundamental principles of HSI, its diverse applications in agriculture, and analyze recent advancements that leverage deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) for enhanced pesticide residue detection. We present insightful case studies demonstrating the practical implications of HSI in real-world scenarios and discuss the challenges and future prospects of this transformative technology, highlighting its potential to contribute to a more precise, efficient, and sustainable food production system.

articleTitle: An Effective LSTM Model for Predicting Tourist Flow at Scenic Spot Based on Seasonal-Trend Decomposition and Discrete Cosine Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of uncertainty and randomness in data mining and feature extraction of tourist flow prediction model, a new hybrid model 'STL-DCT-LSTM' is proposed in this paper. In this model, the seasonal trend decomposition algorithm is first used for data preprocessing, and the tourist flow data of scenic spots is decomposed into three feature channels to extract the feature-related information. Then Fourier transform algorithm is used to convert the time domain information of tourist flow into frequency domain information, and discrete cosine algorithm is used to simulate the frequency correlation between feature channels, so as to alleviate the Gibbs phenomenon of high-frequency noise introduced in the Fourier transform process of Fourier algorithm, improve the ability of the model to extract frequency features and automatically optimize the weight and threshold of each feature. Finally, the long and short term memory neural network is used to forecast the tourist flow of the scenic spot, and the components of the forecast result are added by their respective weights to get the final predicted value. In addition, the STL-DCT-LSTM model is compared with other predictive modeling methods such as linear regression, regression tree and support vector machine, and the results show that the STL-DCT-LSTM model is the best predictive model.

Author Keywords: long short term memory neural networks

articleTitle: LLaVA-Oil Painting Appreciation: A Vision-Language Model for Enhancing Understanding of Oil Paintings Through AI-Driven Analysis and Conversation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Oil painting has been a dominant art form since the 15th century, known for its profound impact on artistic expression. While exhibitions offer people unprecedented access to masterpieces, many viewers lack the formal artistic training or understanding of oil painting found hard to appreciate the intricate techniques and historical context of these works. This paper introduces LLaVA-Oil Painting Appreciation (LLaVA-OPA), a vision-language conversational assistant designed to help individuals engage more deeply with oil paintings. Leveraging the LLaVA-1.6 model and fine-tuning it using LoRA, LLaVA-OPA is trained on a curated dataset of oil paintings, supplemented by expert annotations from art scholars and professionals. The model identifies key elements such as brushwork, composition, and style, offering insightful, accessible feedback to users. By incorporating GPT-4 for generating open-ended questions and responses, LLaVA-OPA creates a conversational experience that allows users, regardless of prior art knowledge, to explore the complexities of oil paintings in an engaging manner. Initial evaluations demonstrate that LLaVA-OPA excels in providing tailored, expert-like analysis while maintaining user-friendly interactions. Future research will focus on deepening the model’s understanding by integrating information about artists' creative inspirations and historical context, enabling even more nuanced and meaningful conversations in various art settings, including exhibitions.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Detection Based on Enhanced YOLOv9 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Underwater target detection is crucial for ocean exploration, yet Traditional ground target detection method struggle under harsh underwater conditions. Issues such as inconsistent lighting, low contrast, and physical obstacles can obscure targets, making it particularly difficult for conventional approaches to accurately detect low-resolution images and small targets, which are further compromised by ambient noise and variable target sizes. These challenges impede accurate feature extraction and slow the detection process. Consequently, advanced detection technologies are imperative to overcome these obstacles and drive progress in marine environmental engineering. In light of the aforementioned challenges, we present an improved iteration of YOLOv9, named the enhanced YOLOv9 model, tailored to bolster detection precision for images of low resolution and minute targets. This upgraded model provides the capacity to fine-tune parameters and modify the shapes of convolutional kernels, leading to a decrease in the computational burden on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Such optimization notably enhances the efficacy of target detection in complex underwater settings, effectively tackling inherent obstacles and fortifying the model's overall resilience. Ablative experiments on Underwater Robot Picking Contest (URPC) and Underwater Object Detection (UOD) datasets and comparative analysis of current mainstream detectors show that this model demonstrates clear superiority in both detection capability and efficiency.

articleTitle: SegFormer+: Online Tobacco-Cut Structure Proportion Measurement Method Based on Improved SegFormer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Online tobacco-cut structure measurement can obtain the mass proportion of different types of tobacco-cut in cigarettes in real time, which is of great significance for monitoring the quality of commercial cigarettes. Traditional tobacco-cut structure measurement methods have not only low accuracy but also less efficiency due to complex processes. We first use the Segformer model as the benchmark model, realize the recognition and segmentation of different tobacco-cut (leaf, slice, Dilated) and stems through semantic segmentation, and introduce key improvements including the introduction of snake convolution and the GHM loss function to SegFormer, and a secondary structure proportion revision to further improve the performance of the model, which yields the improved model SegFormer+. In addition, we propose an automated annotation method to produce machine-generated tobacco-cut semantic segmentation datasets, which can obtain training sets without manual annotation so as to save manual annotation costs. Experimental results show that the average relative error of the structure measurement is less than 15%.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Glioma Surgery-Assisted Navigation System Incorporating 3D-ResUNet and Mixed Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In this study, we propose an intelligent navigation system for glioma surgery that combines 3D-ResUNet and mixed reality technologies. The aim of this system is to enhance the accuracy and safety of glioma surgery. Automatic segmentation is achieved through the use of multimodal MRI data and the 3D-ResUNet model. Additionally, 3D reconstruction is performed using VTK to enable hierarchical visualization of brain tissues and tumor regions. By utilizing the Vuforia platform and HoloLens 2, the system is able to align and display virtual and real environments in real-time, providing surgeons with efficient surgical navigation support. Experimental results demonstrate that the system exhibits excellent segmentation performance, as indicated by the Dice coefficient and Jaccard index. It is anticipated that this system will be adopted and utilized in clinical surgery.

articleTitle: Text-embeding and Visual-reference Less Object Counting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This study presents TET-Count, a novel category-agnostic model for object counting from natural language prompts, addressing limitations in existing methods requiring extensive annotated data. Leveraging pre-training of CLIP, TET-Count integrates feature projection and image regulation for enhanced semantic localization and counting accuracy. Experiments on the FSC-147 dataset using MAE and RMSE metrics show its superiority over other zero-shot techniques. Ablation studies confirm the importance of feature projection, and qualitative results demonstrate robust counting capabilities. TET-Count represents an advance in cross-modal object counting, combining NLP with deep learning for future research and applications.

articleTitle: Research Progress on Computing Resource Scheduling in Computing Power Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the evolution of computing power networks, the effective scheduling of computing resources has become a critical concern, driven by the diversification of computing demands and the increasing heterogeneity of resources. This paper provides a review of scheduling strategies for computing resources within these networks, analyzing methods that are relevant for the current landscape, including CPUs and GPUs. It emphasizes application scenarios and benefits across three key areas: improving resource utilization, balancing fairness and efficiency in scheduling, and minimizing job completion time. By synthesizing and evaluating existing methods, this paper identifies potential future research directions in computing resource scheduling, including the effective scheduling of heterogeneous resources, joint scheduling of multiple resources, cross-domain scheduling, and optimization of energy consumption. Furthermore, the paper addresses the significance of tackling future challenges in computing resource scheduling, focusing on three aspects: heterogeneous perception and measurement, large-scale multi-resource collaborative scheduling, and cross-domain communication.

articleTitle: The GAC-BiLSTM-AM Method and Its Application to the Prediction of Cracking Outlet Temperature in Ethylene Cracking Furnaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional prediction model is limited by the information processing capacity and leads to insufficient generalization ability, a GAC-BiLSTM-AM prediction method combined with the mistake correction mechanism is proposed. The method constructs a base learner by organically combining dual-channel convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory, attention mechanism and fully connected network to deeply mine the intrinsic laws and key information of data. Meanwhile, during the iteration process of the base learner, the proposed mistake correction mechanism is used to dynamically adjust the sample weights and assist the optimizer in refining the model parameters. Furthermore, the linear regression model and the Gold Rush Optimizer are further utilized to achieve result mapping and structural parameter optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the GAC-BiLSTM-AM method exhibits excellent generalization performance across multiple benchmark prediction tasks.

articleTitle: OCProNet: Ovarian Cancer Prognosis Prediction Network Based on Hybrid CNN and ViT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of medical imaging technology and deep learning, prognostic outcome prediction has become an important area of medical research. Prognostic evaluation of ovarian cancer is crucial for patient rehabilitation management. In previous studies, various advanced deep convolutional neural network (CNN) models have been used for prognostic assessment of different cancers. However, CNN models typically focus on learning local feature details for decision-making, often overlooking global features. In this study, we propose a hybrid algorithm based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViT) to accurately predict three key indicators: Lymph Node Metastasis (LNM), Organ Involvement (Organ), and Relapse. First, CNNs are used to preliminarily extract features from medical images, while ViT captures long-range dependencies and global information. The combination of the two aims to improve the accuracy of cancer prognostic predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method excels in predicting LNM, Organ Involvement, and Relapse, achieving an average accuracy of 82.54%, precision of 0.82, and recall of 0.82, significantly outperforming traditional models. This algorithm not only enhances the accuracy of prognostic predictions but also provides strong data support for personalized treatment planning.

articleTitle: Exploring Commonalities Across Programming Languages Using Intermediate Representation-Based Semantic Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cross-language code-to-code search has significant potential to enhance software development and maintenance by helping developers implement specific functionalities or migrate code between programming languages. Existing approaches, however, have notable limitations: static approaches relying on textual or syntactic information often lack effectiveness due to significant cross-language differences, while dynamic approaches relying on input-output behavior have limited applicability as they require executable code, which is difficult to guarantee in real-world projects.In this paper, we introduce CRDSER, a fully static cross-language code searcher designed to address these challenges. Our key insight is that, while code snippets in different languages may vary considerably in token sequences or syntactic structures, those with identical functionality can still share similarities in their Intermediate Representations (IRs). To capture this, we build a semantic graph that effectively models code semantics across languages by leveraging data flow and control flow information from IRs. We further design a hierarchical pooling mechanism to represent this graph structure, inspired by the way human developers hierarchically understand code snippets. Our large-scale evaluation demonstrates that CRDSER achieves both scalability (applicable to any code snippet) and high effectiveness, outperforming the best existing static approaches by up to 20% in Mean Reciprocal Rank. Additionally, ablation studies confirm that each module in our approach contributes substantially to CRDSER ’s overall effectiveness.

articleTitle: LLMs as Master Forgers: Generating Synthetic Time Series Data for Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate synthetic time series data for manufacturing processes. Motivated by the scarcity of labeled time-series data in real-world manufacturing settings, which hinders the development of robust machine learning models, we explore the potential of LLMs to learn complex temporal dependencies and generate realistic synthetic data. Our approach involves fine-tuning pre-trained LLMs on manufacturing process instructions and employing a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technique to enhance data diversity and realism. We evaluate our method against traditional time series modeling techniques like ARIMA and LSTMs, using quantitative metrics, PCA analysis, and downstream task performance (anomaly detection). Results demonstrate that our LLM-driven framework outperforms these baselines, generating high-quality synthetic time series data that effectively captures temporal dependencies and statistical properties of real manufacturing data, leading to improvements in downstream task performance.

articleTitle: Research on the optimization of Rescue Action Policy in Stochastic Weather Conditions through Q-learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Based on the stochastic weather conditions, and the reasonable assumption of the application scenario, the optimal strategy design of carrying food, oil, equipment and other materials to the designated place in the form of a team was studied. Some specific area are divided into several divisions to establish action space for an action team. The weather probability distribution is set, the state-action value function that depends on the expected cumulative reward is constructed and iteratively updated, and the Q learning optimization model of the action policy for rescuing disaster areas is established when there is a ground supply station or airdrop supply point by preset. With the help of two hypothetical maps, the simulation obtains the optimal policy of the action when the most materials remain. The solution results are reasonable and reliable, the model is flexible, and the application range is wide.

articleTitle: Joint Visual and Semantic Information Image Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In image retrieval, there exists a "semantic gap" problem, which refers to the discrepancy between the image semantics understood by computers through extracted image features and the image semantics perceived by humans. This paper studies an image retrieval algorithm based on image visual information and semantic information. The algorithm utilizes image features combined with hash encoding to describe the visual characteristics of images, and employs a word vector generation model to convert semantic words of images into word vectors, thereby describing the semantic features of the images. To better combine the similarities of visual features and semantic features, the algorithm establishes a reranking retrieval matrix for image searching. The paper validates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through experiments, demonstrating that the retrieved images highlighted by this algorithm are consistent in terms of semantic information while ensuring the similarity of visual features.

articleTitle: Travel Route Planning Based on Intelligent Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Travel serves as an essential means for individuals to relax and unwind from work-related stress. The selection of appropriate destinations and the planning of efficient itineraries not only enhance personal experience but also improve the operational efficiency of travel agencies and other commercial entities. To address these concerns, this paper introduces a comprehensive multi-criteria evaluation method that integrates the Entropy Weight Method (EWM) with the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to optimize the selection of travel destinations. Subsequently, a hybrid approach combining the Ant Colony Algorithm (ACA) and Simulated Annealing Algorithm (SAA) is employed to plan optimal travel routes. Utilizing publicly available data from 352 tourist cities, multiple simulations of the proposed methodology have been executed. The numerical results indicate that this approach effectively aids individuals in selecting suitable travel destinations and planning efficient travel routes.

Author Keywords: The Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution

articleTitle: Lightweight Strip Steel Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv8s
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To address the issues of low accuracy, high number of parameters and computational cost in strip steel surface defect detection algorithms, a lightweight strip steel surface defect detection algorithm based on YOLOv8s is proposed. Initially, the Cross-stage Focused Linear Attention (C2F-FLA) module is introduced to enhance the feature extraction capability of the backbone network. Subsequently, to improve the capture of multi-scale defect contours and reduce the model’s parameters and computational complexity, a Wavelet Convolution-Bidirectional Weighted Feature Pyramid Network (WT-BiFPN) is employed in the model’s Neck section for adaptive fusion of features at different resolutions. Finally, Haar Wavelet Downsampling (HWD) is utilized to retain more defect-related information, further reducing the parameters and computational complexity. The proposed method was validated on the NEU-DET dataset, and the results demonstrate that compared to YOLOv8s, this approach achieves a 4.1% increase in mAP, a 44.4% reduction in parameters, and a 32.8% decrease in computational complexity. The method ensures lightweight implementation while improving detection accuracy, offering more possibilities for defect detection on edge terminal devices.

articleTitle: MCDM-DTI: Accelerating Diffusion Tensor Imaging based on Multi-Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probability Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a significant non-invasive neuroimaging technique with valuable applications in clinical medicine. To address the lengthy acquisition times and high costs of traditional DTI technology, we propose a multi-conditional diffusion model for accelerated DTI (MCDM-DTI). This model generates high-quality DTI maps using only six diffusion-weighted images (DWIs) and one b0 image. The model leverages the diffusion process of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) to learn the underlying data distribution of DTI maps. By incorporating the DWIs and the b0 image as conditional inputs to a U-Net denoising network, MCDM-DTI produces more accurate DTI parameter maps. The introduction of Class Label Embedding technology extracts category-specific features, enabling the concurrent generation of all category parameter maps. Additionally, a binary image erosion algorithm can eliminate edge noise. Validated on the Human Connectome Project dataset (HCP), MCDM-DTI demonstrates superior performance in generating FA, MD, and AD, along with good robustness against noise, compared to previously studied methods. Our approach achieves over a 5-fold boost in imaging speed while maintaining high-resolution DTI maps, significantly reducing acquisition time.

articleTitle: MVIB-RGSL: Multi View Information Bottleneck based Robust Graph Structure Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Recently, graph neural networks have achieved significant results in various graph structure learning tasks. However, the graph structure in reality often contains noise, which could affect the effectiveness and robustness of the model prediction. In order to improve the robustness of the graph structure learning model, many studies have introduced the idea of information bottleneck. Information bottleneck can improve the robustness of the model. However, information bottleneck requires labeled data in the dataset to remove the information irrelevant to the prediction task. Therefore, for the unsupervised scenario, we propose MVIB-RGSL (Multi View Information Bottleneck based Robust Graph Structure Learning). We use the method of graph data augmentation to generate different views on the basis of the original input graph data, thereby expanding the problem to the multi-view learning scenario. Then we use the information bottleneck under the multi-view setting to remove view-specific redundant information between the two views. Finally, we use the adversarial method to train the graph encoder while optimizing the graph structure generated by graph data augmentation, thereby obtaining more effective and robust graph structures and graph representations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Sinhala Sign Language Recognition: A Systematic Decade Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The paper reviews the progress in Sinhala Sign Language recognition (SSL) over the last decade, tracing the techniques from early image processing to advanced deep learning models, indicating methodologies involved, datasets used, and challenges. The paper shows that the evolution has progressed from basic classifiers to sophisticated machine learning techniques that integrate CNNs, RNNs, and transformer architectures. It also presents the implementation of multimodal systems using hand gestures, facial expressions, and body postures. The review identifies the limitations of current recognition in SSL, such as scarce complete datasets, technical difficulties, and a lack of robust continuous recognition. Finally, it points out future research directions, stressing that further work must focus on growing datasets, making lightweight models for edge devices, and collaboration for further growth in SSL recognition technology.

articleTitle: DF-SE-ResNet: Orange Leaf Disease Classification Method Based on Improved Attention Mechanism and FPN Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The present study introduces a deep learning-based CNN model, DF-SE-ResNet, designed to enhance the classification precision of orange leaf diseases. This paper employs a feature extraction network that integrates an optimized ResNet50 with FPN (Feature Pyramid Networks) and incorporates an improved attention mechanism module, enhancing the network's ability to extract features from small and dense lesion patches while retaining more semantic information from their surroundings, thus laying a solid foundation for accurate subsequent identification. To address the challenge of capturing lesion patches with random distribution, a region feature weighting fusion method based on permutation invariance is introduced after the feature extraction network, which improves the ability to precisely capture lesion patches and significantly enhances lesion features, effectively resolving the issue of randomly distributed lesion patches. Finally, to mitigate the impact of uneven sample distribution across classes in the dataset, an inverse frequency cross-entropy loss function is adopted in place of the standard cross-entropy loss function, alleviating the model's bias towards the majority classes. In the experimental phase, the DF-SE-ResNet achieved an accuracy rate of 95.4%, demonstrating superior performance compared to other deep learning models.

Author Keywords: Inverse frequency cross entropy loss function

articleTitle: A Network Traffic Prediction for Information Security in the Smart Power
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of network information technology, the volume of network data is increasing exponentially, and the scope of network applications is expanding. Network security issues are receiving increasing attention from the academic community. The integration of data science and artificial intelligence has intensified global network security challenges, especially in the Internet of Things (IoT) for power systems. As more power-related devices are connected to networks, security threats are heightened. Network traffic prediction is crucial for maintaining the information security of power IoT through proactive security measures. This paper proposes a novel model that combines BiGRU and Transformer to enhance long-term temporal dependency modeling. The model integrates Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) for spatial features, BiGRU for time dependencies, and transformer-based feature weight assessment, improving the accuracy of anomaly detection and network traffic prediction. The model’s predictive capabilities are further enhanced by utilizing multi-head self-attention and large-scale language models. We demonstrate the model’s outstanding potential on real-world datasets.

articleTitle: The Enhancement of Advanced Text-to-Image Diffusion Generation Models: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) generation with Diffusion Models (DMs) has drawn considerable attention recently because of their extraordinary performance and huge potential. However, DMs still have some unsolved problems, e.g., computational complexity, less scalability or concept misalignment. This review focuses on discussing the advanced methods developed to enhance the T2I Diffusion Models. The works mentioned have been categorised into three major classes: Prompt Augmentation is about the preliminary works; Fine-grained Alignment is focused on attempts during the phase of training and Model Interpretability mainly discusses the research on improving the model’s explainability.

articleTitle: A Method for Nuclear Power Pipeline Weld Seam Recognition Based on Structured Light Multidimensional Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents an automated method for precise pipeline weld identification and measurement using autonomous robots in nuclear power environments. It addresses challenges related to initial shooting exposure, camera angle, and distance from the environment by employing adaptive data collection techniques. These methods adjust exposure based on statistical brightness information from color images captured by a structured light camera. By detecting the pipeline model in threedimensional point cloud data, optimal camera positions and postures are determined for high-quality data acquisition. Geometric features are extracted from the point cloud data to create a geometric feature response map projected onto a twodimensional image, which is fused with color features to generate a grayscale fusion map. Image recognition algorithms identify weld areas, enabling precise three-dimensional measurements. Experimental results confirm the method’s effectiveness in improving data quality and achieving accurate weld seam identification and measurement.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm for Detection of Small and Complex Morphological Defects in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In recent years, power grid companies have used artificial intelligence image recognition technology to conduct inspections of transmission lines. Although some results have been achieved, defects of small sizes and complex shapes are still easily missed or misdetected. In response to this problem, the DRM-YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed: in the feature extraction part, a C2f_DCNv3_DLKA module that combines DLKA (Deformable Large Kernel Attention) and DCNv3 (Deformable Convolution Network v3) is designed to improve the identification and extraction capabilities of important features; a heavy-parameterized cross-over algorithm is proposed The stage feature fusion local network optimizes and fuses high-level semantic features and low-level spatial features; finally, a multi-head adaptive spatial feature fusion detection head is designed. By adding an additional small target detection layer and improving cross-scale feature fusion, the detection capabilities of multiple small targets with significant size differences are improved. Experimental results show that on a data set containing twenty types of real transmission line defects, compared with the original YOLOv8n model, the overall average detection accuracy (mAP@0.5) reached 84.1%, an increase of 5.2%, for small size and complex shape defects The detection accuracy is increased by 8% and 2% respectively, which is significantly better than the existing algorithm, showing excellent robustness and generalization, and effectively improving the detection ability of multiple types of defects in transmission lines in complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Correction Based on Radiative Transfer Model: Processing and Accuracy Analysis of ZY1- 02E Satellite Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The ZY1-02E satellite can effectively acquire large-width multispectral, infrared, and hyperspectral data. The satellite is networked with the in-orbit ZY1-02D satellite, forming a globally leading operational Earth spectroscopy detection capability. It is capable of achieving full coverage of hyperspectral data across the entire land area of the country every six months, serving various industries such as disaster reduction, environmental protection, housing and transportation, agriculture, forestry, oceanography, and surveying. This paper evaluates the surface reflectance of ZY1-02E AHSI data using three evaluation metrics: correlation coefficient, root mean square error, and spectral angle cosine, and compares the results with ASD measured spectral data. The results indicate that the ZY1-02E AHSI payload can effectively identify information such as kaolinite and salinization, demonstrating outstanding application capabilities in mineral information extraction and salinization detection in mining areas.

articleTitle: Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly Spatio-temporal Data Generation Based on Separated Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Various natural disasters are closely related to the El Niño - Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the stable generation of accurate sea surface temperature anomaly (SSTA) data is key to exploring the occurrence patterns of ENSO and preventing disasters. In this study, we introduces the Separated Attention Data Generation (SADG) model, which efficiently generates SSTA data by capturing the long-range spatiotemporal relationship. SADG achieves high performance while reducing computational complexity compared to standard self-attention based models, generates up to 18 months of accurate SSTA data. Experiments on CMIP datasets show that its performance is better than other models on various lead times.

articleTitle: Research on Abnormal Detection of Rolling Bearing Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper proposes an anomaly detection method for rolling bearings based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector data description (SVDD). The main research contents are as follows. Firstly, to address the problems of pixel point waste and image resolution determination in the image preprocessing process of the current CNN-based bearing anomaly detection method, a transformation method of signal conversion into two-dimensional grayscale images is proposed to improve the image data generation efficiency. Secondly, to solve the problems that CNN-based anomaly detection requires the manual definition of labels and the lack of anomaly data in the actual detection process, a CNN-SVDD method that combines LeNet-5 and SVDD is adopted. By only defining normal sample labels, bearing anomaly detection can be performed with very little or even no anomaly data. The average AUC value reaches 96.50% after the validation of the public dataset, which has a high testing performance. Finally, the practicality of the CNN-SVDD algorithm model is further verified by experiments. Relying on the generator set of the test platform, a comparative test of motor bearing vibration with missing bearing slip oil and sufficient slip oil was designed. After several tests of the actual data in the algorithm model, the average AUC of the test index reached 98.82%. The whole testing system training and testing process is fast, highly accurate, and has strong practical application value.

articleTitle: Research on Lightweight Power Surveillance Video Key Frame Recognition Method for Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Power system video surveillance is an important means to ensure the safe operation of power equipment, but the massive video data generated by it brings great pressure to edge devices. Traditional video processing methods often use cloud computing mode to transmit data to remote servers for processing, which not only increases the burden of network bandwidth, but also brings a large transmission delay. In the edge computing mode, although localized processing can be realized, limited by the computing power of edge devices, how to achieve efficient video processing under resource-constrained conditions has become an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, we propose a lightweight keyframe recognition method for power surveillance video suitable for edge computing environment. By using sliding window mechanism and depthwise separable convolutional network, combined with adaptive resource adjustment strategy, this method achieves efficient key frame recognition under the condition of limited computing resources. Experimental results show that compared with traditional methods, the proposed method significantly reduces computing resource consumption and average processing delay while maintaining high recognition accuracy, and improves the processing efficiency in the edge computing environment.

articleTitle: Multi-Granularity Graph Representation and Augmentation for Image
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) process graph- structured data by learning features and patterns through neural networks, applied to tasks such as clustering, classification, and prediction. Current research primarily employs image-based data augmentation methods, but these methods struggle to capture the complex structures of graphs and multi-dimensional node data. This study proposes a graph data augmentation method within a multi-granularity computational framework, including random cropping, random flipping, and the dropping of nodes and edge relationships, aiming to enhance the learning and generalization capabilities of GNN models. Experimental results indicate that these methods significantly improve model robustness and data distribution, demonstrating good training effects and interpretability. It is hoped that these methods will play a role in computer vision tasks using GNNs.

articleTitle: A Novel Object Detection Method Based on Adaptive Attention Mechanism and Composite Confidence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Currently, some object detection methods combine anchor-free frameworks with single-stage approaches, allowing the model to be freed from the computational burden of using anchor boxes. This provides more space and flexibility, bringing both detection and segmentation closer to real-time accuracy. However, anchor-free object detection algorithms are confronted with some deficiencies due to their immature development, particularly in multi-scale, sampling, and loss functions. To dispose of the aforementioned issues, an object detection method based on adaptive attention mechanism and composite confidence is proposed. First, a matrix feature network based on the adaptive attention mechanism is proposed as the detection neck framework to address the detection difficulties caused by targets of different scales and aspect ratios. Moreover, the adaptive attention mechanism enhances features and facilitates feature transmission and fusion, thereby improving the precision of feature selection. Then, an object detection method guided by composite confidence is raised to refine the non-maximum suppression process, effectively suppressing low-quality bounding boxes. Additionally, the regression loss function is improved to optimize gradients, thereby enhancing detection accuracy. Furthermore, an adaptive center-covered sampling strategy is presented, which improves the overall sample quality by filtering out edge sample points during the sampling process. To validate the availability of our proposed methods, extensive experiments are conducted on two standard datasets: MS COCO 2017 and PASCAL VOC 2007. Experimental results demonstrate that our method can achieve better accuracy and possess higher computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Supervised Asymmetric Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Contrastive learning, as an unsupervised representation learning method, learns representations by exploring intrinsic relationships between sample pairs, achieving notable success in many visual tasks. However, the lack of class labels in contrastive learning means that different instances from the same class may be considered negative pairs, disrupting representation learning and weakening the model’s discrimination ability. The introduction of SupCon partially addresses this issue, but its base model, SimCLR, requires the construction of numerous negative pairs to avoid model collapse, demanding large batch sizes and imposing stringent hardware requirements.In this paper, we propose a novel supervised asymmetric contrastive learning model SupAsCon, based on the self-supervised contrastive learning framework BYOL. By combining asymmetric structure with supervised learning, SupAsCon prevents model collapse while enhancing class recognition abilities, especially excelling in small-batch training. Experimental results demonstrate that SupAsCon outperforms SupCon in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Based Fusion Feature Target Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In order to effectively solve the problems of image texture blurring and contrast degradation caused by the influence of fog, raindrops and other environmental factors on the images of transmission line components acquired by aerial photography in the natural environment, this paper proposes a fused feature target detection method based on image enhancement. Firstly, image enhancement is performed on the original aerial transmission component image based on dark channel defogging and Retinex image enhancement algorithm, then, image features are extracted based on HOG method, secondly, feature fusion is performed based on spatial attention mechanism, and finally, classification and regression tasks are accomplished based on SVM. This paper analyzes the gold fixture as a typical case of transmission line components, and constructs seven types of gold fixture datasets for experiments, and through the experimental results, it can be concluded that the overall detection effect of the target detection method proposed in this paper is better than that of the traditional detection model, and it can effectively solve the problem of the decline in the detection rate of the target due to the influence of the environment on the aerial images of the transmission components.

articleTitle: Second Order Neural Network Optimization: Meta Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Second-order optimization algorithms have garnered significant interest in deep learning due to their ability to leverage curvature information, leading to faster convergence and enhanced generalization compared to first-order methods. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent advancements in second-order optimization techniques tailored for deep neural networks, emphasizing their scalability, efficiency, and applicability across various tasks. We categorize these methods into Quasi-Newton methods, Generalized Gauss-Newton methods, and Parameter Subset Optimization methods, each offering unique strategies to balance computational cost and the advantages of second-order information. Despite their potential, these techniques face challenges such as high computational and memory demands, sensitivity to hyperparameters, and integration complexities in large-scale models. We discuss the innovative approaches employed by these algorithms to address these challenges, including structured approximations and adaptive updates, and provide insights into their theoretical foundations and empirical evaluations. The analysis highlights the critical role of second-order methods in advancing neural network optimization and outlines future research directions aimed at enhancing their scalability and practical adoption in deep learning applications.

articleTitle: Correction of Gridded Precipitation Data Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Gridded precipitation data play a crucial role in hydrological modeling and climate research, but biases between these data and actual ground observations limit their accuracy and reliability. Correcting these biases is essential to improve the accuracy of gridded precipitation data for practical applications. In this study, we developed the MR-interaction model based on single-day and multi-day gridded precipitation data and compared its performance with five machine learning models to achieve optimal predictive accuracy. By applying the RM-CONS correction method to the gridded data, we significantly reduced accuracy errors, resulting in corrected gridded data that more closely match the observed data distribution.

articleTitle: Low Illumination Image Enhancement Algorithm Based on Attention Mechanisms and Multiscale Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: A low-light image enhancement method combining the attention mechanism and multi-scale perception is proposed while stably enhancing the brightness and retaining the detailed information. The algorithm is based on Retinex theory to decompose the image into a reflection component and a light component, and then reconstruct the two components after enhancement. Inspired by the pyramid structure, a multi-scale perception module is designed with the characteristics of the human visual system to improve the feature extraction ability of the model for images of different scales. Combining the multi-scale perception module and the attention mechanism to construct a reflectance enhancement network using parallel convolutional kernel to enhance the model's ability to process information in the region of image luminance change. This enables the model to enhance images at different scales in different illuminated scenes. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has better result in structural similarity index and naturalness image quality evaluator. Processed images maintain a high degree of naturalness while improving brightness, contrast and preserving texture detail.

articleTitle: Research on the Quality Comprehensive Evaluation Method of Gateway Watt-Hour Meter Based on Multi-Source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The gateway watt-hour meter plays the key role of high-precision electricity metering in the power system, and its metering accuracy directly affects the settlement fairness of the power market. However, at present, the quality evaluation methods of gate watt-hour meters rely on a single data source, which is difficult to fully meet the needs of complex power grid environment. In this paper, a comprehensive evaluation method of watt-hour meter quality based on multi-source information fusion is proposed. Combining real-time performance data, historical maintenance records and environmental monitoring data, a systematic evaluation index system including stability, reliability and abnormal events is constructed. Through the fusion of Bayesian network, fuzzy logic and neural network model, the comprehensive view of watt-hour meter quality is formed. The actual case analysis shows that the method can effectively identify the potential failure risk of the watt-hour meter, improve the operation stability and maintenance efficiency of the power system, and provide scientific decision support for power enterprises.

articleTitle: Image Matching of Low Altitude UAV Visual Navigation Methods: Current Situation and Prospect
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The visual navigation technology of low-altitude UAV aims to match the real-time image taken by sensor with the existing image features in database, so as to determine the current position of the UAV and realize the control of the flight trajectory. Among visual navigation procedure, image matching is the most important step. Current image matching methods are divided into traditional methods and deep learning-based methods. This paper takes the classification of image matching techniques and methods as the breach to grasp the research status of image matching methods in low-altitude UAV visual navigation. First of all, the article analyzes steps of image matching and key problems of this field. Secondly, the paper introduces traditional methods of image matching and the method based on deep learning, summarizing the advantages and disadvantages of different methods. Then, the paper summarizes mainstream datasets used in low-altitude UAV visual navigation tasks and compares the performance indexes of different methods. Finally, the article generalizes the existing problems in advanced image matching methods to point out the possible development direction and trend, so as to provide reference for subsequent researchers to get further research.

articleTitle: Garbage Classification Using YOLO: Model Comparison and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper explores the application of YOLO-based deep learning algorithms in garbage classification. Models Yolov3 (Darknet53) and Yolov5s/m (CSP-Darknet53) are trained on three recyclable and three non-recyclable categories, comparing their prediction accuracy and speed. Results indicate that Yolov5s outperforms Yolov3 in recognition rate and efficiency, especially on resource-limited devices. The study highlights the potential of YOLO algorithms in intelligent garbage sorting and suggests future improvements for this application.

articleTitle: Research on Cardiac Medical Image Segmentation Based on an Improved U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: This paper presents a cardiac MRI image segmentation model based on an improved U-Net architecture. Accurate segmentation of cardiac MRI images is critical for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases, yet existing U-Net models exhibit limitations in handling complex cardiac structures and multi-scale features. To address these challenges, this paper proposes two key enhancements. First, we propose a Multi-Dimensional Context Attention module, designed to improve the integration of global and local information within the skip connections, thereby enhancing segmentation accuracy for intricate cardiac structures. Furthermore, we propose a Reverse Feature Modulation module, which generates reverse masks and dynamically adjusts feature weights across different classes using adaptive weighting, effectively mitigating class imbalance issues in multi-class segmentation tasks and improving focus on difficult-to-segment regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the standard U-Net on the ACDC dataset, achieving significant improvements in evaluation metrics such as the Dice coefficient. These enhancements underscore the model's efficacy and robustness in complex cardiac image segmentation tasks, offering new technical support for automated cardiovascular disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Research on Hidden Danger Target Detection of Transmission Line Shock Hammer under Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: During the examination of electrical power systems, the prevailing approach involving human-based, hands-on inspections is beset with several drawbacks, including inadequate levels of automation, suboptimal efficiency and inherent safety risks. The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) target detection method has broad application prospects for the important link of hid-den danger detection of shockproof hammers. Although the traditional shockproof hammer image detection has limitations such as environmental conditions, field of vision and system performance, we can use a new SR-YOLOV8 Convolutional neural network to achieve efficient and accurate target recognition in complex environments. This network adopts SimAM (Simple, Parameter Free Attention Module), which can effectively reduce the burden on the system and achieve more efficient target recognition. Using Res2Net as the foundation, we can greatly improve the feature extraction effect of the shock hammer feature map. This mechanism is capable of assigning pertinent 3D attention weights to the feature map in accordance with its characteristic attributes, thereby significantly enhancing the precision of the feature map, simultaneously, it broadens the potential applicability of the model. At the same time, a new image dataset for power grid shock hammer detection was created using real detection scenarios, and Mosaic data augmentation strategy was introduced for network training to improve the model's generalization ability and resistance to overfitting. After experimental verification, the improved shockproof hammer detection technology of YOLOv8s has performed well in performance indicators such as accuracy, recall, detection speed, and average accuracy, far exceeding traditional target detection methods, providing a reliable reference for power system inspection.

articleTitle: A High-Precision and Lightweight Method of PCB Defect Based on Enhanced Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Printed Circuit Boards, which play a crucial role in smart devices, have found widespread application across various industries. However, the prevalent methodologies for detecting defects in PCBs continue to face persistent challenges in balancing both model performance and computational efficiency. To address this, we propose an enhanced real-time detection model based on YOLOv8. Firstly, the key improvement is the introduction of an enhanced C2f module, named the Re-parametrized Attention-enhanced C2f. This module replaces the original 3x3 convolutional kernels with reparameterizable 1x3, 3x1, and 3x3 kernels, combined with a CBAM attention mechanism, to enhance small-object feature extraction and feature discrimination without increasing computational cost or model size. Secondly, we adopt the Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network to improve the integration of multi-scale features, which enhances detection precision and efficiency. Lastly, an Adaptive Shared Convolutional Head is introduced to reduce the parameter count and computational complexity, enabling the model to maintain high detection accuracy with minimal computational overhead. This design makes it particularly well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Using the PCB dataset from Peking University and employing data augmentation techniques, the model attains a 98.2% mAP in experimental testing, achieving a frame rate of 86.3 FPS on an NVIDIA 2080Ti GPU. The model’s parameters are reduced from 3.2 million to 2.1 million, and the FLOPs decreases from 8.7G to 6.8G, demonstrating an optimal balance between speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Exploring Cross-Domain Techniques in Person Re-Identification: Challenges and Emerging Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cross-domain person re-identification (ReID) has drawn much more attention because of the ability to improve the robustness and versatility of person recognition systems across diverse conditions. This review provides an overview of the modern deep learning methods employed to solve challenges in cross-domain ReID. Considering the level of abstraction of the target domain information, it selects three typical scenarios of infrared images, sketches and text descriptions, and compares classical methods in these three contexts. We not only provide the fundamental paradigms for solving the person re-identification problem, including feature representation learning and metric learning, but also highlight the challenges that exist in different domains and summarize data-efficient and domain-specific solutions. By examining various datasets and evaluation protocols, we identify gaps in current research and propose future directions for improving cross-modality ReID performance. This paper is aimed at providing some resources and pointing out some future trends for researchers looking to advance the field of person re-identification across heterogeneous data sources.

articleTitle: Automation and Classification Cascade Methods for Object Detection : Organising Data Stack for Supervised Learning before Runnning Unnecessary Pathfinders
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Let's assume this scenario, that a machine learning project has grouped 300 classes for each object type to detection, running common algorithms such as a Random walk in which every class can actually be bind to each other in small or larger clusters. A total possible combination for this use case would be around 2.037×10^89 possibilities of different groups. It’s not the amount of combinations that is in question here, but the time and energy consuming to compute this data, every time there would be a new object unsupervised to be properly classified. Therefore, the purpose of this paper aims to help machine learning beginners or enthusiasts, on their process of data stack structure, precisely at the beginning of the whole process, using as a case study of inside housing detection that uses more than 300 classes. Some examples and methodologies, including calculation models, are also cited with the final purpose to clear planning and guidance. The reason substantiated is the fact that many new machine learners, mostly students, are simply eager to run their code to get their object detection classification, directly to the purpose they want to achieve, no matter the path the machine is obliged to go until it shows some results. This anxiety is not only part of youth but part of the self-learning process when the machine starts to declare either is taking too long or the cost is becoming unbearable. Nevertheless, it’s a pain that can be avoided and the stack organisation helps developers additionally on defining better their patterns and create an automation process so that the future data will also just self-organize easily. There will be guidance using some previous works with some examples and algorithms to fully understand how simple, at the beginning, it is to organize data, and to better teach our machines, before just launching and learning at all cost. It is obvious that machines don’t complain and eventually they learn, however the following paper, shows graphically the method in an abstract way, as well as an example of inside house detection, hoping to be a great contribution to save time and to organise new projects for developers, at foundation level.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Facial Expression Generation Algorithm Based on Spatial Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the maturation and application of human-computer interaction and virtual reality technologies, facial expression generation has received widespread attention. However, current technologies often fail to fully capture the fine details of the face, neglecting the differences between various facial parts in an expression, which lowers the quality of the generated expressions. To address this, this paper proposes a facial expression generation algorithm based on spatial attention. The algorithm combines spatial attention mechanisms with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), allowing the adversarial network to better focus on important facial details in the image. Additionally, the algorithm effectively addresses the phenomenon of feature differences across multiple scales by introducing convolution layers with varying receptive fields. This forces the neural network to learn facial features at different scales and the differences between them, thereby improving the quality of expression generation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms current mainstream methods in terms of expression generation quality, enhancing both the efficiency and quality of expression generation and providing new insights for facial expression research.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Insulator Defect Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: To tackle the challenges of slow detection speed, poor performance in detecting small objects, and large model parameters in existing insulator defect detection methods, a lightweight algorithm based on YOLOv8n is proposed. Firstly, a C2PM module is designed to replace the C2f module, reducing redundant computations and optimizing feature extraction. Then, Adown is introduced to replace the standard convolution for improving the downsampling process, enhancing the ability to retain multi-scale features. By integrating the LSCD shared convolutional detection head, efficient processing of regression and classification tasks is achieved. The enhanced model significantly reduces both the number of parameters and the computational load, making it well-suited for real-time insulator defect detection. Additionally, it performs excellently in detecting defects in small insulator targets, even in complex scenarios. Experimental results indicate that, in comparison to YOLOv8n, the improved algorithm increases mAP@0.5 by 1%, with recall and precision improving by 3% and 0.3%, respectively. Moreover, the model's parameter size is only 1MB, which is two-thirds smaller than that of the YOLOv8n network. This demonstrates that the algorithm achieves a lightweight model while also delivering a slight improvement in accuracy, realizing a dual optimization in both precision and model efficiency.

articleTitle: Accurate Surface Area Measurement of Biological Tissues Based on an Improved EfficientSAM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The development of a non-invasive and robust three-dimensional optical imaging method enabled rapid and precise surface area measurements of flexible biological tissues through computer vision techniques. This paper intends to establish accurate and non-invasive measurement methodologies, which have become an urgent requirement for various clinical applications, including skin grafting. In this study, we explore the performance of the EfficientSAM model in wound segmentation tasks, employing targeted fine-tuning strategies to enhance its effectiveness. Key metrics like computational cost, accuracy of segmentation, generalization of the model, and robustness are taken into consideration. We also propose a novel loss function, achieving approximately a 24% improvement in Intersection over Union (IoU) scores, which can support precise surface area calculation and improve biomedical application outcomes.

articleTitle: Research on Image Denoising Based on Combined Adaptive GP and DCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the process of image acquisition and transmission, it is easy to be interfered by electronic equipment and light, resulting in noise, which affects people's acquisition and recognition of information. In image processing and computer vision, image denoising is an important step. Based on this, an image denoising algorithm combining adaptive GP (Gaussian filter, GF) and DCNN (Denoising Convolutional Neural Network, DCNN) is proposed. Through the adaptive GF preprocessing step, the noisy image is preliminarily smoothed and enhanced in detail, which provides a more favorable data basis for the subsequent DCNN deep denoising operation. Experimental results show that, compared with the traditional denoising algorithm, the proposed algorithm performs well in noise suppression, and can significantly improve the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of the image while maintaining the image details. This achievement not only shows the excellent performance of the algorithm in the field of image denoising, but also further verifies its theoretical value in the field of image processing, and provides a strong support and reference for the development of related technologies in the future.

articleTitle: Transformer DGA Fault Prediction Based on WOA and T-SNE Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) of transformer oil is an effective means to timely find potential faults in transformers. In order to further improve the accuracy and the applicability of transformer fault prediction model, a new method based on WOA and T-SNE is proposed to optimize the performance of random forest decision-making model. Based on T-SNE , the original DGA sample data of transformer is condensed and features are optimized. The feature vector is reduced from 12 dimensions to 3 dimensions, and the effect of division in sample space is significantly enhanced. Taking the highest prediction accuracy of the random forest model as the objective function, the WOA is used to find the optimal solution of three key parameters in random forest, including the number of trees, the number of split point sand the depth of trees. The DGA fault prediction model of transformer is constructed based on the optimized random forest. Finally, a transformer fault prediction in a substation is taken as an example to verify the consistency and effectiveness of the method with engineering practice. The model is also compared with traditional random forest, professional mechanism model and a variety of machine learning models. The results show that the accuracy of the transformer’s DGA fault prediction model based on optimal random forest is 95.2%, which is 6.7% higher than the original random forest, Compared with other models, it also has higher prediction accuracy and calculation efficiency.

articleTitle: A2Seg: Adversarial Learning with Channel-Wise Attention for Skin Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the realm of medical image analysis, the segmentation of skin lesions plays a pivotal role in the early detection and treatment of skin-related diseases. Neural network models have been extensively proposed for automatic segmentation task, but suffer from poor segmentation accuracy caused by gradient disappearance. This paper presents a novel adversarial learning model empowered by a channel-wise attention mechanism, called A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Seg, specifically tailored for the segmentation of skin lesions. A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Seg operates through a dual-network architecture comprising a segmentation network and a critic network, both trained under an adversarial paradigm.
