The segmentation network is tasked with generating precise label maps, while the critic network evaluates the segmentation quality, promoting a competitive yet collaborative training environment. The model employs a multi-scale L2 loss function, encouraging the extraction of hierarchical features that capture both local and global image dependencies. Our experimental results, obtained from the ISIC-2017 dataset, validate the efficacy of A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Seg, showcasing its superior performance in skin lesion segmentation tasks. The findings underscore the potential of adversarial training and attention mechanisms in enhancing medical image segmentation, setting a new benchmark for future research in the field.

articleTitle: Prohibited Item Detection Technology Based on Meta-DETR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Prohibited item detection in data-scarce environments poses significant challenges, especially in security applications. Building upon the Meta-DETR framework, this study incorporates adversarial learning to improve model robustness by generating synthetic samples that simulate difficult-to-detect prohibited items. Additionally, a dynamic few-shot adaptation mechanism allows the model to adjust its parameters during inference, enhancing detection accuracy across tasks of varying complexity. Together, these advancements address the limitations of data scarcity and improve the model’s ability to generalize in real-world applications. Experimental results on public benchmarks show marked improvements in detection accuracy and adaptability, particularly in X-ray security screening systems where precise identification is critical.

articleTitle: Kullback-Leibler and Attention-guided Feature Distillation for Hazardous Driving Detection and a Unified Benchmark
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Hazardous driving is the main cause of traffic accidents and thus fast and efficient detection of hazardous driving is meaningful. Various hazardous driving detection schemes have been presented, and the real-time performance need to be improved while it is cumbersome to deploy. In this paper, a Kullback-Leibler (KL) and attention-guided feature distillation method (KLA-FD) for hazardous driving detection are newly proposed. Compared with previous methods, we propose to obtain a soft probability map for each feature map after an attention module and normalization process. By simply minimizing the KL scatter between the soft probability maps of the two networks, the distillation process pays more attention to the most significant region of each feature map, which is valuable for hazardous driving detection. The experimental results show that compared with the original YOLOv8 network, our method shows better performance with higher speed and accuracy requirements.

articleTitle: SHAP-1DCNN Based Detection of Analogue Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the face of highly integrated and complex integrated circuits, traditional IC testing often relies on complex test designs and specialised test instruments, making it difficult to balance testing costs and efficiency. Deep learning algorithms can automatically learn and extract complex features from data, which can be adapted to various types of IC testing and help to realise the intelligence of the testing process. In this thesis, a SHAP-1DCNN based analogue operational amplifier testing technique (title) is proposed based on the actual test data of analogue integrated operational amplifiers (OPAs) using the SHAP-1DCNN deep learning algorithm.Firstly, the traditional CNN deep learning algorithm model is improved using SHAP analysis, and secondly, the general analogue integrated operational amplifier chip test circuit is drawn, and the precision components are patched and soldered to test the circuit board. Testing the key performance parameters of a large number of chips to obtain data sets. Train the optimised and improved SHAP-1DCNN deep learning model based on the collected data, and finally integrate this deep learning model in FPGA and accelerate its computation. The validation results show that the proposed test technique achieves a single OPA test time of 0.6s with an accuracy of 97.3%.

Author Keywords: Feature filtering Physical testing SHAP-CNN FPGA

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Low-light Image Enhancement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Enhancing low-light images is a crucial research topic in computer vision, aiming at revealing image details hidden in the darkness and thus recovering images with normal lighting and color. However, there is a large variety of solutions proposed for this problem, and it is not a simple problem for researchers to systematically understand all types of solutions. This paper provides a comprehensive review of various techniques for low-light image enhancement (LLIE), including algorithms, datasets, evaluation metrics, and more. First, we categorize these methods into two broad directions based on the principles of the algorithms and provide a detailed introduction to each. These two directions are further categorized into four subcategories based on their learning approaches. Then we introduce the principles, characteristics, and current dilemmas and challenges of various methods in detail based on each classification. Finally, we discuss the more promising research directions in the future in light of the latest research progress.

articleTitle: FAVC: Fine-Grained Attribute-Aware Visual Cross-Modal for Zero-Shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to predict the categories of unseen classes by transferring seen class knowledge to unseen classes. Attribute text descriptions as annotations of visual features are currently one of the most effective and widely used semantic information in ZSL. However, conventional vision-language pre-trained models only focus on the global featurealignment between images and text, while ignoring the more fine-grained semantic alignment between local visual features and text phrases, which restricts the model’s ability to zero-shot learning. Therefore, we propose a Fine-Grained Attribute-Aware Visual Cross-Modal (FAVC) learning framework, which correlates local visual features with attribute text descriptions via a cross-attention model and enhances the feature extraction capability and zero-shot recognition ability of the model through a contrastive learning training paradigm. Three standard ZSL benchmark tests show that FAVC achieves excellent performanceand has a better ability to capture localized regions with significant features in images.

articleTitle: BYOLSiam: Self-Supervised Pre-training for Offline Signature Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: We introduce BYOLSiam, a novel approach to offline signature verification that utilizes self-supervised learning techniques to address the challenges of cross-domain generalization and the scarcity of well-annotated signature datasets. Specifically, we adapt the Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL) framework to learn discriminative and generalizable representations suitable for OSV. Our approach comprises two key stages: self-supervised pre-training using BYOL and implementing a Siamese architecture dubbed BYOLSiam for the subsequent downstream OSV task. The BYOLSiam model incorporates our pre-trained BYOL encoder with a multi-layer perceptron, a layer normalization, and a flexible prediction layer which allows for both metric learning and binary classification tasks. We conducted experiments across multiple signature benchmark datasets to evaluate our model’s performance in within-domain and cross-domain scenarios. Our results demonstrate that BYOLSiam achieves state-of-the-art performance, particularly excelling in challenging cross-domain verification tasks.

articleTitle: Pretext Tasks in Test Time Adaptation Under Distribution Shifts-A Survey and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The performance of well-trained models deteriorates significantly under distribution shifts between training and test datasets. In response, various test time adaptive methods have been proposed to narrow domain gaps by capturing distribution cues from test samples. Notably, pretext task-based test time adaptive models exhibit promising performance, as they do not require target test annotations and separate training and testing stages, by leveraging well-designed pretext tasks, enabling effective adaptation at test time. Moreover, to accommodate diverse scenarios, task-specific pretext tasks are proposed to improve adaptive performance. Currently, a review has provided a comprehensive overview of test time adaptive methods. Nevertheless, there remains a notable gap in detailed surveys of pretext tasks employed in test time adaptation. To narrow this gap, this paper presents a survey of pretext tasks employed in test time adaptive models. We begin by providing an overview of test time adaptive methods, followed by giving a concise review of pretext tasks used in common scenarios, with a comparison to those used in test time adaptation scenarios. Subsequently, we delve into pretext tasks employed in various test time adaptation scenarios, exploring their characteristics, strengths, and limitations. Lastly, we conduct an empirical analysis with various pretext tasks in a digit prediction task, and subsequently conclude with a discussion of potential directions for future research.

articleTitle: A Joint Optical Plane-Rotation Axis Calibration Method Based on Line Laser Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Modern 3D reconstruction techniques have been widely used in many fields such as industrial inspection, medical imaging, and cultural relics protection, among which laser 3D scanning technology has the advantage of high accuracy. In this study, an easy-to-implement joint optical plane-rotational axis calibration technique based on line laser rotary scanning is proposed, in which the optical plane and the rotational axis are synchronously calibrated by a set of photographs, the optimal optical plane is fitted by using SVD, and the rotational axis is determined by using the method of minimizing the residual, and the high-precision three-dimensional data acquisition is finally achieved. This technique not only improves the calibration accuracy, but is also simple and easy to implement, ensuring the reconstruction stability in different environments. Finally, three-dimensional laser scanning experiments were carried out on PE water pipes and vernier calipers, and this method is able to realize high-precision three-dimensional reconstruction with a relative error of measurement within 2%. This research provides a new reference for high-precision 3D reconstruction, which has important practical application value.

articleTitle: Language based object detection with human body using CLIPseg : Integrating CLIP and Optical Flow for Unsupervised Object Tracking and Keypoint Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Human pose estimation and keypoint detection are essential tasks in computer vision, with widespread applications in areas such as action recognition, human-computer interaction, sports analytics, and medical imaging. Recent advances in deep learning and optical flow models have revolutionized these fields, enhancing the precision and scalability of tracking human motion. In areas that're not human related or in the field of object tracking in general Challenges arise in settings calling for adaptable frameworks. The main focus of this research is, on understanding how to accomplish recognition. Monitoring of moving points, on various objects without the need, for manual intervention. We demonstrate how combining CLIP and CLIPSeg models, with optical flow enhances annotations. With methods, like Co tracker and Dense Optical Flow, at our disposal we can carry out tasks without supervision. keypoint identification and continuous tracking, across frames, in a video sequence are highlighted in our findings showcasing. This method effectively removes the necessity, for annotations while still upholding standards. Significant progress has been made in identifying and monitoring points accurately marking an advancement, over previous methods. current approaches that heavily depend on existing labeled data. This represents a significant improvement over existing methods that heavily rely on pre-labeled data. The integration of optical flow with CLIP-based models allows for real-time tracking and motion prediction in complex, dynamic scenes, extending the applicability of keypoint detection beyond human pose estimation to arbitrary objects. This approach has broad implications for real-world applications such as video surveillance, autonomous navigation, and sports performance analysis, where unsupervised tracking can provide greater adaptability and efficiency. By eliminating manual intervention, our method sets a new standard for scalability and accuracy in dynamic tracking tasks.

articleTitle: Cross-network Intrusion Detection Based On Selfattention Mechanism Hybrid Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things(IoT), the network environment is becoming increasingly complex, and attack methods are becoming more diverse, posing a huge challenge to cyberspace security. Existing research on network intrusion detection has the problems of incomplete feature extraction, reliance on outdated datasets, and a lack of cross-network intrusion detection. A cross-network intrusion detection method based on a self-attention mechanism Hybrid Neural Network is proposed. The method consists of five parts: the Data Awareness Layer, Feature Extraction Layer, Sequential Information Fusion Layer, Global Context Attention Layer, and Intelligent Decision Layer. To address the problem of incomplete feature extraction, this paper uses a convolutional neural network in the Feature Extraction Layer to extract the spatial features of traffic data; in the Sequential Information Fusion Layer, a bidirectional long short-term memory network is used to capture the contextual temporal dependencies of traffic data in both directions; and a self-attention mechanism is introduced into the Global Context Attention Layer to achieve focused attention on key features. In view of the problems of relying on outdated datasets and the lack of cross-network intrusion detection, this paper trains and tests the model using traditional Internet datasets and IoT datasets that were released relatively late. The experimental results show that this method is robust when faced with different types of datasets and performs well in various Evaluation Metrics.

articleTitle: The Development and Future Challenges of the Multi-armed Bandit Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the wide application of machine learning and data-driven decision-making in various fields, the Multi-armed Bandit problem has received much attention due to its importance in balance exploration and utilization. As a typical sequential decision-making problem, it has a wide range of applications in areas such as online advertisement recommendations, medical trials, and Internet traffic optimization etc. Solving this problem plays a key role in optimizing resource allocation, improving system performance, and making optimal decisions in uncertain environments. This paper reviews the development of Multi-armed Bandit algorithms. It introduces the core algorithms, including ε-Greedy, Upper Confidence Bound (UCB), Thompson Sampling, Contextual Multi-armed Bandit, and Deep Learning Methods from the basic theory. The performance of the main algorithms and their performance in different application scenarios are analyzed. Possible solutions and future research directions are proposed for the challenges faced in comprehensive applications, such as algorithm selection, high-dimensional data processing, computational complexity, data privacy, and robustness. Finally, the current status of Multi-armed Bandit algorithms is summarized, and its prospects for improving performance and practicality in complex environments are envisioned. This study contributes to an in-depth understanding of the developmental lineage and current challenges of the Multi-armed Bandit algorithm and provides guidance for future algorithmic improvements and applications. The in-depth study of the Multi-armed Bandit problem will promote the development of the field of machine learning and decision optimization, promote its wide application in practical problems such as recommendation systems, medical diagnosis, financial decision-making, etc., which is of great significance to improve the decision-making ability of intelligent systems.

articleTitle: An Approach for Rejoining Ancient Dunhuang Manuscripts Automatically Based on Self-Supervised Learning and Encoding with Azimuths Information
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Ancient manuscripts, which document daily life, religious history, social development, and historical progress, embrace immeasurable value. However, these manuscripts often suffer damage and fragmentation due to natural degradation and improper preservation methods. Traditionally, archaeologists dedicated several years to manually reassembling these fragments, a process that is not only labor-intensive but also unsuccessful. Based on previous scholars’ work, this paper presents a new approach comprising feature extraction, data augmentation, and a self-supervised Siamese network that successfully speeds up the process of scrutinizing original fragments. Specifically, we have compiled a well-classified and fully annotated dataset of ancient Dunhuang manuscripts. Among these manuscripts, we extracted the edges of the fragments and encoded them as one-dimensional ordinal sequences using a novel method we named AZfreeman. For the first time, we propose AZfreeman, an improved Freeman encode that fuses azimuths information and can be effectively used to rejoin ancient Dunhuang fragments, which minimizes spatial overhead and enhances operability. Furthermore, we develop a data augmentation strategy capable of learning the features of fragments, which performs well with unbalanced and dynamically expanding datasets. It also brings convenience to subsequent dataset usage. Finally, we employ a self-supervised framework based on a lightweight backbone network, which incorporates attention mechanisms to extract features within sequences. Experimental results show that our approach can quickly and accurately automate the scrutinizing process of fragments, which significantly facilitates subsequent reconstruction. Our finding demonstrates the promising prospect of computer-assisted artifact restoration technology in the field of archaeology.

articleTitle: Based on Low-level Feature Enhancement for Mining Conveyor Belt foreign object detection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The mining conveyor belt is an important equipment for coal transportation. During the transmission process, foreign objects (such as stones, anchor rods, ironware, etc.) are mixed in the coal transported by the conveyor, resulting in safety accidents such as belt derailment and fire at the coal drop opening. Aiming at the problem of low accuracy of foreign object detection algorithm due to weak characterization of elongated objects and poor weak semantic feature extraction, a low-level feature enhancement foreign object detection algorithm based on YOLOv7-tiny is proposed, designated as FE-YOLO. Firstly, to prevent the decline of the accuracy of special foreign objects such as anchor rods and steel bars, deformable convolution is introduced to enhance the network's ability to extract long target objects. Secondly, the Low-Level Feature Enhancement Module (LFEM) is constructed to utilize multi-scale feature fusion to improve the weak semantic features of foreign objects and reduce the probability of missed and wrong detection. Finally, Ghost Shuffle Convolution(GSConv) is introduced in the feature fusion stage to minimize the channel information loss caused by the change of feature map size and dimension scaling, ensure the feature fusion efficiency and reduce the number of parameters. To verify the performance of the method, the test is carried out on the foreign object dataset of the self-built underground conveyor (a total of 6332 images). The results demonstrate that the mAP@0.5 of this algorithm can reach 0.871, the mAP@0.5:0.95 can reach 0.535, and the detection speed can reach 77.12fps, verifying the validity and superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Speech2Sign with ASL-Transformers and SL-GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Sign language is an essential means of communication for the deaf and hard-of-hearing, yet its translation and production are uniquely challenging due to its multimodality and the ambiguity of aligning spoken language sentences with visual signs. The objective of automatic Sign Language Production (SLP) is to transform speech into sign language videos that closely match the accuracy and expressiveness of a human interpreter, facilitating communication between the deaf community and the predominantly speaking world. Many prior SLP works have taken a gloss-free approach at the expense of accuracy, or have produced low-quality 2D sign poses as the final output, failing to convey the intricacies of sign language. Contrary to these approaches, we demonstrate the merits of gloss, a well-crafted loss function, and a multi-scale Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) in the production of accurate and photorealistic sign language videos. Our approach is a multistage SLP framework that begins with translating transcribed speech to its written sign language notation (gloss) using our ASL-Transformers model. We then map the gloss to its dictionary sign frames through a database query and generate the corresponding 2D pose sequence with DWPose, a pretrained pose estimator. Finally, we synthesize a photorealistic sign language video from the 2D pose sequence using our SL-GAN, a pose-conditioned image generation model. We evaluate our ASL-Transformers on the ASLG-PC12 dataset, reporting a BLEU-4 score of 89.58, and our SL-GAN on the ASLLVD dataset, reporting a mean SSIM value of 0.921.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation Based on Convolutional R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence, probabilistic graphical models, and machine learning, computer vision has made significant breakthroughs, making image instance segmentation a new challenging task in computer vision following semantic segmentation and object detection. Compared to traditional computer vision tasks, instance segmentation not only requires distinguishing different objects in an image but also differentiating between instances of these objects, making the task highly comprehensive. Many algorithms have been developed to solve instance segmentation tasks, among which the Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) algorithm is relatively mature. However, there is still room for improvement in Mask R-CNN, especially in terms of segmentation boundaries where significant errors exist. To solve the issue of blurred instance segmentation boundaries, this paper explores a method combining Mask R-CNN with Conditional Random Fields. This method employs convolutional conditional random fields and fully connected conditional random fields in the mask branch to optimize the further segmentation of candidate regions, resulting in more precise boundaries. Experimental results show that compared to the original algorithm, these methods increase the mAP value by 0.6% and 3%, respectively. In the comparison of segmentation results for targets of different scales, the improvements with Mask R-CNN-ConvCRF are particularly notable for medium and large-scale targets, with increases of 4% and 5.1%, respectively.

articleTitle: DTDG-Net: A Few-shot Data Augmentation Method for X-ray Security Inspection Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Since the detection of prohibited items is a low-probability event, the target detection model based on deep learning often suffers from issues of low recognition accuracy due to limited training data. To ad-dress this challenge, this article proposes an enhanced Domain Transformation Data Generation Network (DTDG-Net), aiming to solve the problems brought by the scarcity of training samples. Initially, we designed a Color Consistency Cycle Generative Adversarial Network (CC-CycleGAN) based on a Dynamic Color Attention Module (DCAM), which can effectively ensure the color consistency between the original and generated images. Secondly, we developed a Data Fusion Generator (DFG), which aligns the transparency features of the generated and original images through a blending Poisson fusion method based on hue transformation, ultimately achieving data augmentation with limited samples. Finally, to objectively evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, we introduce a style transfer quality evaluation co-efficient, specifically designed for the performance evaluation of few-shot sample data augmentation for object detection. Through this metric, we can comprehensively and accurately measure the contribution of data augmentation to the object detection task. This unique framework design holds potential for widespread applications in the field of prohibited item detection in X-ray images. Through a series of experiments, we demonstrate that our approach, exhibits stronger robustness and generalization, effectively alleviating the challenges posed by few-shot sample problems, providing an innovative solution for pro-hibited item detection in X-ray images.

articleTitle: Access optimization for small files in HDFS: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: The Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) is an open-source distributed file system optimized for data appending and reading, offering portability, high fault tolerance, and scalability. After more than a decade of development, HDFS has become widely used for big data storage, supporting both structured and unstructured data at a massive scale. It also enables a variety of applications, such as complex query analysis, interactive analytics, detailed billing queries, Key-Value read/write operations, and iterative computations. However, with the rapid growth of internet applications and scientific computing, the number of small files—such as images and text—has surged. Since HDFS was originally designed for large file storage, it encounters issues when handling large volumes of small files, including inefficient metadata structures, master server bottlenecks, and network latency. As a result, efficiently storing and accessing large numbers of small files has become a significant challenge for HDFS. This paper introduces the principles and features of HDFS, and summarizes existing solutions for managing massive small files in HDFS, including Hadoop’s built-in approaches and user-customized solutions. It also reviews related research conducted in recent years. Looking forward, with ongoing technological advancements, indexing, networking, and caching technologies are expected to become key strategies for optimizing HDFS for small file storage.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection Algorithm for Glazed Ceramic Tiles Based on Improved Faster RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In terms of surface defect detection of glazed tiles, there are problems such as false detection and insufficient ability to identify small target defects due to the rich texture on the surface of glazed tiles. In response to these challenges, this article has compiled a dataset of glazed ceramic tiles and proposed an improved algorithm ECANet-FPG based on Faster R-CNN. Due to the similarity in texture and defects on the surface of ceramic tiles, this algorithm introduces the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) module into the feature extraction network of Faster R-CNN to enhance the ability to extract deep features. At the same time, a Feature Pyramid Grids (FPG) structure is adopted to achieve efficient fusion of multi-scale features, in order to improve the recognition accuracy of small target defects. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm achieves higher detection accuracy and efficiency than the baseline model, demonstrating its effectiveness and practicality in detecting surface defects on glazed ceramic tiles.

articleTitle: Specialized Face Encoder for Audio-based Speech to Lip Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Videos that are directly translated and dubbed often fail to provide a natural audiovisual experience, making it crucial to develop methods that can accurately generate lip movements to match the audio. Self-supervised learning models like MAE have proven their robust transfer capabilities. This paper employs the pretraining method of MAE and proposes a new automatic lip-sync network. Additionally, we introduce a separate perceptual loss for the lip region of the generated faces to ensure accurate and clear lip movements. Our automatic lip-sync network consists of four components: video preprocessing, audio preprocessing, generator, and lip-sync discriminator, using facial images and audio features as inputs. We trained an MAE encoder and integrated it into the lip generator. The system was tested on two audiovisual datasets, and the results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance in both the visual quality of generated talking faces and their synchronization with the audio.

articleTitle: An Improved Medical Visual Question Answering Model Based on CLIP and BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) is a versatile tool applicable in autonomous vehicles for manufacturing use cases up to recommendation platforms for e-commerce, thus greatly increasing process efficiency, sophistication of decisions, and user engagement. One area that stands out is healthcare, where this could revolutionize diagnostic procedures and patient comprehension, which will help patients at large readings more effectively. Reduced convergence time and enhanced interpretability because solution paths are directly enforced through constraints. Coherent question answers are difficult to form, yet, remain a key challenge. In this work, we present a framework for knowledge-based VQA utilizing answer heuristics. Then, two types of answer heuristics are presented: answer candidates and answer-aware examples. Answer candidates and also answer-aware examples with the same answer as the test input, which was a downside as well as a limitation in our benchmark were currently provided which were aimed to make our experiment extra straightforward. Our proposed MedVQA version with CLIP-based visual attributes along with BERT to enhance the MCAN model was able to increase the model to an accuracy of 78.89% (11.09+) over the current state-of-the-art. This is a significant development, proving that state-of-the-art models and visualization elements lead to improved system performance. The original framework intended to facilitate adoption and thereby improve healthcare decision-making and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Anti-Occlusion Scale-Adaptive Correlation Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Target tracking at high-speed conditions is highly desirable for embedded systems, such as visual navigation. However, existing methods face challenges in achieving real-time processing due to algorithm complexity and computational limitations. To address this issue, we propose an anti-occlusion scale-adaptive correlation tracker (OSCT) based on a Kernelized Correlation Filter (KCF), which considers tracking confidence and multiple features in embedded systems. Specifically, we employ a discriminative correlation filter to estimate the scale of the tracking target. Subsequently, our tracker dynamically adjusts the learning rate by evaluating the confidence of tracking results. Moreover, the OSCT uses a re-detector to re-detect the target in case of tracking failure. Instead of relying on a single feature, our method integrates multiple features to address variation and occlusion in tracking objects. Experimental results demonstrate that: 1) OSCT achieves an average precision of 0.778 at 20 pixels, representing an improvement of over 8% compared to other high-speed trackers. 2) The average running speed of OSCT is 32 FPS, outperforming LCT (26 FPS). Therefore, our approach is well-suited for long-term tracking on embedded platforms.

articleTitle: MTC-Net: Multi-granular Temporal Cascade Learning for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel Multi-granular Temporal Cascade Learning framework (MTC-Net), which effectively combines coarse-grained and fine-grained detection capabilities. By leveraging visual features extracted from CLIP and integrating visual-language associations, MTC-Net addresses the limitations of existing methods and achieves outstanding performance across multiple benchmark datasets. Furthermore, we incorporate multiscale temporal feature fusion and an improved attention mechanism into the framework, and introduce a feature consistency-based auxiliary loss to enhance the model's focus on anomalous patterns and generalization ability. Extensive experiments on the XD-Violence and UCF-Crime datasets demonstrate that MTC-Net outperforms both semi-supervised and classification-based weakly supervised methods across all evaluation metrics. For the coarse-grained Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection (WSVAD) task, MTC-Net achieves an AP of 84.83% on XD-Violence and an AUC of 75.23% on UCF-Crime, significantly surpassing current state-of-the-art methods. In the more challenging fine-grained WSVAD task, MTC-Net achieves a 13.1% improvement in average precision over previous methods. These results validate the effectiveness of our approach, highlighting MTC-Net's potential to advance the field of video anomaly detection through the efficient use of weak supervision, multiscale temporal feature fusion, and multimodal feature integration.

articleTitle: Attention-driven Graph-Sequence Fusion Network for Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation has been widely applied on social network-based platforms, aiming to recommend a user’s potential next location based on their historical check-in data. Current research faces limitations in both graph neural networks and sequential learning models, with challenges in fully extracting user check-in features and effectively integrating global and personal information. To address these issues, we propose a model that fuses features obtained from a graph neural network and a sequential encoder through an attention fusion mechanism, followed by learning with a hierarchical Transformer encoder to enhance feature representation. Our model has been extensively tested on three datasets, achieving promising results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Receptive Field and Multi-Scale Features for Object Detection with Lightweight Hybrid Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Currently, object detection models have achieved a relatively ideal balance between speed and performance. However, taking the YOLO model as an example, it relies on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to extract image features. Traditional convolutions face limitations in capturing multi-scale features, and increasing the receptive field often comes with significant computational overhead. Moreover, existing channel attention mechanisms tend to overlook the multi-scale feature space, while hybrid spatial-channel attention approaches face the challenge of high computational complexity. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight attention module that combines spatial and channel information, integrating both local and global features. Additionally, we design a novel multi-scale hybrid convolution module, which significantly enhances multi-scale feature representation and receptive field, while maintaining low computational complexity. We evaluated our method on the COCO and VisDrone datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model performs excellently across multiple metrics, significantly improving detection performance.

articleTitle: A Novel ISAR Cross-Range Scaling Algorithm Based on Image Entropy Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Cross-range scaling can transform range-Doppler imaging results of targets into range Cross-range images, which is beneficial to accurate size estimation and feature extraction of targets. Accurate rotation angle estimation is a necessary condition for cross-range scaling. In this paper, a robust ISAR cross-range scaling algorithm is proposed. In this method, the degree of focus of the target imaging result is taken as the objective function, the target motion parameters are solved by the snow ablation optimizer (SAO) algorithm, and then cross-range scaling is realized. The effectiveness and performance of the proposed method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Algorithmic Robustness through Noise-Induced Dataset Augmentation for Fusion Fuel Profile Inversion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: In the field of nuclear fusion fueling, the distribution of fuel beam parameters is of great significance for optimizing injection techniques and for in-depth study of the interaction between particles and plasma. To obtain the beam velocity distribution of the supersonic molecular fueling beam, a U-net model has been applied in our previous research, successfully capturing the mapping relationship between density distribution and velocity distribution, and effectively predicts velocity distributions across a wide range of parameters. To effectively apply this model to the inversion of experimental data, it is imperative to rigorously investigate its noise resistance capabilities. This paper focuses on enhancing algorithmic robustness through noise-induced dataset augmentation. The results suggest that under 20% noise interference, the model can still achieve stable prediction of the velocity distribution of the supersonic molecular beam, providing strong support for subsequent research.

articleTitle: A Classification Method of the Crescent Status in IgA Nephropathy Based on Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a prevalent glomerulonephritis with an insidious onset. Early diagnosis and treatment significantly improve patient prognosis. Renal biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosis, but it is an invasive procedure with several limitations. Therefore, it is essential to explore a non-invasive diagnostic method. The crescent status is an independent predictor of IgAN progression, and subtle differences in CT scans make it difficult for CNNs to distinguish the progression. Contrastive learning enables CNNs to learn effective representations by comparing similarities and differences between samples, rather than relying on predefined labels. Consequently, we incorporate this approach into conventional CNNs to enhance their representational learning capabilities. In cases where the pathological characteristics of both kidneys exhibit similar features, the method utilizes the SimSiam contrastive learning method to compare images of two kidneys and combines it with supervised learning for end-to-end training. For supervised training, feature fusion is used to combine features from both kidneys into a more comprehensive representation, which avoid inconsistent results between the two kidneys, thereby accelerating model convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN performance can be improved stably through applying the designed end-to-end training method of contrastive learning and feature fusion. Furthermore, we use a balancing factor to adjust the losses of the two training processes and explore its optimal range through experiments. Three balancing factor decay strategies are proposed and compared. Ultimately, the method proposed in this paper achieves an accuracy of 0.695 and an AUC of 0.699, demonstrating its potential to assist physicians in diagnosis.

articleTitle: Improved DenseNet-ECA Network with Continuous Wavelet Transform for High-Accuracy Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Stable operation of rolling bearings is crucial in mechanical systems, as failures can lead to severe performance degradation and shutdowns. Early fault detection significantly reduces maintenance costs and safety risks, yet traditional diagnosis methods often struggle with inefficiency and poor adaptability. This paper presents an improved DenseNet-ECA network combined with Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) for signal preprocessing to extract key features. The model achieves 100% fault detection accuracy across various speeds, showcasing superior performance and stability under diverse conditions, providing a promising solution for rolling bearing fault detection.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Fusion of Complementary Transformer-Cnn Features for Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Image Processing, Computer Vision and Machine Learning (ICICML)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to correctly predict human pose in the case of occlusion, scale change and low resolution, a human pose estimation model based on bidirectional fusion of convolutional neural network and Transformer feature is proposed.. Using the characteristics of convolutional neural network and Transformer feature learning network, the expression ability of local features is improved while strengthening the remote modeling ability of the model. The model is mainly composed of three parts ; transformer branch which focuses on the remote modeling ability of the model ; the CNN branch that mainly extracts local detail information ; a bidirectional fusion interaction module based on deformable self-attention mechanism. The bidirectional fusion interaction module uses the attention mechanism to eliminate the architectural differences between CNN and Transformer, thereby achieving complementary features and ultimately improving the performance of the model. The experimental results show that compared with the benchmark model, the proposed model improves the accuracy by 2.3 % and 0.5 % on the COCO dataset and MPII dataset, respectively.
